jobinrwanda.title: Senior Resource Development Manager
jobinrwanda.description:
JOB OPPORTUNITY 

Senior Resource Development Manager

World Vision is a child-focused Christian humanitarian organization implementing development programmes in 30 Districts of Rwanda. Our interventions in the strategic period of 2026-2030 seek to reach 2.5 million of the most vulnerable children. This is done through programming in Child Protection, Education, Nutrition and WASH, and Poverty Alleviation (Resilience and Livelihoods).

World Vision Rwanda seeks to hire a highly qualified, dedicated, and experienced Rwandan national for the role of Senior Resource Development Manager, joining an established and experienced team. This stimulating position incorporates a range of skills and development in multiple areas, allowing for an exciting opportunity for career growth in a dynamic, global organization. It will be based in Kigali at the Head Office and will report to the National Director. 

Purpose of the position:

 The Senior Resource Development Manager provides strategic leadership and overall accountability for World Vision Rwanda's resource mobilization and external engagement agenda. The position leads the development and implementation of strategies that secure sustainable and diversified funding, strengthen organizational positioning, and advance strategic relationships that contribute to the achievement of World Vision Rwanda's Strategic Objectives. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Manager provides organizational leadership on resource acquisition, donor engagement, funding diversification, business development, and market positioning across institutional, private sector, philanthropic, and domestic funding streams. The role ensures that World Vision Rwanda is strategically positioned within the development landscape, influences key stakeholders, and secures the resources required to deliver sustainable impact for vulnerable children, families, and communities. The Manager serves as a principal advisor to the National Director and Senior Leadership Team on donor trends, development financing, external relations, strategic opportunities, and organizational growth priorities.

 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

 % of time

 Activity

 End Results

 15%

 Strategic Leadership and Organizational Growth

 Effective implementation of World Vision Rwanda's Resource Mobilization Strategy, resulting in achievement of organizational resource acquisition objectives.

 Diversified and sustainable funding portfolio that supports organizational growth, resilience, and long-term impact.

 Strong alignment between resource acquisition priorities and National Strategy objectives, ensuring resources are directed toward strategic priorities.

 Enhanced organizational decision-making through timely advisory support on funding opportunities, market trends, and resource mobilization risks.

 A culture of innovation, accountability, and resource stewardship embedded across the organization, strengthening funding competitiveness and sustainability.

 20%

 External Relations, Donor Engagement and Positioning

 Enhanced organizational visibility, reputation, and influence among donors, government institutions, development partners, foundations, and private sector stakeholders.

 Strong and sustainable strategic relationships established and maintained with senior donor representatives, decision-makers, and key development partners.

 World Vision Rwanda positioned as a preferred and credible development partner in national, regional, and international forums.

 Increased strategic partnership and resource acquisition opportunities through effective representation, stakeholder engagement, and high-level negotiations.

 20%

 Resource Acquisition and Business Development (Growing the pipeline and securing new funding)

 Annual resource acquisition targets established and achieved, contributing to overall strategic funding goals.

 Increased funding secured through proactive business development, donor positioning, and opportunity pursuit.

 Strong strategic partnerships, consortiums, and alliances that enhance competitiveness and access to high-value opportunities.

 A healthy and forward-looking funding pipeline that supports sustained organizational growth.

 30%

 Resource Acquisition, Portfolio Performance and Sustainability (Managing and growing the value, quality, and sustainability of the funding portfolio).

 A diversified and sustainable funding portfolio that supports long-term organizational impact and resilience.

 Improved proposal success rates and funding outcomes through high-quality, competitive, and compliant submissions.

 Strong donor retention, stewardship, and strategic partnerships that expand funding opportunities.

 Enhanced financial sustainability through diversified revenue streams and continuous improvement in resource mobilization performance.

 5%

 Technical support, Mentorship and Talent Development

 A high-performing, skilled, and motivated Resource Mobilization team capable of delivering World Vision Rwanda's resource acquisition and growth objectives.

 Effective workforce planning, succession management, and staff development, ensuring continuity of critical resource mobilization capabilities and leadership pipeline development.

 Strong cross-functional collaboration and alignment across Programmes, Operations, Finance, Communications, Support Offices, and other stakeholders in support of resource acquisition goals.

 A culture of accountability, continuous learning, and high performance embedded within the Resource Mobilization function, resulting in improved effectiveness, efficiency, and results delivery.

 5%

 Strategic Advisory and Organizational Leadership

 Resource mobilization priorities effectively integrated into organizational strategy, planning, and decision-making.

 Senior leadership equipped with timely strategic intelligence and analysis to guide growth, sustainability, and funding decisions.

 Enhanced organizational positioning, readiness, and responsiveness to emerging donor, partnership, and development financing trends.

 Strengthened organizational influence and visibility through effective representation in strategic national, regional, and global forums.

 5%

 Other Responsibilities

 Effective contribution to National Office leadership, organizational priorities, and strategic initiatives.

 Compliance with organizational policies, standards, and regulatory requirements across the Resource Mobilization function.

 Successful delivery of special assignments and cross-organizational initiatives as delegated.

 Consistent promotion of World Vision's mission, values, and organizational reputation through all resource mobilization activities.

 Knowledge/Qualifications for the role

 Required Professional Experience

 Minimum 7 - 10 years of progressive experience in resource mobilization, donor engagement, business development, strategic partnerships, and grant acquisition, including senior leadership responsibility.

 Demonstrated track record of securing significant funding from institutional donors, bilateral and multilateral agencies, UN organizations, foundations, private sector partners, and domestic funding sources.

 Proven experience leading resource acquisition and business development functions, including donor positioning, funding pipeline management, partnership development, opportunity prioritization, and strategic funding decisions.

 Experience overseeing donor intelligence, portfolio management, funding diversification, and resource mobilization systems to support long-term organizational growth and impact.

 Extensive experience building and managing high-level relationships with donors, government institutions, development partners, foundations, private sector leaders, and other strategic stakeholders.

 Demonstrated success leading complex proposal development processes, consortium building, negotiations, and high-value funding pursuits involving multidisciplinary teams and multiple stakeholders.

 Experience advising senior leadership on donor trends, development financing, funding risks, resource mobilization strategies, and organizational growth opportunities.

 Proven leadership experience in developing high-performing teams, strengthening organizational capacity, and driving resource mobilization performance and sustainability.

 Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification

 Education

 Master's Degree in International Development, Business Administration, Economics, Public Policy, International Relations, Communications, Social Sciences, or a related field.

 A Bachelor's Degree in a relevant discipline, combined with substantial senior-level resource mobilization and leadership experience, may be considered.

 NOTE: If a foreign institution issued the degree, an equivalence certificate from the Rwanda Higher Education Council (HEC) will be required)  

 Professional Training

 Advanced training in resource mobilization, donor engagement, business development, strategic partnerships, fundraising, grant acquisition, or organizational growth.

 Training in strategic planning, development financing, results-based management, proposal design, donor compliance, and grant management is an advantage.

 Professional Certifications (Desirable)

 Professional certification in Project Management (PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent).

 Certification in fundraising, resource mobilization, grant management, business development, partnership management, or leadership development.

 Additional certifications in strategic planning, organizational development, MEAL, or Results-Based Management are desirable.

 License / Registration

 No specific professional license or registration required.

 Other Requirements

 Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and resource mobilization, donor intelligence, pipeline management, and grants management systems.

 Excellent written, presentation, negotiation, and verbal communication skills in English.

 Demonstrated ability to engage and influence senior-level stakeholders, including donors, government officials, development partners, foundations, and private sector leaders.

 Preferred Knowledge

 and Qualifications

 Strong knowledge of strategic resource mobilization, donor engagement, business development, grant acquisition, funding diversification, and partnership development within the international development and humanitarian sectors.

 In-depth understanding of bilateral, multilateral, UN, Foundations and Trusts, government, private sector, and domestic funding mechanisms, donor priorities, compliance requirements, and evolving development financing trends.

 Sound knowledge of organizational growth strategies, market positioning, consortium development, localization approaches, and partnership models that strengthen competitiveness and sustainable funding acquisition.

 Familiarity with project design, results-based management, proposal development, budgeting, grant management, and funding portfolio oversight.

 Knowledge of donor intelligence platforms, pipeline management systems, grants management tools, and resource mobilization reporting frameworks.

 Strong strategic thinking, analytical, stakeholder management, networking, influencing, negotiation, and communication capabilities, with the ability to engage effectively at senior levels.

 Experience working in international development, humanitarian, faith-based, or comparable sectors, with a strong understanding of the external funding environment.

 Professional training or certification in project management, resource mobilization, fundraising, grant management, business development, strategic partnerships, leadership, or related fields is an added advantage.

 Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement

 Travel to the field (20%)

 Physical Requirements

 Language Requirements

 English proficiency

 Key Working Relationships

 Contact (within WV or outside WV)

 Reason for contact

 Frequency of contact

 Senior Leadership Team (SLT),

 Provide strategic advice and updates on resource mobilization performance, funding opportunities, donor trends, business development priorities, portfolio health, funding risks, and organizational positioning.

 Support strategic planning, decision-making, funding diversification, and alignment of resource acquisition efforts with World Vision Rwanda's strategic objectives.

 Daily / Weekly / As Required

 Programme, Technical, Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, Communications, Advocacy, and MEAL Teams

 Provide leadership and coordination across functions to ensure alignment of resource acquisition priorities, donor requirements, proposal development processes, implementation planning, and organizational positioning, resulting in high-quality funding submissions and successful resource mobilization outcomes.

 Daily / Weekly / As Required

 Regional Office (RO) and Global Centre (GC)

 Coordinate resource mobilization strategy, funding priorities, donor engagement, business development initiatives, proposal investments, organizational positioning, compliance, and performance reporting; contribute to regional and global growth agendas and strategic opportunities

 Weekly / Monthly

 Support Offices (SOs)

 Lead collaboration on donor positioning, funding opportunity pursuit, proposal development, consortium engagement, grant acquisition, and strategic donor relationship management.

 Weekly / Monthly

 Government Institutions, Development Partners, Donors, Private Sector, Foundations, Academic Institutions, NGOs, INGOs, and Consortium Partners

 Lead and maintain strategic relationships and partnerships to advance resource mobilization objectives, align funding opportunities with national and organizational priorities, strengthen donor positioning and stewardship, influence development agendas, negotiate partnerships and consortium arrangements, promote innovation and evidence generation, and expand sustainable funding opportunities through collaborative engagement with key stakeholders.

 Ongoing / Monthly / As Required

 Decision Making

 The role requires the ability to provide strategic leadership, exercise sound professional judgment, and make informed decisions that influence World Vision Rwanda's resource mobilization performance, organizational growth, and long-term sustainability. The incumbent is expected to lead the resource mobilization function, providing direction, oversight, and accountability for resource acquisition, donor engagement, business development, and funding diversification efforts. The role demands strong strategic thinking, foresight, and a solution-oriented mindset to identify opportunities, anticipate risks, and guide organizational responses within a dynamic funding environment. Success depends on the ability to influence senior stakeholders, build strategic partnerships, navigate complex donor and development landscapes, balance competing priorities, and drive results through effective leadership, collaboration, and sound decision-making. The position requires confidence, resilience, negotiation skills, and the ability to inspire high performance while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, stewardship, and continuous improvement.

 Salary: The salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience.

N.B: Women are highly encouraged to apply. 

How to apply:

Should you wish to apply for this position, please go to https://worldvision.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/WorldVisionInternational/job/Kigali-Rwanda/Resource-Development-Manager_JR52415

If this is your first time applying online via the World Vision International careers website, you will need to register an account along with your application details. This site will provide you with additional functionality, such as saved searches and email alerts. Registration requires minimal information to create your account. Further details will be collected during the application process.

All applicants must apply using our online application system; CVs received via email or standard post will NOT be considered. 

If you encounter any challenges during the application process, please don’t hesitate to let us know at wvrwanda-recruitment@wvi.org (no applications will be accepted through this email).

The closing date for submission of applications is October 09, 2026; no late applications will be accepted. Note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

As a child-focused organization, World Vision is committed to the protection of children and does not employ staff whose background is not suitable for working with children. All employment is conditional upon the successful completion of all applicable background checks, including criminal record checks.

It is also important to note that World Vision is a Christian humanitarian organization with a mission centered on following Jesus Christ in service to the world´s most vulnerable children. Therefore, in all locations to the fullest extent legally permissible, the successful applicant will affirm our core documents, observe conduct compatible with Christian principles, serve at a high level of professional ethics, and strive to act in accordance with cultural sensitivities. Furthermore, regular attendance at team and office devotions, chapel, and prayer gatherings is expected in line with policies in the World Vision host location and its departments.

It supports over 1.8 million people, especially children, across all 30 districts, focusing on education, health, nutrition, WASH, and livelihoods.

Senior Resource Development Manager

World Vision is a child-focused Christian humanitarian organization implementing development programmes in 30 Districts of Rwanda. Our interventions in the strategic period of 2026-2030 seek to reach 2.5 million of the most vulnerable children. This is done through programming in Child Protection, Education, Nutrition and WASH, and Poverty Alleviation (Resilience and Livelihoods).

World Vision Rwanda seeks to hire a highly qualified, dedicated, and experienced Rwandan national for the role of Senior Resource Development Manager, joining an established and experienced team. jobinrwanda.title: Mining Supervisor
jobinrwanda.description:
JOB ADVERT - Mining Supervisor

Trinity Musha Mines Ltd is a Mining company focused on the production and exploration of Tin, Tantalum, and Lithium in Rwanda. Trinity Musha is currently inviting suitable candidates to apply for the following position:

i. Position/Job Title: Mine Supervisor

ii. Grade: C4 

iii. Department: Mining

iv. Reports To: Mining Section Leader

Job Brief: The Mine Supervisor is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the day-to-day mining operations to ensure safe, efficient, and productive mining activities within the designated area.

Responsibilities: The Mine Supervisor has the following responsibilities and duties:

1. Supervise Mining Operations:

Coordinate and direct mining activities, including drilling, blasting, excavation, hauling, and ore processing, to meet production targets and quality standards.

 Allocate resources, such as manpower, equipment, and materials, to optimize efficiency and productivity.

 Monitor production schedules, equipment performance, and ore grades to identify and address operational issues or bottlenecks.

 Supports the Mining Team Leaders to ensure that production team delivers on the daily planned production and necessary measures are taken whenever the production targets are not met.

 Observe and enforce any code of practice, instructions, procedures, directives, permissions, exemptions etc. issued by the Mine Manager or any other person authorized to do so 

2. Ensure Health and Safety Compliance:

Inspect all other workings, in your area of responsibility, at least once a week 

 Be responsible for the proper discipline of all persons working under your charge Provide and maintain a working environment that is safe and without risk to the health and safety of employees within your area of responsibility

 Identify relevant hazards and assess the related risks within your area of responsibility

 Implement and enforce safety protocols, procedures, and regulations to minimize risks and prevent accidents or injuries.

 Conduct regular safety inspections, hazard assessments, and safety training sessions for mining personnel.

 Investigate incidents or near misses, report findings, and recommend corrective actions to improve safety performance.

 Ensure adherence to the SHEC laws, regulations and policies

3. Maintain Equipment and Infrastructure:

Oversee maintenance and repair activities for mining equipment, vehicles, and infrastructure to ensure operational reliability and longevity.

 Schedule preventive maintenance tasks, inspections, and repairs to minimize downtime and maximize equipment availability.

 Coordinate with maintenance staff and suppliers to procure spare parts, components, and consumables as needed.

4. Management of Personnel:

Ensure that people under your supervision adhere to HR Policies and Procedures

 Provide Employees within your area of responsibility with any information, instructions or supervision that is necessary to enable them to perform their work professionally, safely and without risks

 Consider Employees’ training and capabilities before assigning tasks to them

 Ensure that all persons working under your charge are fully trained on job training or otherwise in their tasks.

 Responsible for staffing needs of the area of responsibility

 Supervise and mentor mining staff, including operators and labourers, to ensure adherence to company policies, procedures, and performance standards.

 Provide leadership, guidance, and support to promote teamwork, motivation, and professional development among team members.

 Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and address disciplinary issues or concerns in accordance with HR policies.

5. Environmental Monitor and Compliance:

Ensure compliance with environmental regulations, permits, and standards governing mining operations, waste management, and land reclamation.

 Implement environmental management practices, such as erosion control, water management, and rehabilitation measures, to minimize environmental impacts.

6. Data Collection and Reporting:

Record in ink in your logbook the following during or at the conclusion of your shift:

The designation of every working place or other working place inspected by yourself during your shift

 Particularly of any unsatisfactory conditions of working places, traveling ways or other workings in your area of responsibility as observed by yourself or reported to you by the Mine team leader or any other person, specifically in respect of ground conditions and where safety of people are concerned

 Any instructions given by you to secure the health and safety of persons under your charge and adhered to.

Give regular reports on the Production, HSEC, Security and HR to the Section team leader / Site manager for your designated area of responsibility.

Prepare regular reports, dashboards, and presentations for management review, highlighting key operational KPIs, trends, and challenges.

7. Job Requirements: The Mine Supervisor should have the following education, experience and skills:

Bachelor’s degree/Advanced diploma in mining Engineering

 At least 3 years Certification in mining from a competent mining school

 Experience of at least 3 years in the field.

 Physical fitness.

 Excellent Communication skills (English preferable)

 Willing to work overtime

 Good supervisor skills and be able to delegate different work to workers/Team work spirit

Equal Opportunity Employer

Trinity Musha Mines Ltd values diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, ethnicity, disability, or background.

HOW TO APPLY:

Applications should be submitted no later than Monday 1st October 2026 at 4 PM. Please click on Apply Here. Applications sent through other channels will be rejected.

Indicating which position, you are applying for and addressed to the General Managerof Trinity Musha Mines Ltd. For other inquiries please contact the HR office on 0788525141/0788361758. Only applicants fulfilling the requirements will be contacted. 

Done at Musha, on 18/09/2026.

Missionnaire Mbanza

General Manager

Trinity Musha Mines Ltd

 Project Staff

Strong analytical skills.

 Language Proficiency: English & Kinyarwanda, French (optional

 Excellent interpersonal skills and team player.

Donor data will remain under the control of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda and shall not be forwarded to or swapped with other organizations.

Passionate about childcare and development

 Punctuality and assiduity 

 Knowledge of child rights and child development issues

 Good standards of conduct and ethics as well as integrity, appropriate judgment, independence and confidentiality

 Personal organization and planning skills; ability to organize and prioritize

 Capable of a rigorous analytical approach and result oriented.

 Ability to place details in a wider context (understanding the broader context). 

 Flexible, resilient and able to manage stress.

 Team spirit

Competencies:

Promotes the vision, mission and strategic goals of SOS Children Villages;

 Display cultural, gender sensitivity and adaptability;

 Demonstrate creativity and abilities to complete multiple tasks by establishing priorities, deadlines and multiple reporting relationships;

 Establishes, builds and maintains effective working relationships with staff and clients to facilitate the provision of support, knowledge, management and learning;

 In depth knowledge of Planning, Monitoring and Information System, Monitoring and Evaluation and organizational development issues;

 Excellent abilities to identify significant capacity building opportunities and capacity to deliver such trainings using a clear communications skill.

 Demonstrates strong oral and written communication skills;

The interested Candidates in this position should send a detailed Curriculum Vitae with three (3) traceable professional references, application letter , Rwandan national Identity Card and academic certificates/degrees to sos.recruitment@sos-rwanda.org and properly fill the application form found via the followingLINKby not later than 01st October, 2026 at 5:00 pm Kigali time. 

Please mention in the subject of your email “Planning MEAL Officer”.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

“SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda/ International holds strict child safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for conducts of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring decisions will give due emphasize to assessing candidates value congruence and thorough background checks, police clearance reference check processes”. 

Done in Kigali on 24th September 2026.

jobinrwanda.title: Agriculture Associate
jobinrwanda.description:
Gardens for Health International

Job Description

Position: Agriculture Associate

About the Organization

Gardens for Health International bridges the disconnect between food, agriculture, and nutrition. For over a decade, Gardens for Health International (GHI) has implemented nutrition-sensitive agriculture programs to combat childhood malnutrition in Rwanda. We equip families and communities with the knowledge, resources and support they need to meet their nutritional needs. GHI’s core program works in collaboration with government-run health centers to identify and support rural families struggling with malnutrition. In addition to this core program, GHI collaborates with a variety of governmental and non-governmental partners to bring our expertise to new settings and new populations, such as primary schools and refugee camps. We are an impact-driven organization with a deep commitment to ensuring that every program we design meets and responds to the unique needs of the communities we serve. Our team is flexible, innovative, and passionate about sparking lasting change.

About the Role

The Agriculture Associate will be in charge of the overseeing of the agriculture related partnerships on the farm. He/She will ensure the farm is growing crops according to the farm strategy and GHI vision, that the farm is well-maintained and healthy, and that all farm tasks related to the program are completed on time.

He/She will also participate in the farm tours along with the Ag team to organization, visitors and donors. He/She will also build capacity of farm technicians on the permaculture and conservation agriculture principles and practices. He/She will be assisting to the development of different reports to farm project partners and represent the farm to external partners.

Overview of the Role

Position: Agriculture Associate

Place of Work: Ndera, Gasabo with travel to the field as required

Staff reporting to this position: None

Reports to: Agriculture Coordinator

Roles and Responsibilities

Works alongside with farm technicians to implement the planned activities at the farm

 Record all farm data including farm produce into Commcare

 Lead homemade pesticide preparation, ensure its quality and research on types of pests which can be managed by such pesticide

 Lead manure production from the farm and check quality depends on the techniques applied.

 Lead seeds’ saving and advise farm team accordingly to ensure the quality of seeds

 Preparation of crop plan and lead its’ implementation on seasonal basis

 Lead farm related trials, records keeping and reporting

 Collaborate with the farm livestock technician to monitor and manage livestock farming activities 

 Conducts agricultural trainings for fellow farm technicians on permaculture principles practices

 Monitoring the on-going farm activities and preparing farm expense requests and monthly budgets

 Work with the farm technicians to hire part-time workers and distributes assignments and payment to them

 Work closely with the farm technicians ensuring that all equipment, machinery and facilities are kept to an optimum level.

Broader role at GHI

Conducts farm tours for visitors and educates permanent staff and fellows about the farm

 Provide support to the Ag Team in various ways, including curriculum development and external trainings as needed.

Qualifications and experience:

Bachelors’ degree in Agriculture, Crop Production or other related fields.

 At least one year of experience preferably in Organic farming, Conservation agriculture, and Climate smart agriculture.

 Having technical expertise in livestock husbandry will be an added value.

 Fluency in spoken and written English and Kinyarwanda.

 Ability to multitask, priorities, and manage time efficiently

 Excellent communication skills

 Accurate attention to details

 Goal-oriented, organized team player

 Ability to work well with management and staff at all levels

 Passion for Gardens for Health’s vision and values, with a commitment to serving the organization mission

Equal Employment Opportunity

Gardens for Health International is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer fully dedicated to achieving a diverse staff. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage and welcome all interested potential applicants, regardless of background or prior experience volunteering with Gardens for Health International, to apply.

Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)

Gardens for Health International has zero – tolerance policy for exploitative and abusive relationships. Gardens for Health International will ensure the fulfillment of our moral obligation to protect minor children and other vulnerable members of society from abuse, exploitation, neglect, and other forms of violence.

Child Safeguarding:  

Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

Health and Safety:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with GHI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

How to Apply

Qualified and interested candidates are recommended to email their Resume with a signed cover letter in a single PDF format and any supporting documents to careers@gardensforhealth.org

We are an impact-driven organization with a deep commitment to ensuring that every program we design meets and responds to the unique needs of the communities we serve. Our team is flexible, innovative, and passionate about sparking lasting change.

About the Role

The Agriculture Associate will be in charge of the overseeing of the agriculture related partnerships on the farm. He/She will ensure the farm is growing crops according to the farm strategy and GHI vision, that the farm is well-maintained and healthy, and that all farm tasks related to the program are completed on time.

He/She will also participate in the farm tours along with the Ag team to organization, visitors and donors. He/She will also build capacity of farm technicians on the permaculture and conservation agriculture principles and practices. He/She will be assisting to the development of different reports to farm project partners and represent the farm to external partners.

Overview of the Role

Position: Agriculture Associate

Place of Work: Ndera, Gasabo with travel to the field as required

Staff reporting to this position: None

Reports to: Agriculture Coordinator

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Works alongside with farm technicians to implement the planned activities at the farm
  • Record all farm data including farm produce into Commcare
  • Lead homemade pesticide preparation, ensure its quality and research on types of pests which can be managed by such pesticide
  • Lead manure production from the farm and check quality depends on the techniques applied.
  • Lead seeds’ saving and advise farm team accordingly to ensure the quality of seeds
  • Preparation of crop plan and lead its’ implementation on seasonal basis
  • Lead farm related trials, records keeping and reporting
  • Collaborate with the farm livestock technician to monitor and manage livestock farming activities 
  • Conducts agricultural trainings for fellow farm technicians on permaculture principles practices
  • Monitoring the on-going farm activities and preparing farm expense requests and monthly budgets
  • Work with the farm technicians to hire part-time workers and distributes assignments and payment to them
  • Work closely with the farm technicians ensuring that all equipment, machinery and facilities are kept to an optimum level.

Broader role at GHI

  • Conducts farm tours for visitors and educates permanent staff and fellows about the farm
  • Provide support to the Ag Team in various ways, including curriculum development and external trainings as needed.

Qualifications and experience:

  • Bachelors’ degree in Agriculture, Crop Production or other related fields.
  • At least one year of experience preferably in Organic farming, Conservation agriculture, and Climate smart agriculture.
  • Having technical expertise in livestock husbandry will be an added value.
  • Fluency in spoken and written English and Kinyarwanda.
  • Ability to multitask, priorities, and manage time efficiently
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Accurate attention to details
  • Goal-oriented, organized team player
  • Ability to work well with management and staff at all levels
  • Passion for Gardens for Health’s vision and values, with a commitment to serving the organization mission

Equal Employment Opportunity

Gardens for Health International is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer fully dedicated to achieving a diverse staff. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage and welcome all interested potential applicants, regardless of background or prior experience volunteering with Gardens for Health International, to apply.

Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)

Gardens for Health International has zero – tolerance policy for exploitative and abusive relationships. Gardens for Health International will ensure the fulfillment of our moral obligation to protect minor children and other vulnerable members of society from abuse, exploitation, neglect, and other forms of violence.

Child Safeguarding:  

Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

Health and Safety:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with GHI Health and Safety policies and procedures.  

How to Apply

Qualified and interested candidates are recommended to email their Resume with a signed cover letter in a single PDF format and any supporting documents to careers@gardensforhealth.org

Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is looking for two (2) Special Needs Education Coordinator (SNECO)
 Project

 Job titles

 Place of work 
 RUB Head office, KigaliGATSIBO and MUSANZE for 2 SNECOs
 Line Manager for SNECO
 Project coordinator
 Duration and type of Contract
 Full time and annual renewable subject to performance and availability of funds
 Application deadline
 October 2nd 2026
 Organizational background

Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is a national organization committed to promote the rights, inclusion, education, empowerment and socio-economic well-being of blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda.

The Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is a non-governmental organization that was founded in August 1994 as a National unified voice for persons with visual impairment. After registering with the Rwanda Governance Board under the legal personality number 60/05 on 16/03/1995, and complies with the new law No 058/2024 of 20/06/2024 and related regulations. RUB works towards the improvement of the situation of blind people through education and rehabilitation to facilitate meaningful equality and integration. RUB holds membership in 2 National umbrellas including UPHLS and NUDOR and also affiliated to the African Union of the Blind (AFUB) and the World Blind Union (WBU). The organization has 64 well established branches in all districts of the country and all those branches managed by persons with visual impairment themselves. RUB’ activities aim at improving the living conditions of Blind and Partially Sighted (BPS) persons through advocacy, promoting the education of blind and partially sighted persons, capacity development of members and rehabilitation program/service.

1.1. Vision

 The vision of RUB is to ‘achieve a situation where people with visual impairment enjoy the same rights as other citizens, receive rehabilitation and education and have equal access to employment’.

1.2. Mission 

RUB's mission is to ‘work towards the improvement of the situation of people with visual impairment through rehabilitation and education to facilitate meaningful equality and integration into the society’.

1.3. Objectives 

With the purpose of improving the living condition of Blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda, RUB sets the following objectives to guides its strategic implementations:

Bring together persons with visual impairment in a national organization to promote their fundamental rights; 

 Raise awareness on needs, potentials, and aspirations of persons with visual impairment in Rwanda; 

 Advocate for access to education and rehabilitation of persons with visual impairment through dialogue with the government and other partners in development; 

 Seek support to provide adequate and appropriate services to persons with visual impairment; 

 Promote prevention of visual impairment through dialogue with relevant authorities; 

 Promote the inclusion of persons with visual impairment in sport and cultural activities. 

About project

Under support from the Marga Schulze Foundation through CBM, RUB is implementing a multi-year project 2026-2028 to advance educational inclusion and equitable learning opportunities for blind and partially sighted girls and women in Rwanda.

The project recognizes that girls and women with disabilities experience multiple and intersecting barriers to education. These may include inaccessible learning environments and materials, limited availability of appropriate support, negative social attitudes, inadequate teacher preparation, financial constraints, and limited opportunities for participation in decisions that affect their education and future.

Children with disabilities in Rwanda continue to face significant barriers to accessing, participating in, and completing education. Girls with disabilities may experience additional barriers because of the intersection of disability and gender. These challenges can be particularly pronounced in rural and emergency-affected communities.

The proposed project therefore seeks to move beyond simply increasing access to schools. It aims to support meaningful participation, retention, learning, progression and empowerment, while strengthening schools and communities to become more inclusive of all learners.

A central element of the project will be the development and testing of practical approaches to inclusive education that can generate evidence and learning for wider application in Rwanda.

2.1 Overall Objective

To identify, support and empower girls and boys with disabilities, both in and out of school, particularly in rural and emergency-affected areas of Rwanda, with a specific focus on improving educational opportunities and outcomes for girls and women with visual impairments.

2.2 Specific Objectives

Identify girls and boys with disabilities who are in and out of school across selected rural and emergency-affected contexts in Rwanda and assess their individual and educational support needs.

 Provide identified girls and women with visual impairments with appropriate and comprehensive support to enhance their enrolment, participation, retention, learning and progression.

 Support selected schools to develop and implement a holistic approach to inclusion that enables all learners, including learners with disabilities, to participate and learn equitably.

 Empower women with visual impairments with knowledge, skills and opportunities in human rights, social justice and advocacy, enabling them to contribute to policy, practice and decision-making on disability inclusion and gender equity.

 RUB is therefore inviting qualified Rwandans with or without disabilities to apply for this opportunity.

Position Information

3.1 Special needs education coordinator (SNECO)

Position
 Special needs education coordinator (SNECO)

Main Purpose of the Position
 The Special Needs Education Coordinator will be responsible for coordinating and providing technical expertise for RUB's special and inclusive education interventions.The position will work closely with learners, families, teachers, school administration, local authorities, organizations of persons with disabilities, and other stakeholders to promote inclusive and accessible education for Blind and Partially Sighted learners and other special educational needs.
 Key Responsibilities
 SNECO will:Ensure the implementation and coordination of RUB's special and inclusive education programmes.Improve access to quality and accessible education for blind and partially sighted learners.Strengthen the capacity of teachers, schools, parents, and other stakeholders to support learners with disabilities.Promote the use of Braille, assistive technology, accessible learning materials, and inclusive teaching approaches.Strengthen collaboration between RUB and relevant education stakeholders.Contribute to evidence-based advocacy and policy engagement on inclusive education.Monitor and document education programme results, lessons learned, and good practices.
 Qualifications 
 In academic Qualifications, applicants should meet the following requirements:A Bachelor's degree in Special Needs Education, Inclusive Education, Education, Disability Studies, Educational Psychology, or a related field
 Professional Experience
 At least three (3) years of relevant professional experience in special needs education, inclusive education, disability programming, or a related area.Demonstrated experience working with blind and partially sighted learners is highly desirable.Knowledge of inclusive education policies, approaches, and practices.Knowledge of Braille, assistive technology, and accessible learning materials is an advantage.Experience in training, mentoring, programme coordination, monitoring, and reportingExperience in an NGO, civil society organization, organizations of persons with disabilitiesThe candidate should demonstrate:Strong knowledge of special and inclusive education.Excellent programme coordination and organizational skills.Strong communication and interpersonal skills.Ability to work effectively with persons with disabilities and diverse stakeholders.
 Required Skills and Competencies
 Good analytical, report-writing, and documentation skills.Ability to work independently and as part of a team.Strong computer skills, particularly Microsoft Office applications.Good advocacy and stakeholder engagement skills.Commitment to disability rights, equality, inclusion, and safeguarding.Knowledge of Braille is an added advantageSafeguarding and Professional Standards
 How to Apply

Interested and qualified candidates should submit the following documents:

 Application letter addressed to the RUB Executive Director, specifying the position your are applying for.,

 An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) with contact details of at least three referees.

 Copies of relevant academic and professional certificates.

 A copy of a valid identification document.

 Applications should be submitted as hard copy to RUB office located at Nyarugenge district, Muhima sector, Amahoro cell, Kabirizi village, KN7 Ave poids lourds Road not later than October 2nd 2026 at 12Pm:00

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Equal Opportunity and Inclusion

RUB is committed to equal opportunity, diversity, and inclusion in its recruitment processes. Qualified persons with disabilities and women are strongly encouraged to apply.

RUB reserves the right to verify the information provided by applicants and to conduct appropriate reference and background checks before appointment.

Approved by

MUGISHA Jacques 

Executive Director/RUB

The organization has 64 well established branches in all districts of the country and all those branches managed by persons with visual impairment themselves. RUB’ activities aim at improving the living conditions of Blind and Partially Sighted (BPS) persons through advocacy, promoting the education of blind and partially sighted persons, capacity development of members and rehabilitation program/service.

1.1. Vision

 The vision of RUB is to ‘achieve a situation where people with visual impairment enjoy the same rights as other citizens, receive rehabilitation and education and have equal access to employment’.

1.2. Mission 

RUB's mission is to ‘work towards the improvement of the situation of people with visual impairment through rehabilitation and education to facilitate meaningful equality and integration into the society’.

1.3. Objectives 

With the purpose of improving the living condition of Blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda, RUB sets the following objectives to guides its strategic implementations:

Bring together persons with visual impairment in a national organization to promote their fundamental rights; 

 Raise awareness on needs, potentials, and aspirations of persons with visual impairment in Rwanda; 

 Advocate for access to education and rehabilitation of persons with visual impairment through dialogue with the government and other partners in development; 

 Seek support to provide adequate and appropriate services to persons with visual impairment; 

 Promote prevention of visual impairment through dialogue with relevant authorities; 

 Promote the inclusion of persons with visual impairment in sport and cultural activities.

These may include inaccessible learning environments and materials, limited availability of appropriate support, negative social attitudes, inadequate teacher preparation, financial constraints, and limited opportunities for participation in decisions that affect their education and future.

Girls with disabilities may experience additional barriers because of the intersection of disability and gender. These challenges can be particularly pronounced in rural and emergency-affected communities.

The proposed project therefore seeks to move beyond simply increasing access to schools. It aims to support meaningful participation, retention, learning, progression and empowerment, while strengthening schools and communities to become more inclusive of all learners.

jobinrwanda.title: Accountant Receivable
jobinrwanda.description:
Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course Ltd

Job Description

Title:Accountant Receivable

Reports to:Chief Accountant 

Job Purpose:

The Accountant Receivables is responsible for managing all accounts receivable functions of Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course Ltd. This includes billing, posting payments, reconciling customer accounts, monitoring outstanding balances, and ensuring timely collection of revenues from members, guests, and corporate clients. The role also supports accuracy in reporting and coordination with operational departments to maintain financial integrity and excellent customer service.

Key Responsibilities

Prepare and issue invoices for all sales transactions, including F&B, golf, membership, accommodation, wellness, and corporate events.

 Record and reconcile daily revenue from point-of-sale systems (e.g., MICROS) and Property Management Systems (PMS).

 Post customer payments accurately and in a timely manner.

 Maintain up-to-date accounts receivable records, ensuring accuracy and completeness of customer ledgers.

 Follow up on outstanding payments and ensure collections are made within agreed credit terms.

 Monitor member accounts and prepare monthly statements for distribution.

 Liaise with the Membership, F&B, Golf, and Commercial departments to confirm billing details and resolve discrepancies.

 Work closely with the Chief Accountant and finance director to reconcile revenues and receivables at month-end.

 Coordinate with the Front Office and Cashiers to ensure accurate posting of guest folios and event charges.

 Support management with data for financial reports, audits, and budgeting exercises.

 Ensure all receivable transactions comply with company financial policies and internal controls.

 Assist in maintaining proper documentation for all billing and collection activities.

 Prepare reports on overdue accounts and recommend actions for collection or escalation.

 Participate in the monthly and year-end closing process.

 Prepare aging analysis of accounts receivable and highlight delinquent accounts.

 Support periodic revenue reconciliation between POS, PMS, and accounting systems.

 Generate customer account summaries and assist in financial statement preparation.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

 Professional certification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) is an added advantage.

 Minimum of 3 years’ experience in accounting, preferably in hospitality, leisure, or service-oriented industries.

 Solid understanding of accounting principles, billing, and collections processes.

 Proficiency in accounting software (e.g., Sage, QuickBooks, or ERP systems).

 Experience with hospitality systems such as MICROS POS, Opera / Protel / Cloudbeds PMS, and membership billing platforms is an asset.

Key Skills & Competencies

Strong analytical and numerical skills with attention to detail.

 Excellent communication and customer service skills for interacting with clients and members.

 Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams (Finance, F&B, Golf, Commercial, Guest Experience).

 High integrity, confidentiality, and commitment to accuracy.

 Time management and ability to handle multiple priorities under tight deadlines.

 Strong problem-solving and reconciliation abilities.

Required documents: 

A detailed CV with 3 contacts of professional referees. 

 A one-page signed cover letter with a motivation statement in relation to the responsibilities and requirements for this position. 

 Copies of academic degree, professional training certificates, and other relevant training certificates. 

 A copy of your national ID 

How to Apply

The deadline for submitting applications is Thursday, October 08, 2026, at 17:00 hrs Rwanda time. 

 All applicants must send their zipped documents to hr@palasthotelrwanda.com with the subject line " Accountant Receivable Position." 

 Only selected candidates for interview will be contacted.

Strategic Leadership & Business Management

Provide overall leadership and strategic direction for Palast Rock Hotel.

 Develop and implement annual business plans, operational strategies, and performance objectives aligned with the hotel's strategic goals.

 Translate the hotel's strategic objectives into clear departmental priorities, targets, and action plans.

 Lead initiatives aimed at improving operational efficiency, profitability, service quality, and business growth.

 Advise the Group CEO and senior management on hotel performance, business opportunities, operational challenges, and strategic priorities.

 Represent the hotel in key business, professional, government, corporate, and stakeholder engagements.

 Promote a culture of professionalism, accountability, teamwork, innovation, and service excellence.

Hotel Operations & Service Excellence

Provide overall oversight of the hotel's day-to-day operations and ensure effective coordination across all departments.

 Oversee accommodation, restaurants and bars, conferences, weddings and events, wellness and recreational facilities, and other hotel services.

 Ensure departments operate in accordance with approved policies, procedures, service standards, and operational requirements.

 Monitor service delivery and ensure appropriate action is taken to address operational gaps and improve efficiency.

 Monitor guest satisfaction and ensure guest complaints and service issues are addressed promptly and professionally.

 Ensure appropriate standards of cleanliness, safety, maintenance, functionality, and presentation of hotel facilities and equipment.

 Oversee the implementation of quality assurance and continuous service improvement initiatives.

 Ensure effective planning and coordination of major conferences, weddings, events, and other functions hosted by the hotel.

Financial Performance & Cost Management

Take overall accountability for the financial performance and profitability of the hotel.

  Review and monitor budgets, financial reports, forecasts, revenue performance, and expenditure plans.

Monitor hotel revenues, operational costs, departmental performance, and profitability against approved targets.

 Ensure effective cost control and responsible utilization of hotel resources.

 Support the implementation of revenue optimization and business development strategies.

 Review and authorize purchases, contracts, and operational expenditures within approved authority limits.

 Work closely with the Finance & Administration Manager and Group Finance function to ensure accurate financial reporting, financial controls, and compliance.

 Monitor key financial indicators and ensure appropriate corrective actions are taken where performance is below target.

Sales, Marketing & Business Development

Provide leadership and support in the development and implementation of sales, marketing, and revenue-generation strategies.

 Drive initiatives aimed at increasing room occupancy, food and beverage revenue, conferences, events, weddings, and other revenue streams.

 Build and maintain strong relationships with corporate clients, government institutions, travel agencies, business partners, and other key stakeholders.

 Identify new business opportunities, partnerships, and potential markets for the hotel.

 Monitor market trends, customer preferences, competitor activities, and industry developments to support the hotel's competitiveness.

 Promote the PRH brand, reputation, products, and services through appropriate business and market engagement activities.

 Ensure appropriate staffing levels, workforce planning, and deployment of employees in line with operational requirements.

 Ensure clear departmental objectives, performance targets, and accountability across the hotel.

 Promote staff development, coaching, training, succession planning, and employee engagement initiatives.

 Foster a professional, respectful, collaborative, and performance-oriented working environment.

 Ensure appropriate measures are in place to safeguard hotel assets, guests, employees, and business operations.

Achievement of approved hotel revenue and profitability targets.

 Room occupancy and Average Daily Rate (ADR) performance.

 Growth in revenue from accommodation, food and beverage, conferences, events, weddings, and other hotel services.

 Achievement of agreed departmental and operational performance targets.

 Guest satisfaction, customer feedback, and resolution of guest complaints.

  Improvement and maintenance of hotel service quality and operational standards.

 Effective cost control and adherence to approved budgets.

 Timely and effective implementation of approved business and operational plans.

 Employee productivity, performance, engagement, and retention.

 Compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, safety, and hotel standards.

 Effective implementation of internal controls and corrective actions.

 Growth in corporate, institutional, travel trade, and other strategic business relationships.

 Successful execution of conferences, weddings, events, and other major hotel functions.

 Timely submission of accurate operational and management reports.

 Progress toward the hotel's strategic objectives, including its ambition to achieve 4-Star recognition and maintain a 4+ Star guest experience.

Bachelor’s Degree in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, Hotel Management, or a related field.

 Master’s Degree in Business Administration (MBA) or Hospitality Management is an added advantage.

 Minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in hotel or hospitality management.

 At least 5 years in a senior management or leadership role within the hospitality industry.

 Strong understanding of hotel operations, financial management, customer service, and business development.

 Experience managing multi-department hotel operations including accommodation, food & beverage, events, and recreational services.

 Knowledge of hospitality industry regulations, health & safety standards, and operational best practices.

Strong leadership, people management, and team-building skills.

 Strategic planning, organizational management, and business growth orientation.

 Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and conflict-resolution abilities.

 Strong financial management, budgeting, and operational analysis skills.

 Good understanding of hotel operations, performance management, revenue optimization, and customer service standards.

 Excellent communication, negotiation, interpersonal, and stakeholder relationship-management skills.

 High level of professionalism, integrity, accountability, and commitment to quality standards.

 Ability to work under pressure, manage multiple priorities, and maintain attention to detail.

Required documents: 

A detailed CV with 3 contacts of professional referees. 

 A one-page signed cover letter with a motivation statement in relation to the responsibilities and requirements for this position. 

 Copies of academic degree, professional training certificates, and other relevant training certificates. 

 A copy of your national ID 

How to Apply

The deadline for submitting applications is Thursday, October 08, 2026, at 17:00 hrs Rwanda time. 

 All applicants must send their zipped documents to hr@palasthotelrwanda.com with the subject line " General Manager Position." 

 Only selected candidates for interview will be contacted.

jobinrwanda.title: Driver
jobinrwanda.description:
JOB ANNOUNCEMENT

INDATWA SACCO RUSIZI is a saving and credit cooperative created through the consolidation of 18 Umurenge SACCOs operating in Rusizi District, in line with Rwanda’s SACCO reform agenda aimed at strengthening governance, capital adequacy, risk management, and service delivery. The consolidation complies with Law No. 057/2024 governing cooperatives and Law No. 072/2021 governing deposit-taking microfinance institutions, and aligns with BNR regulatory standards.

It is from that background that the Management of INDATWA SACCO RUSIZI informs the public that it is recruiting competent and qualified staff to fill the following positions:

S/N
 Vacant Post
 Number of Staff Required
 Key Responsibilities & Requirements
 1
 Driver
 1

 Under the supervision and guidance of the Logistics and Procurement Officer, the Driver is responsible for:

 Driving SACCO vehicles or motorcycles safely for authorized official activities.

 Transporting staff, management, documents, and official materials as required.

 Conducting daily checks and ensuring proper cleanliness and maintenance of the assigned vehicle or motorcycle.

 Keeping accurate records of mileage, fuel consumption, servicing, and movements.

 Reporting faults, accidents, and maintenance needs promptly.

 Ensuring all required vehicle or motorcycle documents are valid.

 Observing traffic laws, road safety requirements, and SACCO policies.

 Performing other duties assigned by management.

 Required Qualifications and Experience

 At least a Secondary School Certificate (A2) or equivalent.

 A valid driving permit for the category A & B 

 At least 2 years of relevant professional driving experience.

 Experience in driving for an organization or financial institution is an added advantage.

 Good knowledge of road safety, traffic regulations, and basic vehicle/motorcycle maintenance.

 Good communication skills, discipline, reliability, and a clean driving record.

 General Requirement

 To be Rwandan

 Not to have been definitely sentenced to a term of imprisonment equal to or exceeding six (6) months;

 Not to have been dismissed from any other institution unless applicant is entitled to reinstatement under laws and regulations in force;

 Not have been involved in the bankruptcy of a financial institution;

 Required Documents for application:

An application letter addressed to the Chairperson of BoD of INDATWA SACCO RUSIZI.

 A detailed and updated Curriculum Vitae.

 Copy of academic degree, Transcript and Certificate where Required.

 A proof of work experience if any.

 A photocopy of the Identity card.

 Full addresses of three referees with recommendations letter, including preferably one of previous supervisors.

Submission of Applications

Interested and qualified candidates must submit their applications from their own email addresses to indatwa.rusizi@indatwa.dsacco.rw . Applications submitted using another person's email address will not be considered.

 Application Deadline is the 5th October, 2026. 

 Only a single document (PDF Format) will be considered

NB: E-mail subject should be the Applicant Names followed by a Position is applying for.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process. Done at Rusizi on the 21st September, 2026.

SEMUCYO Alsene Managing Director INDATWA SACCO RUSIZI

It has been established by law No 45/2012 of 14/01/2013 relating to the organization, functioning, and competence of the Council of pharmacists herein referred to as National Pharmacy Council.
jobinrwanda.description_html:
JOB ADVERTISEMENT

Position: REGISTRATION AND LICENSING OFFICER Organization: Rwanda National Pharmacy Council (NPC) Duty Station: Kigali, Rwanda Employment Type: Permanent, Full-time Salary: As per the NPC's approved salary structure. Application Deadline: October 3, 2026, at 5:00 PM (Kigali time)

ABOUT US

The National Pharmacy Council (NPC) is an independent statutory regulatory authority established by Law No. 45/2012 of 14/01/2013, mandated to ensure that the rules, honour and dignity of the pharmacy profession are upheld and that public health is protected. The Council promotes the principles of morality, integrity and dedication essential to pharmacy practice, and ensures that all its members comply with their professional obligations and the laws and regulations governing pharmacy professionals in Rwanda. The vision of the National Pharmacy Council is to become a Centre of Excellence in the regulation and control of the pharmacy profession.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The National Pharmacy Council is seeking to recruit a qualified and experienced Registration and Licensing Officer to be based in the City of Kigali. Under the overall supervision of the Permanent Secretary and Registrar, the Registration and Licensing Officer will support the effective administration and implementation of the Council’s registration, licensing, internship, indexing, pre-registration examination, and related professional regulatory functions. The Officer will ensure that registration and licensing processes are conducted efficiently, accurately, transparently, and in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, standards, and NPC procedures, while providing timely professional support and communication to pharmacy professionals, applicants, training institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Registration and licensing officer will be responsible for the following:

  • Review all matters relating to applicants for registration and licensing and determine applicants’ eligibility for registration including establishing the conditions, restrictions and requirements for registration; 
  • Establishing academic standards and the qualifications required for registration as a pharmacy professional in Rwanda; 
  • Coordinate the internship program for pharmacy professionals; 
  • Responsible for the timeous execution of the registration and licensing of pharmacy professionals; 
  • Participate in the development and execution of the NPC action plan and strategic plan; 
  •  Develop policies and requirements with respect to the registration, licensing and reinstating registrants; 
  • Set, administer and maintain policies on all matters related to assessment competencies, standards, principles, selection or design and processes; 
  • Work with technical committee to develop, administer and maintain assessments for the purposes of the registration processes; 
  • Establish protocols for substantial equivalence assessment processes; 
  • Standardize consolidation and timely dissemination of reports and statistics on registration data; 
  • Inform pharmacy professionals and the public about professional obligation and responsibilities of registration and licensing; R
  • Manage the communication related to the indexing, pre-registration exams, internship, registration, licensing and any other communication assigned by his/her supervisors; 
  • Initiation of the day-to-day activities of the Professional operations affairs department of the NPC; 
  • Perform any other duties assigned to her/him either by the Professional operations Manager and/or the Registrar 

QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

Educational Qualifications

  • A Bachelor degree in Pharmacy with at least 3 years of experience.
  • Having the License to practice Pharmacy Profession in Rwanda is a must; 
  • Be in good standing in the pharmacy profession and practice.

Knowledge and Skills

  • organizational skills, both analytical and problem solving, and the ability to work with confidential documents; 
  • The ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously and being able to work under pressure; 
  • Demonstrated leadership, strategic planning, visioning and management abilities; 
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with senior-level colleagues; particularly interacting productively, and comfortably with NPC stakeholders; 
  • Excellent writing skills, communication skills and presentation skills in English are required, along with good French; 
  • Computer literate and a friendly user of most Microsoft Office programs; 
  • Must be able to work independently and solve complex problems using own judgment/discretion; 
  • Must be able to develop/maintain effective partnerships with medical, pharmaceutical and health teaching institutions. 

HOW TO APPLY

Interested and qualified candidates should submit a complete application package comprising:

  • A cover letter addressed to the Chairperson of the National Pharmacy Council
  • A Curriculum Vitae
  • Proof of relevant work experience
  • A notarized copy of the Pharmacy degree
  • A notarized copy of the equivalence certificate of the degree from the higher Education Council (for applicant who studied abroad)
  • A copy of the license to practice pharmacy
  • A copy of the National Identity Card
  • A valid criminal record certificate, to be submitted by the successful candidate prior to issuance of the appointment letter.

APPLICATION SUBMISSION

  • Submission Deadline: October 3, 2026, at 5:00 PM (Kigali time) 
  • Submission Channel: Complete application packages must be submitted in hard copy. 
  • Submission Venue: National Pharmacy Council (NPC) Head Office, KG 632 St, Kimihurura, Rugando, City of Kigali.

jobinrwanda.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

About the Role

Seeking a driver to transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between OAF sites, maintain the fleet and cargo in excellent condition, and provide insights on truck operations and charging to inform future electric truck ownership.

Responsibilities

Cargo Transport

Transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between assigned OAF sites, ensuring delivery strictly to the specified locations within set timelines.

 Collaborate with the warehouse team to load, offload, and reload trucks, verifying that the physical cargo matches the exact quantity and quality stated on delivery documents.

 Secure all materials in transit using appropriate equipment to prevent loss, theft, tampering, or damage (e.g., perforations, wet bags, or torn stitching).

 Proactively gather information regarding the location and accessibility of field sites and chargers within the assigned district prior to departure.

Vehicle Maintenance

Conduct weekly vehicle checks, perform minor repairs, and submit maintenance requests to your manager to ensure that the vehicle under their care is kept in good running condition at all times.

 Mitigate damage to the truck by avoiding risky routes or driving techniques.

 Ensure safety and custody of the vehicles including tools.

 Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, registration, first aid kit, and necessary spare parts in the assigned vehicle.

 Ensure that, in the event of an accident involving the vehicle, the necessary steps required by rules and regulations are followed.

Documentation & Communication

Accurately manage all delivery documents, including Delivery Notes, Load Cards, and Truck Management Sheets (TMS). Return fully signed delivery documents to your manager within one (1) business day of delivery. 

 Obtain official signatures from authorized OAF representatives at both the originating and destination sites to confirm the exact weight/number of inputs dispatched and received.

 Immediately notify your manager via text (or call for urgent cases) in the event of accidents, field staff unavailability, data discrepancies, charging problems, mechanical problems, adverse weather, route accessibility issues, data discrepancies, or if any party refuses to sign the delivery documents.

 Communicate regularly relevant trial information, such as GPS coordinates, KM range, battery levels, charging experience, driving experience, road quality, etc.

 Ensure that all required driving training is successfully completed and certifications are kept up to date

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Valid category C driver’s licence

 Experience driving cargo trucks on dirt roads outside of Kigali

 Working knowledge of local roads and routes, ability to utilize maps / GPS systems

About the Role

Seeking a driver to transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between OAF sites, maintain the fleet and cargo in excellent condition, and provide insights on truck operations and charging to inform future electric truck ownership.

Responsibilities

Cargo Transport

Transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between assigned OAF sites, ensuring delivery strictly to the specified locations within set timelines.

 Collaborate with the warehouse team to load, offload, and reload trucks, verifying that the physical cargo matches the exact quantity and quality stated on delivery documents.

 Secure all materials in transit using appropriate equipment to prevent loss, theft, tampering, or damage (e.g., perforations, wet bags, or torn stitching).

 Proactively gather information regarding the location and accessibility of field sites and chargers within the assigned district prior to departure.

Vehicle Maintenance

Conduct weekly vehicle checks, perform minor repairs, and submit maintenance requests to your manager to ensure that the vehicle under their care is kept in good running condition at all times.

 Mitigate damage to the truck by avoiding risky routes or driving techniques.

 Ensure safety and custody of the vehicles including tools.

 Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, registration, first aid kit, and necessary spare parts in the assigned vehicle.

 Ensure that, in the event of an accident involving the vehicle, the necessary steps required by rules and regulations are followed.

Documentation & Communication

Accurately manage all delivery documents, including Delivery Notes, Load Cards, and Truck Management Sheets (TMS). Return fully signed delivery documents to your manager within one (1) business day of delivery. 

 Obtain official signatures from authorized OAF representatives at both the originating and destination sites to confirm the exact weight/number of inputs dispatched and received.

 Immediately notify your manager via text (or call for urgent cases) in the event of accidents, field staff unavailability, data discrepancies, charging problems, mechanical problems, adverse weather, route accessibility issues, data discrepancies, or if any party refuses to sign the delivery documents.

 Communicate regularly relevant trial information, such as GPS coordinates, KM range, battery levels, charging experience, driving experience, road quality, etc.

 Ensure that all required driving training is successfully completed and certifications are kept up to date

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Valid category C driver’s licence

 Experience driving cargo trucks on dirt roads outside of Kigali

 Working knowledge of local roads and routes, ability to utilize maps / GPS systems

 Working knowledge of electric vehicle mechanics (truck maintenance, interpret truck KM range / battery life)

 Sound knowledge of road safety regulations

 Effective communication skills (verbal and written) in Kinyarwanda

 Punctual and reliable, customer service
