brightermonday.title: Cluster Manager, Sales & Marketing
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

( 20911 )
At One&Only, we exist to create joy for our guests through anticipation, creativity, precision, empathy and warmth. We tailor every aspect of our guests’ stay to bring their dreams and desires to life. With an atmosphere that’s chic but wonderfully unstuffy™, and a team who are meticulous but warm, we seek to exceed our guests’ expectations at every possible turn.
Cushioned in the foothills of the breath-taking Virunga Volcano Range, One&Only Gorilla’s Nest makes the magical possible to enjoy a once-in-a-lifetime, personal encounter with the rare and majestic mountain gorilla, roaming free in its own natural habitat. The warm African charm is one of our most unique and valued assets. With abundant knowledge and generosity, we anticipate our guest’s every need and surpass expectations. Whether we are designing the perfect day out or arranging a romantic private dinner, we approach everything with imagination to spark a sense of playfulness, discovery and adventure. This is not simply our job, it’s our passion. We don’t just exist in the environment, we exist with the environment; from working the land or building a shelter, we like to give back in as many ways as we can to help our communities flourish.

 Position Details 
 Position Cluster Manager, Sales & Marketing 
 Department Sales & Marketing 
 Reports to Cluster General Manager and Regional Director of Sales & Marketing 
 Subordinates Sales and Marketing Team and Reservations Manager 
 Job Details & Requirements

Job Summary
To ensure the efficient running of the Sales and Marketing department through achieving budgeted Colleagues Satisfaction, Guest Satisfaction and GOP results for each area
Key Duties and Responsibilities

 Align management style, working practices and conduct with One & Only Gorillas Nest and Nyungwe Forest Tea Resort and Kerzner’s vision, Global Support values, operating standards and policies. To comply with Kerzner’s code of conduct at all times. 
 Personally build clear and open lines of communication with all departments 
 Understand and abide by all Government laws relating to the Sales and Marketing department. 
 Develop strategies and initiatives to increase resort’s market share. 
 Understand Rwanda’s business trend in terms of targeting right market. Also be aware of the political up lift of the country. 
 Work in conjunction with the F&B creating, implementing and assessing Food and Beverage promotions and marketing. 
 Be actively involved in maintaining all Kerzner International programs. 
 Be critical and demanding of operating standards. 
 Monitor and control all financial aspects of the business including the preparation of the annual commercial plan. 
 Add value through revenue growth and operational efficiency through process improvement; understand and focus on the key drivers of sales, associate and customer satisfaction, profitability, and quality 
 Build a team with different opinions, skills, experiences, and backgrounds; leverage personal, cultural, and functional differences to optimize team performance. 
 Align plans with business strategy; understand short- and long-term impact of business decisions. 
 Actively involved and work with Finance department in tour operator contracting. 
 Organize tour operator visits to One&Only and Rare Finds Rwanda to showcase the resorts on regular intervals. 
 Travel to various parts of the world to attend business fairs, meet up with tour operators to enhance business opportunities for the resort. 
 Ensure all communications are aligned to the One & Only and Rare Finds brand image. 
 Conduct regular creative events, key account appointments and activity programs to ensure all important contacts are regularly updated and entertained, keeping One & Only Gorillas Nest & Nyungwe Forest Tea Resort top of mind. 
 Develop and maintain rapport with key community contacts to ensure a visible presence in the community.

brightermonday.title: Logistics Intern
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

Background

The Supply Chain function supports the timely, efficient and accountable movement, storage and delivery of food, non-food items and logistics services. Reliable operational data is essential for planning, monitoring performance, anticipating constraints and supporting emergency preparedness. The intern will reinforce routine data analysis and operational follow-up while gaining practical exposure to end-to-end supply chain activities.

Purpose of the assignment

Under close supervision, the intern will support the consolidation, quality assurance, analysis and presentation of supply chain information. The assignment combines data work with practical exposure to transport, warehousing, commodity tracking, service provision and preparedness activities. It is a learning assignment and does not carry supervisory or decision-making authority.

Key responsibilities

Compile and clean data from operational records, spreadsheets, enterprise platforms and partner inputs; identify gaps, inconsistencies and duplicate records and follow up on corrections.
Support routine tracking of consignments from dispatch through receipt, including transport status, delivery timelines, outstanding documentation and exceptions requiring operational follow-up.
Prepare concise weekly and monthly analyses, visual summaries and management dashboards on volumes, lead times, service performance, stock movements and emerging bottlenecks.
Assist with transport planning and load allocation by organizing information on requirements, vehicle capacity, routes, delivery priorities and delivery schedules.
Support reconciliation of information across operational and financial records and maintain clear supporting documentation and audit trails.
Contribute to warehouse and inventory activities, including receipt and dispatch documentation, physical counts, stock reporting and investigation of variances.
Support demand mapping and operational planning for logistics services provided to partners, including requests, capacity, costs, service timelines and follow-up of completed services.
Contribute to emergency preparedness through scenario data, readiness trackers, partner and supplier mapping, and identification of potential transport, storage or staffing constraints.
Document recurring workflows and propose practical improvements, including simple automation or data-visualization solutions where appropriate.
Participate in coordination meetings, prepare action trackers and undertake other related learning tasks consistent with the purpose and level of the internship.

Expected outputs and learning objectives

Reliable, regularly updated operational datasets and trackers with documented validation checks.
Periodic analytical products that highlight trends, exceptions, risks and actions required.
A documented end-to-end view of at least one operational process, with feasible recommendations for improvement.
Practical exposure to transport, warehousing, inventory, delivery tracking, partner-service support and emergency preparedness.
A final learning note summarizing work completed, skills acquired and recommendations for sustaining useful tools or analyses.

Eligibility and minimum qualifications

Currently enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a recognized undergraduate or graduate programme in supply chain management, logistics, engineering, data science, information systems, statistics, economics, business administration or another relevant field, in accordance with the applicable internship eligibility rules.
Demonstrated ability to organize and analyse quantitative information using spreadsheets or comparable data-processing tools.
Ability to communicate clearly in written and spoken English.
Ability to work respectfully and effectively in a diverse team and to handle operational information with discretion.
Availability to work at the duty station and, where required, undertake authorized field travel.

Desirable qualifications

Coursework, project work or practical exposure related to logistics, transport, warehousing, inventory, procurement, humanitarian operations or emergency preparedness.
Experience consolidating data from several sources, conducting data-quality checks and presenting findings to non-technical colleagues.
Familiarity with business-intelligence, enterprise-resource-planning, mapping, database or programming tools. No prior knowledge of a specific organizational platform is required.
Working knowledge of French or another language relevant to the operating environment.
Evidence of initiative, curiosity and practical problem solving.

Competencies

Analytical thinking: distinguishes reliable evidence from assumptions and draws proportionate conclusions.
Attention to detail: checks data and documentation carefully and escalates discrepancies.
Communication: presents technical information in a concise and accessible manner.
Collaboration: builds constructive working relationships and seeks guidance appropriately.
Planning and accountability: organizes tasks, meets agreed deadlines and maintains clear records.
Integrity and respect: acts consistently with organizational values, standards of conduct and safeguarding requirements.

Supervision and performance review

The supervisor will agree a workplan and learning objectives at the start of the assignment, provide regular guidance, and review progress against the expected outputs. Access to operational information and digital tools will be limited to what is required for assigned tasks and governed by applicable data-protection and information-security rules.

Selection approach

Candidates should be assessed consistently against the published criteria. A practical exercise may be used to evaluate data organization, basic analysis and written communication. Prior exposure to the organization or to a particular internal platform should not be treated as a mandatory requirement or used as a substitute for an objective assessment of relevant skills.

Administrative conditions

The selected candidate must satisfy all applicable internship eligibility, medical, security and administrative requirements.
The internship does not create an expectation of subsequent employment.
Close relatives of personnel are subject to the organization’s applicable eligibility and conflict-of-interest rules.
The organization is committed to equal opportunity and to a respectful workplace free from harassment, discrimination and abuse of authority.

Under close supervision, the intern will support the consolidation, quality assurance, analysis and presentation of supply chain information. The assignment combines data work with practical exposure to transport, warehousing, commodity tracking, service provision and preparedness activities. It is a learning assignment and does not carry supervisory or decision-making authority.

Key responsibilities

  • Compile and clean data from operational records, spreadsheets, enterprise platforms and partner inputs; identify gaps, inconsistencies and duplicate records and follow up on corrections.
  • Support routine tracking of consignments from dispatch through receipt, including transport status, delivery timelines, outstanding documentation and exceptions requiring operational follow-up.
  • Prepare concise weekly and monthly analyses, visual summaries and management dashboards on volumes, lead times, service performance, stock movements and emerging bottlenecks.
  • Assist with transport planning and load allocation by organizing information on requirements, vehicle capacity, routes, delivery priorities and delivery schedules.
  • Support reconciliation of information across operational and financial records and maintain clear supporting documentation and audit trails.
  • Contribute to warehouse and inventory activities, including receipt and dispatch documentation, physical counts, stock reporting and investigation of variances.
  • Support demand mapping and operational planning for logistics services provided to partners, including requests, capacity, costs, service timelines and follow-up of completed services.
  • Contribute to emergency preparedness through scenario data, readiness trackers, partner and supplier mapping, and identification of potential transport, storage or staffing constraints.
  • Document recurring workflows and propose practical improvements, including simple automation or data-visualization solutions where appropriate.
  • Participate in coordination meetings, prepare action trackers and undertake other related learning tasks consistent with the purpose and level of the internship.

Expected outputs and learning objectives

  • Reliable, regularly updated operational datasets and trackers with documented validation checks.
  • Periodic analytical products that highlight trends, exceptions, risks and actions required.
  • A documented end-to-end view of at least one operational process, with feasible recommendations for improvement.
  • Practical exposure to transport, warehousing, inventory, delivery tracking, partner-service support and emergency preparedness.
  • A final learning note summarizing work completed, skills acquired and recommendations for sustaining useful tools or analyses.

Eligibility and minimum qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in, or recently graduated from, a recognized undergraduate or graduate programme in supply chain management, logistics, engineering, data science, information systems, statistics, economics, business administration or another relevant field, in accordance with the applicable internship eligibility rules.
  • Demonstrated ability to organize and analyse quantitative information using spreadsheets or comparable data-processing tools.
  • Ability to communicate clearly in written and spoken English.
  • Ability to work respectfully and effectively in a diverse team and to handle operational information with discretion.
  • Availability to work at the duty station and, where required, undertake authorized field travel.

Desirable qualifications

  • Coursework, project work or practical exposure related to logistics, transport, warehousing, inventory, procurement, humanitarian operations or emergency preparedness.
  • Experience consolidating data from several sources, conducting data-quality checks and presenting findings to non-technical colleagues.
  • Familiarity with business-intelligence, enterprise-resource-planning, mapping, database or programming tools. No prior knowledge of a specific organizational platform is required.
  • Working knowledge of French or another language relevant to the operating environment.
  • Evidence of initiative, curiosity and practical problem solving.

Competencies

  • Analytical thinking: distinguishes reliable evidence from assumptions and draws proportionate conclusions.
  • Attention to detail: checks data and documentation carefully and escalates discrepancies.
  • Communication: presents technical information in a concise and accessible manner.
  • Collaboration: builds constructive working relationships and seeks guidance appropriately.
  • Planning and accountability: organizes tasks, meets agreed deadlines and maintains clear records.
  • Integrity and respect: acts consistently with organizational values, standards of conduct and safeguarding requirements.

Supervision and performance review

The supervisor will agree a workplan and learning objectives at the start of the assignment, provide regular guidance, and review progress against the expected outputs. Access to operational information and digital tools will be limited to what is required for assigned tasks and governed by applicable data-protection and information-security rules.

Selection approach

Candidates should be assessed consistently against the published criteria. A practical exercise may be used to evaluate data organization, basic analysis and written communication. Prior exposure to the organization or to a particular internal platform should not be treated as a mandatory requirement or used as a substitute for an objective assessment of relevant skills.

Administrative conditions

  • The selected candidate must satisfy all applicable internship eligibility, medical, security and administrative requirements.
  • The internship does not create an expectation of subsequent employment.
  • Close relatives of personnel are subject to the organization’s applicable eligibility and conflict-of-interest rules.
  • The organization is committed to equal opportunity and to a respectful workplace free from harassment, discrimination and abuse of authority.

brightermonday.title: Experience Expert
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

( 20979 )
At One&Only, we exist to create joy for our guests through anticipation, creativity, precision, empathy and warmth. We tailor every aspect of our guests’ stay to bring their dreams and desires to life. With an atmosphere that’s chic but wonderfully unstuffy™, and a team who are meticulous but warm, we seek to exceed our guests’ expectations at every possible turn.
Cushioned in the foothills of the breath-taking Virunga Volcano Range, One&Only Gorilla’s Nest makes the magical possible to enjoy a once-in-a-lifetime, personal encounter with the rare and majestic mountain gorilla, roaming free in its own natural habitat. The warm African charm is one of our most unique and valued assets. With abundant knowledge and generosity, we anticipate our guest’s every need and surpass expectations. Whether we are designing the perfect day out or arranging a romantic private dinner, we approach everything with imagination to spark a sense of playfulness, discovery and adventure. This is not simply our job, it’s our passion. We don’t just exist in the environment, we exist with the environment; from working the land or building a shelter, we like to give back in as many ways as we can to help our communities flourish.
1 Position Details

 Position Guest Experience Expert 
 Level Colleague 
 Department Experience Department 
 Reports to Experience Manager 
 Subordinates None

2 Job Details & Requirements
Job Summary
Organize, arrange and follow through personalised tours and itineraries, field activities and services for the guests of One&Only Gorillas Nest through direct or indirect co-ordination with other departments and external/governmental excursion providers.
Being responsible for accurate and timely information delivery to guests with regards to history, cultural heritage as well as natural particularities of the property and destination. Additionally, responsible for daily activities, in line with One&Only Gorillas nest services and functionalities. When necessary and appropriate accompanying guests on arranged excursions and activities.
Key Duties And Responsibilities

 Responsible for finding the best quality, high-end providers and activities in the area. 
 Ensure that allocated guests receive the activities, tours and excursions in an informed, timely and professional manner, while respecting the policies, procedures and systems of One&Only Gorillas Nest . This is to be carried out by maintaining personal contact with the guest and providing continuity to the guests’ interactions with the other departments of the One&Only Gorillas Nest . 
 Arrange on and off-site activities, tours/transfers and special requests of guests ensuring maximum comfort and convenience for the duration of their visit. 
 Be responsible for a particular zone of the resorts’ reserve area, with regards to ecological maintenance, security and monitoring, and to ensure its’ sound development as part of an integrated environmental policy for the property. 
 Report on any maintenance needs relevant Department/s. 
 Maintain an updated deep and comprehensive knowledge of the resort’s services, its function and offerings. Actively enquire and recommend services and activities to guests and visitors, ensuring that they are kept informed of the full range of options available to them. 
 As directed, carry out property conservation and land care work that include but are not limited to the maintenance of decks, shelters, tracks and trails, slashing and mowing, maintenance of fences, planting and maintaining flora, and the removal of deceased wildlife from the property. 
 Report to your assigned working area according to the scheduled roster, correctly groomed and in a condition to perform assigned duties. 
 Take a proactive approach to ensuring the guests experience is memorable by participating in guest activities, as required, within the scope of responsibilities. 
 Respond to emergency situations based on property’s emergency procedures and ensure that in these situations the safety of the people and the protection of company equipment is adequately. 
 It is your responsibility to know what these are at all times. 
 Adheres to all resort policies, procedures and standards laid out by One&Only Resorts.

Skills, Experience & Educational Requirements
Knowledge & Skills

 Any of the following specialized areas of interest, ability or training would be relevant: 

 Knowledge of African and Rwandan flora and fauna, natural history, history and culture. 
 Natural Sciences. 
 Professional guiding with Knowledge of wildlife 
 Fluency in English is essential; any additional languages are preferable. 

3 Core VAlues & Competencies
Blow Away The Customer

 I care and work towards exceeding the expectations of my customers 
 I am proactive and deliver unique and everlasting memories for our customers

Develop Passionate and Committed People

 I am committed to being thoughtful towards our colleagues 
 I am passionate about my role

Continuously Strive for Perfections (good enough never is)

 I constantly seek new ways and ideas to improve what I do 
 I am inspired to make a difference

Achieve Sustainable Bottom Line Performance

 I am honest and fair 
 I take responsibility and contribute towards the financial performance of where I work

4 Functional competencies
Grooming

 I present a professional image according to established standards

Communication

 I speak in a clear and concise manner both in person and over the phone 
 I express ideas in a clear and coherent manner

Functional Skills and Knowledge

 I demonstrate my knowledge and skills effectively 
 I take responsibility for my actions

Time Keeping & Grooming

 I report for work in my department on time daily

Response to Supervision

 I demonstrate respect for my leaders 
 I respond to supervision positively

Our brand is expanding faster than ever before. We are investing in the growth of our company, and that means we are committed to investing in you. Join a team that is open-hearted, intuitive, generous, and spontaneous in spirit. We believe in making our guests happy beyond anything they have ever imagined. We wow them at every turn and create memories that will last a lifetime. You will be at the heart of this vision, to constantly innovate to deliver Amazing Experiences and Everlasting Memories.

Position Summary
Our jobs aren’t just about serving guests during a banquet or event. Instead, we want to build an experience that is memorable and unique. Our Guest Event Experts are skilled in a wide range of event functions with responsibility for making sure the event is well-executed from start to finish. Whether setting up or breaking down the materials, transporting supplies, taking orders, interacting with guests, or anything in between, the Guest Event Expert makes transactions feel like part of the experience.
No matter what position you are in, there are a few things that are critical to success – creating a safe workplace, following company policies and procedures, upholding quality standards, and ensuring your uniform, personal appearance, and communications are professional. Guest Service Experts will be on their feet and moving around (stand, sit, or walk for an extended time) and taking a hands-on approach to work (move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 50 pounds without assistance). Doing all these things well (and other reasonable job duties as requested) is critical for Guest Event Experts – to get it right for our guests and our business each and every time.
Preferred Qualifications
Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.
Related Work Experience: Less than 1-year related work experience.
Supervisory Experience: No supervisory experience.
License or Certification: None

brightermonday.title: Head Of Local Social Sector
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

About Inkomoko
Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive.
In 2026, Inkomoko was listed by the Financial Times as the 5th fastest-growing company in Africa, supporting entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa to grow thriving businesses and build inclusive, resilient economies.
Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 100,000 entrepreneurs, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest investor to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa.
Inkomoko has 1000+ staff in 50 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko's 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives.
 INKOMOKO VALUES
All staff at Inkomoko are connected to a shared set of organizational values:

Purpose: be solutions-oriented, produce high-quality work, and be a global leader
Achievement: push yourself to reach beyond what you previously thought possible. 
Improvement: be humble, engage in continuous growth through open & accurate feedback
Bravery: willing to take risks, create a safe space for others, be compassionate, and inclusive
We Eat Goat: we celebrate success and support each other in hard times. We do this work together in the spirit of turikumwe, tuko pamoja, abren nen, Kula na sawa, On est ensemble

Inkomoko is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer. Refugees, women, and persons who reflect the diverse communities we serve are strongly encouraged to apply.
About The Opportunity And Responsibilities
The Head of Local Social Sector is a senior regional leadership role responsible for building and institutionalizing Inkomoko's approach to partnering with, strengthening, and ultimately enabling greater independence of local social sector organizations across our markets.
Local organizations, including refugee-led, community-based, youth-led, women-led, faith-based, and other locally rooted organizations, often possess capabilities, relationships, trust, and contextual knowledge that are essential to sustainable development outcomes. Inkomoko sees an opportunity to build a more intentional institutional pathway through which these organizations can become stronger, more sustainable partners and, where appropriate, increasingly take ownership of functions that complement or extend Inkomoko's work.

brightermonday.title: Senior Business Development Manager
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

(English and French required)

Asopo is the software company that grew out of Bboxx. For ten years the Bboxx group ran its own PAYGO, asset-finance and customer platform in-house, across solar, LPG cooking and electric motorcycles in a dozen African markets. Pulse is that platform, now offered to other companies: distributors, MFIs, banks and OEMs who finance small assets and need to collect on them. We have paying customers in East Africa and the Indian Ocean, a delivery team that

ships integrations with mobile money and core banking systems, and a pipeline that currently outruns the people we have to work it.

That is the job. We need one person to own commercial relationships for Pulse end to end: find the next customers, get them live, keep them, and grow the account.

What you will actually do:

Run the pipeline. Qualify inbound, prospect outbound, and take a deal from first call to signed platform agreement. Most buyers are a head of credit, a head of operations or a founder, so you will be selling to people who will check your numbers.
Closely work and collaborate with Marketing on planning Events, Developing Sales Enablement Assets, Market Positioning, and Campaigns.
Own the accounts you sign. Onboarding, renewals, fee negotiations, the hard conversations when a customer's default rate rises and they want to know what the platform can do about it.
Price the work. Platform fees, per-account fees, implementation fees. You will build the quote, defend it, and know when to walk.
Scope with the delivery team. Sit with our software leads, turn a customer's request into a feature that can be built and priced, and tell the customer honestly what is in the roadmap and what is not.
Work in two languages. A real share of our customers and prospects are in DRC, Madagascar, Togo and francophone West Africa, and one of our largest partners drafts contracts in French. You will negotiate in French, not just say hello in it.

Who this suits:

You are probably in a customer success, account management or sales role at a software company that sells to lenders or distributors in Africa. You may have started in a bank's credit operations or in a PAYGO company's field team before moving to the software side. You have sat in a room with an MFI's credit committee and a distributor's field manager in the same week and were useful in both. You have handled at least one renewal that nearly did not

happen. 

We are less interested in years and titles than in specifics. If you can tell us about a customer you closed, a price you held, and a feature you talked a customer out of, we want to hear it. If you have a non-AI generated vision as to how to grow a business and close prospects, then you tick a lot of the boxes.

The Cold Reality:

The team is small and the product is still being defined. You will not have a sales operations function behind you.
This is a mid-senior band role. Compensation is disclosed on the first call, not at offer stage.
The path to Head of Commercial is written into the offer and tied to revenue. It is real, and it is earned.
We test French. One of your interviews will be conducted entirely in French by a native speaker.

How to apply:

Send a short note, half in English and half in French, covering one account you grew and one you lost and why. Attach your CV. No cover letter template, please; we can tell. Reports to the Managing Director. Start date as soon as possible; we will work around notice

brightermonday.title: Senior Business Development Manager
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

(English and French required)

Asopo is the software company that grew out of Bboxx. For ten years the Bboxx group ran its own PAYGO, asset-finance and customer platform in-house, across solar, LPG cooking and electric motorcycles in a dozen African markets. Pulse is that platform, now offered to other companies: distributors, MFIs, banks and OEMs who finance small assets and need to collect on them. We have paying customers in East Africa and the Indian Ocean, a delivery team that

ships integrations with mobile money and core banking systems, and a pipeline that currently outruns the people we have to work it.

That is the job. We need one person to own commercial relationships for Pulse end to end: find the next customers, get them live, keep them, and grow the account.

What you will actually do:

Run the pipeline. Qualify inbound, prospect outbound, and take a deal from first call to signed platform agreement. Most buyers are a head of credit, a head of operations or a founder, so you will be selling to people who will check your numbers.
Closely work and collaborate with Marketing on planning Events, Developing Sales Enablement Assets, Market Positioning, and Campaigns.
Own the accounts you sign. Onboarding, renewals, fee negotiations, the hard conversations when a customer's default rate rises and they want to know what the platform can do about it.
Price the work. Platform fees, per-account fees, implementation fees. You will build the quote, defend it, and know when to walk.
Scope with the delivery team. Sit with our software leads, turn a customer's request into a feature that can be built and priced, and tell the customer honestly what is in the roadmap and what is not.
Work in two languages. A real share of our customers and prospects are in DRC, Madagascar, Togo and francophone West Africa, and one of our largest partners drafts contracts in French. You will negotiate in French, not just say hello in it.

Who this suits:

You are probably in a customer success, account management or sales role at a software company that sells to lenders or distributors in Africa. You may have started in a bank's credit operations or in a PAYGO company's field team before moving to the software side. You have sat in a room with an MFI's credit committee and a distributor's field manager in the same week and were useful in both. You have handled at least one renewal that nearly did not

happen. 

We are less interested in years and titles than in specifics. If you can tell us about a customer you closed, a price you held, and a feature you talked a customer out of, we want to hear it. If you have a non-AI generated vision as to how to grow a business and close prospects, then you tick a lot of the boxes.

The Cold Reality:

The team is small and the product is still being defined. You will not have a sales operations function behind you.
This is a mid-senior band role. Compensation is disclosed on the first call, not at offer stage.
The path to Head of Commercial is written into the offer and tied to revenue. It is real, and it is earned.
We test French. One of your interviews will be conducted entirely in French by a native speaker.

How to apply:

Send a short note, half in English and half in French, covering one account you grew and one you lost and why. Attach your CV. No cover letter template, please; we can tell. Reports to the Managing Director. Start date as soon as possible; we will work around notice

brightermonday.title: Senior Agronomist
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

Job Description
Job title: SENIOR AGRONOMIST
Location: Kigali, Rwanda
Job reference #: 31306
Contract type: Fixed-term contract
Language requirements: Proficient in English. Knowledge of Kinyarwanda and/or French is a plus.
At Eni, we are looking for a Senior Agronomist within Eni Natural Energies S.p.A. in Kigali, Rwanda.
About Eni Natural Energies SpA – Rwanda Branch
Eni Natural Energies SpA (ENE) is an integrated energy company with headquarters in Milan, Italy. Its subsidiary, Eni Natural Energies SpA - Rwanda Branch (ENE Rwanda), operates in Rwanda on two main streams of activities: Agri-Business and Carbon Offset.
Regarding the Agri-Business, with its seeds multiplication project, ENE Rwanda multiplies seeds of oil crops for export to other ENE geographies in collaboration with the National Industrial Research and Development Agency (NIRDA) and Rwandan operating companies. The overall objectives are to increase the quantity and quality of the produced seeds, share ENE's knowledge on oil crops built over previous years and in different African countries, and apply the latest technologies to this agricultural sector. So far, more than 135 tons of castor seeds have been produced and processed in the country over three planting seasons (from September 2023 until March 2025), and the fourth season is starting with a significant scale-up in terms of involved area and investments.
The ENE Rwanda Clean Cooking Program is the main company Carbon Offset activity currently ongoing in the country, supporting corporate decarbonization targets. The program aims to distribute up to 500,000 improved cookstoves (ICS) across the country, mainly locally manufactured, to provide direct positive benefits to the involved communities—especially regarding health, reducing pressures on Rwandan forests, enhancing local manufacturing, and creating job opportunities. As of now, more than 10,000 ICS have been distributed in Nyagatare District with the Rwandan NGO Rwanda Women’s Network (RWN), and a new project will kick off before the end of the year.
Main Responsibilities

Seed production and management, including seed quality management.
Selecting suitable crop varieties based on climate and soil conditions.
Soil management: assessing soil quality and recommending appropriate land preparation techniques.
Monitoring crop performance and identifying potential risks.
Implementing sustainable farming techniques, such as crop rotation and integrated pest management.
Research and innovation: conducting field trials and experiments to improve oil crop yields.
Training and capacity building: providing technical training to farmers, field officers and project staff regarding oil crops and good agricultural practices.
Project implementation and monitoring: supervising field operations to ensure compliance with project goals.
Sustainability and compliance: ensuring that farming practices align with environmental and regulatory standards.
Stakeholder engagement: collaborating with local operating companies and government agencies; coordinating with relevant authorities for agriculture, import-export of seeds, and seed certification/quality assurance, as well as research institutions and agricultural organizations.

Skills And Experience Required

Master's degree in Agricultural Sciences, with a preference for specializations in Tropical Agronomy, Environment and Bioenergy. Qualifications other than those indicated may also be evaluated based on significant experience relevant to the role.
Extensive experience in agro-industrial supply chains or farm management, preferably aimed at the energy sectors. Previous experience in Africa or the bioenergy sector is considered a plus.
Knowledge of aggregation systems in agriculture with small and large-scale farmers, supply chain management, preparation and organization of sowing campaigns and post-harvest activities.
Knowledge of cultivation systems to produce oil crops for bio feedstock, with reference to rotation crops and crops suitable for cultivation in degraded areas not suited to food production.
Knowledge of seed production and management, including seed quality management.
Knowledge of agricultural regulations and, if possible, reference to renewable energy from biomass, biofuels, certifications and general environmental and social sustainability criteria.
Ability to work in a team and coordinate other people.
Willingness to travel in or out of the country for field missions.
Ability to relate to public entities.
Proficient in English. Knowledge of Kinyarwanda and/or French is a plus.
Knowledge of agricultural digital solutions, tracking and mapping systems (GIS, Google Earth, etc.) is a plus.
Experience in agricultural research trials.
Consolidated experience in managing all Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) aspects associated with core agricultural activities under own supervision.

How To Apply

Applications are only accepted through our online application system.
Please upload your CV in English.

About Eni
Eni is a global energy company operating in 61 Countries, with over 30,000 employees. Originally an oil & gas company, it has evolved into an integrated energy company, playing a key role in ensuring energy security and leading the energy transition. Eni's goal is to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 through the decarbonization of its processes and of the products it sells to its customers. In line with this goal, Eni invests in the research and development of technologies that can accelerate the transition to increasingly sustainable energy. Renewable energy sources, bio-refining, carbon capture and storage are only some examples of Eni's areas of activity and research. In addition, the company is exploring game-changing technologies such as fusion energy – a technology based on the physical processes that power stars and that could generate safe, virtually limitless energy with zero emissions.
Working at Eni
At Eni we believe in enterprising people, capable of making a difference and making their contribution with passion and innovation, to respond to the global challenges of the energy transition. For us, the skills and attitudes of each individual , continuous training , and diversity and inclusion are fundamental. We promote flexible ways of working with particular attention to well-being, welfare and work life-balance.
Eni will evaluate applications considering plurality and diversity as sources of enrichment. If your application is assessed to be among those most in line with the required profile, you will be contacted to continue the selection process.
Whatever your ambition, at Eni you can find the tools to make it happen.
Energy for action takers

How To Apply

Applications are only accepted through our online application system.
Please upload your CV in English.

About Eni
Eni is a global energy company operating in 61 Countries, with over 30,000 employees. Originally an oil & gas company, it has evolved into an integrated energy company, playing a key role in ensuring energy security and leading the energy transition. Eni's goal is to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 through the decarbonization of its processes and of the products it sells to its customers. In line with this goal, Eni invests in the research and development of technologies that can accelerate the transition to increasingly sustainable energy. Renewable energy sources, bio-refining, carbon capture and storage are only some examples of Eni's areas of activity and research. In addition, the company is exploring game-changing technologies such as fusion energy – a technology based on the physical processes that power stars and that could generate safe, virtually limitless energy with zero emissions.
Working at Eni
At Eni we believe in enterprising people, capable of making a difference and making their contribution with passion and innovation, to respond to the global challenges of the energy transition. For us, the skills and attitudes of each individual , continuous training , and diversity and inclusion are fundamental. We promote flexible ways of working with particular attention to well-being, welfare and work life-balance.
Eni will evaluate applications considering plurality and diversity as sources of enrichment. If your application is assessed to be among those most in line with the required profile, you will be contacted to continue the selection process.
Whatever your ambition, at Eni you can find the tools to make it happen.

brightermonday.title: Rwanda Seed Quality Control Coordinator
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

 About One Acre Fund
Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.
Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.
About the Role
Seeking an agriculture professional with 1–2 years of Hybrid Maize seed industry experience and a Bachelor's in Agriculture to serve as Seed Quality Control Coordinator. You will oversee quality, SOPs, and compliance for our 4,000 MT processing plant.
Responsibilities
Seed Quality Assurance & SOP Compliance
Oversee comprehensive quality assurance, SOP implementation, and regulatory compliance across every stage of the 4,000 MT seed processing plant to meet partner, client, and regulatory standards.
Processing Plant Operations & Technical Guidance
Partner closely with the Processing Coordinator to provide technical guidance, conduct continuous quality inspections, and balance operational efficiency with production targets.
People & Team Management
Lead and manage plant quality staff and casual workers, driving capacity building and training to ensure strict adherence to SOPs and quality standards.
Stakeholder Management & System Improvement
Act as the primary liaison between internal processing teams, external clients, and regulatory bodies while continuously strengthening quality control systems across the seed value chain.
Career Growth and Development
We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.
Qualifications
Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:
1–2 years of experience in the hybrid maize seed industry, seed quality control, or plant operations.
Bachelor's degree in Agriculture
Proven expertise in seed quality assurance, SOP development, and regulatory compliance
Demonstrated technical understanding of 4,000 MT processing plant operations and quality risk mitigation.
Strong leadership and people management skills with experience training diverse plant staff and casual workers
Preferred Start Date
As soon as possible
Job Location
Eastern Province, Gatsibo District, Kabarore, Rwanda
Benefits
Health insurance, paid time off 
Eligibility
This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.
Application Deadline
16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.
One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.
Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.
We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

 Apply

About the Role
Seeking a driver to transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between OAF sites, maintain the fleet and cargo in excellent condition, and provide insights on truck operations and charging to inform future electric truck ownership.
Responsibilities
Cargo Transport
Transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between assigned OAF sites, ensuring delivery strictly to the specified locations within set timelines.
Collaborate with the warehouse team to load, offload, and reload trucks, verifying that the physical cargo matches the exact quantity and quality stated on delivery documents.
Secure all materials in transit using appropriate equipment to prevent loss, theft, tampering, or damage (e.g., perforations, wet bags, or torn stitching).
Proactively gather information regarding the location and accessibility of field sites and chargers within the assigned district prior to departure.
Vehicle Maintenance
Conduct weekly vehicle checks, perform minor repairs, and submit maintenance requests to your manager to ensure that the vehicle under their care is kept in good running condition at all times.
Mitigate damage to the truck by avoiding risky routes or driving techniques.
Ensure safety and custody of the vehicles including tools.
Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, registration, first aid kit, and necessary spare parts in the assigned vehicle.
Ensure that, in the event of an accident involving the vehicle, the necessary steps required by rules and regulations are followed.
Documentation & Communication
Accurately manage all delivery documents, including Delivery Notes, Load Cards, and Truck Management Sheets (TMS). Return fully signed delivery documents to your manager within one (1) business day of delivery. 
Obtain official signatures from authorized OAF representatives at both the originating and destination sites to confirm the exact weight/number of inputs dispatched and received.
Immediately notify your manager via text (or call for urgent cases) in the event of accidents, field staff unavailability, data discrepancies, charging problems, mechanical problems, adverse weather, route accessibility issues, data discrepancies, or if any party refuses to sign the delivery documents.
Communicate regularly relevant trial information, such as GPS coordinates, KM range, battery levels, charging experience, driving experience, road quality, etc.
Ensure that all required driving training is successfully completed and certifications are kept up to date
Career Growth and Development
We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. Valid category C driver’s licence
Experience driving cargo trucks on dirt roads outside of Kigali
Working knowledge of local roads and routes, ability to utilize maps / GPS systems
Working knowledge of electric vehicle mechanics (truck maintenance, interpret truck KM range / battery life)
Sound knowledge of road safety regulations
Effective communication skills (verbal and written) in Kinyarwanda
Punctual and reliable, customer service

Seeking a driver to transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between OAF sites, maintain the fleet and cargo in excellent condition, and provide insights on truck operations and charging to inform future electric truck ownership.
Responsibilities
Cargo Transport
Transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between assigned OAF sites, ensuring delivery strictly to the specified locations within set timelines.
Collaborate with the warehouse team to load, offload, and reload trucks, verifying that the physical cargo matches the exact quantity and quality stated on delivery documents.
Secure all materials in transit using appropriate equipment to prevent loss, theft, tampering, or damage (e.g., perforations, wet bags, or torn stitching).
Proactively gather information regarding the location and accessibility of field sites and chargers within the assigned district prior to departure.
Vehicle Maintenance
Conduct weekly vehicle checks, perform minor repairs, and submit maintenance requests to your manager to ensure that the vehicle under their care is kept in good running condition at all times.
Mitigate damage to the truck by avoiding risky routes or driving techniques.
Ensure safety and custody of the vehicles including tools.
Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, registration, first aid kit, and necessary spare parts in the assigned vehicle.
Ensure that, in the event of an accident involving the vehicle, the necessary steps required by rules and regulations are followed.
Documentation & Communication
Accurately manage all delivery documents, including Delivery Notes, Load Cards, and Truck Management Sheets (TMS). Return fully signed delivery documents to your manager within one (1) business day of delivery. 
Obtain official signatures from authorized OAF representatives at both the originating and destination sites to confirm the exact weight/number of inputs dispatched and received.
Immediately notify your manager via text (or call for urgent cases) in the event of accidents, field staff unavailability, data discrepancies, charging problems, mechanical problems, adverse weather, route accessibility issues, data discrepancies, or if any party refuses to sign the delivery documents.
Communicate regularly relevant trial information, such as GPS coordinates, KM range, battery levels, charging experience, driving experience, road quality, etc.
Ensure that all required driving training is successfully completed and certifications are kept up to date
Career Growth and Development
We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:
Valid category C driver’s licence
Experience driving cargo trucks on dirt roads outside of Kigali
Working knowledge of local roads and routes, ability to utilize maps / GPS systems
Working knowledge of electric vehicle mechanics (truck maintenance, interpret truck KM range / battery life)
Sound knowledge of road safety regulations
Effective communication skills (verbal and written) in Kinyarwanda
Punctual and reliable, customer service

As soon as possible
Job Location
Kigali, Rwanda
Benefits
Health insurance, paid time off 
Contract Duration
3 months
Eligibility
This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

23 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. brightermonday.title: Head Of Customer Experience
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

Company Description EVPulsar is developing the charging infrastructure needed to support the electrification of transport, starting in East Africa. The company focuses on building accessible, reliable charging facilities that enable EV users to travel smoothly and confidently. EVPulsar aims to remove barriers to electric mobility by ensuring convenient access to charging in key urban and transit hubs. Team members contribute directly to sustainable transport solutions and the growth of EV ecosystems across the region.
Role Description The Head of Customer Experience is a full-time, on-site role based in Kigali City, Rwanda. This position is responsible for designing and leading the overall customer experience strategy across EVPulsar’s charging network. Day-to-day tasks include mapping customer journeys, defining service standards, and coordinating with operations, product, and support teams to ensure a consistent, positive experience for EV users. The role involves monitoring customer feedback, overseeing resolution of service issues, and implementing initiatives to increase satisfaction and loyalty. The Head of Customer Experience will also establish performance metrics, lead a customer-facing team, and drive continuous improvement in processes, communication, and service delivery.
Qualifications

Strong capabilities in Customer Experience Management and Customer Experience strategy, with a track record of designing and improving end-to-end journeys.
Demonstrated focus on Customer Satisfaction, including setting and monitoring satisfaction targets and implementing initiatives to enhance loyalty.
Proficiency in Customer Service leadership, including managing frontline teams, establishing service standards, and handling escalations.
Solid Analytical Skills to interpret customer data, feedback, and usage patterns, and translate insights into practical actions.
Experience in building and scaling customer-centric processes in fast-growing or startup environments, ideally within mobility, energy, or technology sectors.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams.
Proven people management experience, including coaching, performance management, and creating an inclusive, high-performing team culture.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management, Marketing, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree is an advantage.
Comfort working on-site in Kigali City and engaging directly with customers, partners, and local communities.
Commitment to sustainability, innovation, and accessible mobility solutions in emerging markets.

brightermonday.title: Technical Advisor, Sexual, Reproductive, Maternal And Newborn Health (srmnh)
brightermonday.description:
Job descriptions & requirements

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work http//www.clintonhealthaccess.org
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.
Program Overview
The Government of Rwanda has demonstrated strong leadership and commitment to improving maternal and newborn survival through the Fifth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP V) 2024-2029. The strategy sets ambitious targets to reduce the maternal mortality ratio from 105 to 60 per 100,000 live births, the neonatal mortality rate from 20 to 15 per 1,000 live births by 2029, the unmet need for family planning from 14% to 8%, and the prevalence of stunting among children under five from 33% to 15% prioritizing quality of care, system performance, and sustainability.
Supporting the national goals, CHAI is partnering with the Ministry of Health (MoH) to strengthen the foundations required for impact at scale. CHAI’s assistance spans access to SRMNH commodities, institutional strengthening, digital and data system enhancement, and workforce capacity development, through government structures.
CHAI will provide technical assistance to the MoH, particularly the Clinical and Public Health Services Department. This support is organized around four complementary areas of work improving the quality and reliability of care in health facilities; strengthening data and digital systems to enable real-time performance management and evidence-based decisions; advancing workforce capability through institutionalized professional development and mentorship; and reinforcing coordination, governance, and implementation learning to ensure alignment, accountability, and scalability. The Technical advisor will be expected to bring a systems-thinking lens to all four pillars, ensuring synergy across workstreams and coherence with Rwanda's Quality of Care (QoC) agenda and the WHO Quality, Equity, Dignity Network standards
Position Overview
CHAI is seeking a Technical Advisor to be seconded to MoH in the office of the Head of Clinical and Public Health Services Department. The Technical Advisor will provide support for strategic and operational leadership to the Clinical and Public Health Services Department driving systemic improvements in Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) outcomes across the continuum of care.
In this role, the Technical Advisor will lead the translation of national RMNCAH strategy into scalable, durable system improvements — designing frameworks, engaging stakeholders, and ensuring that performance management routines are strengthened for long-term sustainability. The Technical Advisor will draw on deep expertise and strategic acuity to navigate complex institutional environments. The technical Advisor will be expected to engage with high-level policy processes including HSSP V annual reviews, national quality of care summits, and inter ministerial coordination forums on RMNCAH financing and accountability.
Working at the intersection of national policy and frontline delivery, the Technical Advisor will lead a portfolio of cross-cutting interventions and engage with various stakeholders in RMNCAH forums. The Technical Advisor will report to the Director General of Health Quality Services with streamlined reporting to the CHAI Associate Program Director — Women & Children’s Health, and NCDs. The Technical advisor is expected to function with a high degree of autonomy, demonstrating the judgment to represent the MoH's maternal unit at strategic forums and providing technical recommendations backed by evidence.
 Strategic Leadership and Program Direction

Drive the design, refinement, and execution of RMNCAH program strategy at a senior technical level, ensuring coherence with HSSP V goals and the national policy agenda.
Support the development of multi-year operational frameworks with clear accountability structures, milestone tracking, and adaptive management mechanisms.
Proactively identify strategic risks and systemic bottlenecks; develop and present solutions to Clinical and Public Health Services Department leadership.
Provide technical support to Clinical Service Department in designing, implementing, and scaling facility-led quality improvement (QI) initiatives with demonstrable impact on RMNCAH outcomes.
Anchor QI frameworks to internationally recognized standards (e.g., WHO Standards for Improving Quality of Maternal and Newborn Care in Health Facilities) and ensure alignment with national quality assessment tools.
Provide support for strategic oversight of RMNCAH commodity supply chain management, ensuring alignment across health facilities, MoH, RBC, and RMS, and procurement partners.
Lead the development of a maternal and newborn health Quality of Care (QoC) policy brief, translating facility level performance data into actionable policy recommendations for MoH leadership.
Provide high level technical input into the revision and adaptation of national RMNCAH clinical protocols, guidelines, and standards of care, in collaboration with MoH technical working groups.

 Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning, and Knowledge Management

Support the design and institutionalization of MEL frameworks that build lasting MCCH capacity in data governance, analysis, and use for performance management.
Support the optimization and continuous improvement of national data systems (HMIS, eLMIS, e-Buzima, mentorship reporting) as infrastructure for evidence-based governance.
Support complex, multi-source analyses of RMNCAH indicators, translating findings into strategic recommendations for senior government and donor audiences. This includes the ability to disaggregate equity indicators by district, wealth quintile, and facility type, identifying patterns that require targeted policy responses.
Support the use of quarterly hospital performance data to inform systemic corrective action planning and institutional learning cycles.
Produce high-quality project reports, evaluation contributions, learning briefs, and technical publications for national dissemination.
Champion the use of real-time data dashboards and digital health tools (e.g., e-Buzima,) at the District Health Management Team level to ensure data-driven performance review cycles are embedded, not episodic.

 Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as a senior operational and strategic liaison between RBC/MOH, District Health Officers, health facility leaders and development partners.
Build and sustain high trust relationships with stakeholders, advising on policy alignment, program design, and scale up decisions.
Lead strategic coordination and monitor RMNCAH partner interventions and the implementation of RMNCH grants at all levels." This includes actively contributing to the national RMNCAH Technical Working Group, ensuring donor and partner interventions are coherent with MoH strategy and not fragmented.
Participate in high-level joint supervision visits, technical working groups, and national RMNCAH forums.
Perform other strategic duties assigned by the Clinical and Public Health Services Department leadership or CHAI Manager to advance RMNCAH strategic objectives and ensure successful service delivery.
Clinical background with a master's degree in public health or health related field; advanced specialization in RMNCAH or health systems strengthening preferred.
Minimum 5 years of progressively senior experience in a results-driven, complex program environment. At least 3 of these years must be in a role with demonstrated policy advisory or norm-setting responsibilities at the national or sub-regional level, not solely program management or direct service delivery.
Demonstrated track record of translating national health strategies into measurable system-level improvements, with evidence of sustainable institutional impact.
Exceptional ability to build and sustain senior-level relationships with government, health facilities, and donor stakeholders in complex environments.
Advanced analytical capability — able to synthesize multi-source data, identify strategic patterns, and communicate findings compellingly to technical and non-technical audiences. Demonstrated ability to conduct or commission health systems analyses at national scale, including experience with cost-effectiveness, equity, and quality of care frameworks as analytical lenses.
Proven experience leading and mentoring teams toward ambitious deliverables in fast-paced, resource constrained settings.
Expert level proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; familiarity with data visualization tools and digital health platforms is a strong asset. Proficiency in at least one statistical or data analysis tool (Stata, R, or equivalent) is strongly preferred. 
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to senior government officials and partners. Demonstrated ability to author policy briefs, technical guidance documents, or peer reviewed contributions that have been formally adopted or cited by health system decision makers.
Strong strategic judgment, and ability to navigate ambiguity with confidence and resilience.

Advantages

Significant experience embedded within or providing technical assistance to Ministries of Health in sub-Saharan Africa, with deep familiarity with health system governance structures.
Extensive knowledge of global health frameworks, including health systems strengthening, UHC, and RMNCAH quality of care agendas. Specific familiarity with MPDSR (Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response) methodology is strongly advantageous.
Prior engagement with the Rwanda Ministry of Health or in a low- or middle-income country.

Job descriptions & requirements

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work http//www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. ndangira.title_raw: Driver  at Water Access Rwanda: (Deadline 2 Oct 2026)
ndangira.description:
About the Role

The Company Driver moves WAR staff, partners and equipment safely and on time between our Kigali office, our project sites and government and partner offices. The role sits in the Finance & Logistics team. A driver at WAR is a trusted ambassador of the company on the road and a first-line guardian of our vehicles.

Key Result Areas
Safe and on-time transport of staff, partners and cargo to all designated destinations.
Day-to-day vehicle care — cleanliness and basic maintenance of the assigned company vehicle.
Accurate trip logging — fuel reporting and adherence to WAR's vehicle policies.
Professional representation — courteous conduct with passengers and the public.
Full compliance with the Rwandan highway code and all WAR safety and integrity policies.

Detailed Responsibilities
Drive WAR staff and authorised passengers within Kigali and to project sites in Bugesera, Eastern Province and Western Province.
Conduct daily pre-trip vehicle checks (fluids, tyres, lights, fuel) and report defects immediately.
Carry out basic vehicle troubleshooting and arrange professional repairs through the Direct Supervisor.
Maintain accurate trip logs, fuel records and mileage reports; submit weekly to Finance & Logistics.
Plan routes ahead of time; anticipate traffic, road and weather conditions to ensure punctuality.
Keep the vehicle clean inside and outside at all times; safeguard tools, equipment and documents on board.
Observe the Rwandan highway code at all times; respect WAR speed limits, seat-belt and no-phone-while-driving rules.
Support light loading and unloading of equipment when collecting parts or delivering materials.
Be on call for early-morning, evening or weekend trips when the schedule requires.

Strictly observe WAR's anti-corruption policy — accepting or offering any bribe is grounds for immediate termination.

Qualifications & Profile

?? Education: High school diploma or equivalent certificate (A2, TVET or recognised vocational driving school).
License: Valid Rwandan driving license covering at least two of the following categories: B, C, D or F.
Experience: 3+ years professional driving experience preferred — applications with less are still considered if other qualifications are strong.
Mechanical Knowledge: Basic vehicle mechanics — able to diagnose simple faults and perform routine maintenance.
Languages: Fluent Kinyarwanda; English is a strong advantage.
Clean driving record — we will request and verify.

Skills & Values Fit
Trustworthiness — reliable, honest, discreet with confidential passenger information.
Accountability — owns mistakes, reports issues early, never hides incidents.
Punctuality — non-negotiable; excellent time management.
Multitasking - comfortable juggling shifting schedules, last-minute changes and competing requests.

Compensation

Base Salary: RWF 165,340 / month gross

Transport Allowance: RWF 83,900 / month gross

Retention Pay: RWF 35,000 / month gross

Net Take-Home (probation, first 3 months): RWF 187,000 / month

Net Take-Home (post-probation): RWF 221,000 / month

Annual Review: 5-7% Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA)

Benefits: Statutory per WAR HR Manual and Rwandan labour law (RSSB, public holidays, leave)

How to Apply

Send the following to: hr@wateraccess.rw

Subject: Application: Company Driver — (Your Full Name)
Your CV with at least two contactable references
A short cover letter (max one page) covering: (1) which driving license categories you hold and since when, (2) the most challenging trip you have ever completed and how you handled it, and (3) why you want to drive for Water Access Rwanda specifically

Note: Shortlisted candidates will be invited for a practical driving test, a Kinyarwanda highway-code interview, and our standard bribe-test screening before any offer is made.
