As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

The Project Manager plays a critical role in overseeing the successful implementation of multiple projects within a district, ensuring alignment with RTV’s strategic goals, project designs, and work plans. This role involves providing strong leadership, mentorship, and operational support to Team Leads and Officers, ensuring they have the necessary resources, guidance, and capacity to execute projects effectively.
In addition to people and team management, the Project Manager is responsible for office administration and operations, fostering an environment where teams are fully supported to meet program objectives. They serve as the key liaison between staff, government counterparts and management, proactively addressing challenges, streamlining processes, and ensuring smooth communication and workflow across all levels.
The ideal candidate is a results-oriented leader with strong experience in coaching and managing teams, mobilizing and coordinating with government institutions, and delivering complex, multi-sector projects in rural contexts. They are solutions-driven, highly organized, and committed to building high-performing teams that deliver sustainable, government-aligned impact for communities served by RTV. Note: The Project Manager may be based at a District Government Office and embedded with government teams to foster collaboration and strengthen partnerships.

Role and ResponsibilitiesProject Management

Reports to the Area Manager, providing key updates and where needed arises escalates issues to the Area Manager for Support or decision guidance.

Coordinates weekly plans of activities and key deliverables to Team Leads every Friday for the coming week

Debrief with Team Leads and Officers on project progress in the communities (covering deliverables, key issues and risks, key activities in villages)

Identify key issues and risks for projects during project reporting.

Oversee the timely and effective execution of day-to-day activity, work plans, and project life cycles, starting from project identification to implementation to post-implementation and evaluation to ensure that organizational objectives are achieved.

Ensure strong collaboration with all departments to optimize project performance

Strategic growth and resource planning, recruitment, supervision, and training and development of program staff

On-the-ground sourcing and procurement of trainers and supplies, with cost and delivery evaluations

Strategic planning and execution of strategic initiatives to further RTV’s mission and program strategy

Create a detailed work plan that identifies and sequences the activities in different communities

Review project schedules with Team Leads and other staff to ensure community problems and issues are solved.

Monitor the progress of community activities and adjust as necessary to ensure the successful completion of planned activities;

Government Coordination, Capacity Building & Partnership Management

Lead district- and sector-level coordination with government counterparts (e.g., District Directors, Sector Executive Secretaries, Sector Agronomists, BDEOs) to ensure collaborative implementation of RTV projects in line with district priorities & targets, as well as national strategies.

Serve as the primary RTV focal point for government engagement at district and sector levels, maintaining strong, professional, and collaborative partnerships.

Plan, coordinate, and oversee trainings for government staff on RTV methodologies, implementation standards, roles, and accountability frameworks.

Coach and mentor sector- and district-level government staff to strengthen joint planning, supervision, reporting, and implementation quality.

Support government counterparts in supervision and monitoring of RTV-supported activities, including joint field visits, household coaching sessions, and structured problem-solving.

Collect, validate, and consolidate activity and progress reports from government counterparts and ensure timely integration into RTV reporting systems.

Promote a strong partnership culture between RTV staff and government officials to enable smooth, effective, and sustainable project implementation at scale.

Methodology

Provide contributions and feedback to project designs and methodologies;

Support implementation and transition activities;

Supervision

Coordinate contacts and planning of initial project visits and prepare budgets;

Conduct the initial project visits for prospective visitors and resolve any challenges pertaining to visit

Monitor performance of program staff and provide continuous coaching and corrective feedback

Maintain strong working relationship within and among the programs, planning and evaluation, M&E, and operations teams

Ensure staff receive proper orientation and training;

Administration and logistical support

Oversee store management and ensure effective utilization of all input management tools such as the Goods Received Note, Stock Request Form and Goods Returned Form.

Conduct on-going interviews of leadership and community on performance, participation, and perceptions

Manage and report on office budgets and expenditures

Track and review on-going financial reports and progress

Complete weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual reports and provide them to relevant management staff

Complete necessary reporting for local government district office

Oversee on-going growth and development programming

Support in the recruitment of new staff

Prepare office accountability and ensure bi-weekly submission to the Finance Officer

Qualifications, Education and Job Requirements

University Degree in Project Management, Social Work and Social Administration, Project planning and Development, Community Development, or related fields

Masters or Post Graduate Diploma in Project planning and Management will be an added advantage.

Minimum of four (5) years of working experience.

Demonstrated experience (at least 3 years) working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at District and Sector levels (mandatory)

At least 3 years at a supervisory level.

Experience in project design, budgeting and project management and implementation at village levels

Personal and Skills Development

Develop skills and attend training in RTV’s focus areas, including but not limited to: health, agriculture, income-generation, WASH, VSLAs, Market Linkages/Collective Marketing, etc.

Provide input in skills development of team members under your management

Conduct mid-term and final performance evaluations for team leads

Preferred Experience and Skills

Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English & Kinyarwanda

Strong Computer Skills with good knowledge of Microsoft Suite;

Excellent organizational and leadership skills with keen attention to details;

Accurately completes multiple tasks while taking into consideration special assignments, frequent interruptions, available resources and multiple reporting relationships

Strong training & facilitation skills

Strong interpersonal skills

Reliable, with high integrity and strong work ethic

Able to work as part of a team and create a sense of cohesion within teams;

Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment;

Energetic and physically able to hike high terrain;

Able to travel 80% of time

Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory)

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace. Disclaimer: Raising the Village DOES NOT charge any kind of FEE(s) at whichever stage of the recruitment process.

ndangira.description:
Conservation Agriculture (Fixed-term) at One Acre Fund : (Deadline 03-12-2026)

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.

Responsibilities

Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.

Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.

Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.

Rwanda Contracts Procurement Coordinator at One Acre Fund: (Deadline 1-10-2026)

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund supplies over 1.5 million smallholder farmers with the agricultural services they need to make their farms more productive. Our 8,000+ team is drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. With operations across ten African countries, we make farmers more prosperous by providing easy access to quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, and agricultural training to improve harvests. On average, the farmers we serve earn 40 percent more profits from their land when they enroll with One Acre Fund. To learn more about our work, look at our Why Work Here blog for more information.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007, is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

About the Role

Seeking an exceptional procurement and contracts professional with 2+ years of experience to increase our impact on farmers by driving cost savings and coordinating contracting activities for the procurement department. 

Responsibilities

Tender Management

Lead end-to-end tendering and contract execution for high-value goods and services by collaborating on departmental procurement plans.

Establish 0-6 month strategic targets and set price baselines to negotiate maximum cost savings.

Continually optimise sourcing processes for higher operational efficiency.

Contract Planning & Management

Analyse annual spend across key categories to establish a quarterly-reviewed tender calendar.

Conduct market research to boost competition and contract effectiveness.

Oversee full contract lifecycles and Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) by tracking price tolerances and managing change control systems.

Analyse market risks and report overall cost savings.

Supplier & Stakeholder Management

Conduct bi-annual vendor evaluations and monthly meetings with top suppliers to create performance improvement plans and enforce contractual commitments.

Act as the key liaison between external suppliers and One Acre Fund while directly supporting internal team procurement needs.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

2–3 years of relevant experience in contract management, procurement sourcing, and end-to-end tendering operations.

Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Law, Business Administration, or a related field.

Proven ability to manage supplier performance, negotiate agreements to maximise cost savings, and enforce contractual commitments.

Proactive problem solver skilled in data analysis, spend tracking, and sourcing process optimisation.

Strong relationship management skills with both internal stakeholders and external suppliers.

Eligibility
This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

Job Location
Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits
Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

Contract Duration
Permanent

Preferred Start Date
As soon as possible

1 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed continuously until a hire is made.

Impact Division Chief of Staff at One Acre Fund: (Deadline 1-12-2026)

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

About the Role

We are looking for an exceptional strategist and communicator to improve coordination between all of the Impact Division's workstreams. You will support the CIO in advancing One Acre Fund's Global Impact Strategy.

Responsibilities

The Impact Division supports all One Acre Fund programs to generate more impact, wherever we work. We help the organization keep three core aspects of impact at the forefront of our work: 

Improving farmer livelihoods in the short-term

Ensuring long-term viability through sustainable agricultural practices (soil health, crop diversity, etc.)

Addressing non-agricultural needs of farming households (energy, nutrition, etc.)

The role of the Impact Chief of Staff is to support the Chief Impact Officer (CIO) in advancing our organization’s Impact Strategy. Three critical components of this role are to:

Improve coordination of many different actors to implement our Impact Strategy.

Increase the reach and effectiveness of Impact Division leadership.

Lead strategic research, communications, or operational initiatives.

Specific responsibilities include:

Improving Impact Division communication & coordination around achieving goals

Goal setting and tracking. Lead the annual development of OKRs aligned to organizational impact strategy; monitor progress against the strategic plan, OKRs, and other organizational indicators.

Coordination across the Impact Division. Ensure fluid collaboration between technical support teams and operational teams through clear work planning and frequent, transparent communication.

Increasing the reach of Impact leadership

Conduct regular prioritization reviews with division leadership to ensure we’re tackling the most important problems.

Serve as the Chief Impact Officer’s “whip” by moving complex projects forward.

Represent the Division externally by pursuing early stage opportunities with partners.

Take on direct or indirect management responsibilities from division leadership, as appropriate.

Leading strategic Initiatives

Lead strategic research or operational initiatives that: 

Are highly important to One Acre Fund and organizational leadership 

Sit outside the day-to-day purview of the current team

Specific projects will depend on the candidate's background and interests, organizational priorities, bandwidth of implicated teams, and timing. Examples could include:

Impact-focused internal campaigns

Researching a new technology or partnership

Lead the drafting and delivery of Finance Division communications, including decision announcements, priority rollouts, and key organisational cycles.

Maintain the Division's communications calendar and coordinate inputs, timelines, follow-ups, and actions with department leads.

Prepare high-quality presentation decks, briefing notes, data summaries, and other materials for senior leadership.

Translate complex data, analytical findings, and team inputs into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable messages.

Maintain clear trackers and work plans to support effective coordination and execution across the Division.

Own clearly defined projects and workstreams from planning through execution and delivery.

Coordinate selected CFO- and Senior Manager-sponsored initiatives by aligning stakeholders, tracking milestones, and proactively addressing blockers.

Lead or contribute to high-priority cross-functional and ad hoc projects across the Finance Division.

Apply structured problem-solving to ambiguous challenges and develop practical options and recommendations for leadership.

Conduct research, benchmarking, data synthesis, and financial analysis to support strategic decision-making.

Develop structured outputs, including summaries, frameworks, financial models, and scenario analyses.

Provide flexible support across the Finance Division during periods of peak demand, staff transitions, or extended leave.

Take ownership of assigned responsibilities during temporary assignments, ensuring clear communication, continuity, and effective handover.

Support divisional recruitment and other priority initiatives as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.

CPA or ACCA finalist.

About 5 years of working experience in finance, strategy, consulting, project management, or operations, within fast-paced medium- to large organisations.

Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Proactive, detail-oriented, and solutions-focused approach.

Familiarity with financial analysis, management reporting, and business decision-making is preferred.

Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting to changing priorities.

Full professional proficiency in English, with strong written communication skills.

ndangira.description:
Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier at American Embassy Kigali Mission Rwanda : (Deadline 22-09-2026)

Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier

Vacancy Announcement: KIGALI-2026-010

The Embassy of the United States of America in Kigali, Rwanda is recruiting for an Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier.
The position is open to All Interested Candidates/All Sources and available to start immediately.

Duties:

The Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier (APT/Alt Cashier) is a key member of the Accounts Payable Unit (APU) within the Financial Management Center (FMC) at Mission Kigali. The APT/Alt Cashier performs the full range of accounts payable and accounts receivable services for all subscribed ICASS agencies. The position also serves as a financial advisor to the Accounts Payable Manager (APM), ensuring timely and accurate processing of payments and receivables.

In the capacity of Alternate Cashier, the incumbent serves as the Embassy’s Principal Class B Cashier and accountable officer, responsible for managing cashier operations within an authorized advance. This includes oversight of cash on hand, transactions in transit, replenishments, and funds deposited in local checking accounts. ndangira.description:
RwandAir Ltd Vacancy: Head of Organization Design & Total Rewards – Deadline 11 September 2026

RwandAir Ltd, the flag carrier airline of Rwanda, is expanding its operations as it works toward 4-Star status and stronger regional hub leadership.

The airline is inviting applications from highly qualified and experienced professionals for the following position:

Job Title: Head of Organization Design & Total Rewards

Department: HR & Administration
Reports to: Chief HR & Administration Officer
Location: Kigali International Airport, Rwanda
Experience Required: 10–12 years

Job Purpose

The Head of Organization Design & Total Rewards will lead the development of RwandAir's organization design, job architecture, workforce planning, compensation and benefits frameworks.

This is a strategic build role, responsible for developing and embedding systems covering an estimated workforce of 1,200–1,500 employees, including headquarters, outstations, flight crew, cabin crew, engineering and ground operations.

The successful candidate will help establish how work is organised across RwandAir and how roles are evaluated, graded, compensated and rewarded.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1. Organization Design & Job Architecture

Develop and maintain RwandAir's organisation design standards, including spans, layers and decision rights.

Lead structural reviews across Commercial, Flight Operations, Ground Operations, Engineering, Cargo, Cabin Services and Corporate functions.

Design and implement an enterprise-wide job architecture covering job families, career levels and role profiles.

Establish workforce planning methodologies and productivity ratios.

Translate fleet and network plans into a credible three-year workforce and cost plan.

2. Total Rewards & Compensation

Develop RwandAir's Total Rewards philosophy, including market positioning, pay mix and differentiation.

Present the Total Rewards strategy for Executive Committee and Board approval.

Lead job evaluation using recognised methodologies such as Korn Ferry Hay, Mercer IPE or WTW GGS.

Chair the technical job evaluation panel.

Develop and maintain salary structures and annual pay review processes.

Conduct market benchmarking against regional and global airlines.

Develop compensation rules for flight crew and technical employees, including flight/duty pay, allowances and licence pay.

Oversee employee benefits such as medical insurance, pension, staff travel and housing.

3. Governance & Leadership

Lead the employment cost strategy and localisation/expatriate rewards framework.

Advise the Chief HR & Administration Officer and CFO on employment cost and organisational structure decisions.

Ensure structural changes maintain RCAA and IOSA postholder requirements and regulatory accountability.

Build and lead a technically strong Organization Design & Rewards team.

Develop and transfer technical capabilities to Rwandan HR professionals.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants should have:

A Bachelor's Degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Economics, Statistics, Industrial/Organisational Psychology or a related field.

10–12 years of progressive HR experience.

At least 5–6 years of specialist experience in reward, job architecture or organisation design.

Preferred Qualifications

The following are strongly preferred:

A Master's degree, such as MBA, MSc in HR Management or MSc in Organisational Psychology.

Accreditation in a recognised job evaluation methodology, including Korn Ferry Hay, Mercer IPE or WTW GGS.

Essential Experience

Candidates should demonstrate:

Experience leading at least one enterprise-wide job evaluation and grading implementation in an organisation with 1,000+ employees.

Experience in aviation or another regulated, multi-site and safety-critical industry. Aviation experience is strongly preferred.

Experience designing compensation for mixed workforce populations, including licensed/technical, operational shift, unionised, expatriate and local employees.

Experience presenting pay and organisational structure decisions at Board or Executive Committee level.

Other Desired Competencies & Skills

Previous Experience

Proven ability to move an organisation from having no formal framework to a governed and effective framework.

Strong ability to manage and communicate organisational change.

Confidence to challenge senior leaders when proposed structures or grades are not supportable.

Strong understanding of employment costs and their impact on business performance and the P&L.

Ability to handle executive compensation, restructuring and confidential employee information with a high level of discretion.

Job-Specific Skills

Strong knowledge of organisation design methodologies, including Galbraith Star Model, Kates Kesler and Ulrich value-chain logic.

Advanced job evaluation and grading expertise.

Strong compensation and benefits design capabilities.

Experience in salary structure development, market pricing, incentive design and benefits economics.

Advanced workforce analytics and cost modelling skills.

Working knowledge of aviation operations, including ICAO, IOSA, RCAA postholder structures, FTL, crew productivity, CASK and ASK.

Working knowledge of Rwandan Labour Law No. 66/2018.

Proficiency in HRIS/ERP systems, position management, organisation modelling and compensation modules.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit:

Application letter addressed to the Chief HR & Administration Officer.

Recent Curriculum Vitae.

Copies of notarized Degree/Diploma certificates.

Relevant professional certificates.

Copies of academic papers.

Photocopy of Passport or National ID.

Three referees.

How to Apply

Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications through the RwandAir e-Recruitment portal.

Application Deadline: 11 September 2026

Application Documents: PDF format only.

Important

This is a senior-level HR leadership position requiring substantial experience in organisation design, job evaluation, compensation and total rewards. Candidates should carefully review the minimum experience and specialist requirements before applying.

ndangira.title_raw: Senior Program Manager, Cervical Cancer  at CHAI - The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.: (Deadline 24 Aug 2027)
ndangira.company: The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc
ndangira.company_name: The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc
ndangira.description:
Senior Program Manager, Cervical Cancer  at CHAI - The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.: (Deadline 24 Aug 2027)

Job Description

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Program Overview

More than 300,000 women die of cervical cancer each year, despite the availability of proven prevention interventions that can dramatically reduce the burden of disease. Over 90% of these deaths occur among women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to high-quality prevention services has historically been limited. In 2018, the WHO issued a Global Call to Action Towards Cervical Cancer Elimination, and in 2020, the Member States of the World Health Assembly adopted a Cervical Cancer Elimination Strategy, setting targets to reach 70% screening coverage and 90% treatment coverage of screen-positive women by 2030.

CHAI’s cervical cancer program works to reduce cervical cancer incidence in LMICs by expanding access to secondary prevention services, thereby preventing mortality and morbidity while lowering cancer treatment costs for health systems. The program complements CHAI’s HPV vaccines work, which supports LMICs to introduce and routinize HPV vaccination for adolescent girls (primary prevention).

The program’s approach rests on three interconnected areas of work: (1) supporting Ministries of Health to introduce optimal tools, integrate services into routine healthcare, update policy, build workforce capacity, and strengthen health systems for scale-up; (2) market shaping to improve the access and affordability of existing and new technologies for screening and precancer treatment; (3) advancing innovation, including AI-based screening, to enable same-day screening and treatment.

The program has supported over 12 countries since 2019 to scale screening and treatment services, reaching more than 1.4 million women, while working to ensure high linkage to treatment and referral, improving the affordability and access of critical tools, and advancing the development of AI-assisted tools for screening. CHAI is now supporting governments to build nationally owned costed elimination plans, identifying sustainability pathways, and bringing low-cost AI-assisted screening tools to market.

Position Overview

The Senior Program Manager (SPM) holds day-to-day operational and technical leadership across country support, costing and financing, and diagnostics strategy and execution. The SPM guides associates, senior associates on the team, quality-assures outputs before Director reviews, and represents the program in technical coordination with CHAI's global diagnostics team and other teams across the matrix. The role combines people management, technical review, and direct workstream ownership, and acts as the critical link between country-facing staff and Director-level strategy and donor engagement.

The SPM works closely with the program’s country teams and CHAI’s global diagnostics, markets, health financing, AIR/research, and HPV vaccines teams.

The role manages some senior relationships, including at Unitaid, WHO, and other major donors, and is recognized as a subject-matter expert in cervical cancer prevention.

The base location is flexible with a preference for the role to be based in a program country, pending country leadership approval. An estimated 20% of international travel time is expected.

Responsibilities

Country support and cross-country learning

Guide associates and senior associates on the team in responding to country requests across relevant functional areas, including elimination plans, work plans, technical reports, and case studies.

Review and quality-assure country support outputs produced by associates and senior associates before Director review, including elimination plans, technical reports, donor reports, learning agenda pieces, memos, decks, case studies etc. Provide structured, actionable technical feedback to strengthen outputs.

Serve as the first point of escalation for country teams before issues reach the Director; quickly identify critical problems, break down and prioritize different parts of complex challenges, and apply lessons and best practices to redirect activities effectively.

Monitor the volume and pattern of country support requests and propose the team structure best suited to manage demand, whether organized around dedicated country assignments or around functional specialization.

Costing and financing workstream leadership

Provide technical and managerial oversight on the costing workstream, including on methodology, data quality, and consistency of costing outputs across programme countries. Guide the Associate serving as the costing focal point to deliver high-quality analyses aligned with the programme's broader elimination planning and financing strategy. (This workstream is expected to conclude within the next 6-9 months.)

Take on ownership of the cervical cancer financing workstream, with guidance from CHAI's global health financing team. Support countries to identify sustainable financing pathways for scale-up, conduct financing analyses, translate costing outputs into formats suitable for donor reporting and national planning, and develop a toolkit of financing approaches that can be adapted across settings.

Maximize the use of data to identify problems in financing and costing approaches, monitor progress, and develop effective, evidence-based solutions; apply lessons and best practices from across the program to inform or redirect activities.

Lead on creation of the learning agenda pieces for the costing and financing workstreams. Lead the development of cross-country learning products, work closely with the Senior Associate to track progress on other learning agenda commitments, provide technical reviews, and coordinate the dissemination and socialization of outputs with the communications team.

Diagnostics strategy and AI-assisted screening

Refine the program's diagnostics strategy, aligning country needs with global market-shaping priorities for screening and precancer treatment technologies, including new technologies entering the market — AI-assisted screening tools and near point of care HPV tests.

Work closely with the Global Diagnostics Team to ensure country-level and supplier-facing inputs are reflected in the program’s diagnostic strategy; apply knowledge across disciplines to inform approaches that bridge product, policy, and country adoption.

Flag country-level constraints or opportunities that should inform diagnostic tool selection, procurement pathways, or rollout sequencing.

Support country teams in scoping and planning for the deployment of AI-assisted screening tools. This would involve working closely with Global Markets team, global project manager for AI-assisted screening tools and the country teams to develop detailed, sequenced work plans that lay the operational groundwork for in-country introduction of such tools, covering regulatory approval pathways, digital health integration requirements, procurement and supply chain considerations, and service delivery readiness. Engage relevant CHAI teams with prior experience rolling out new health technologies to incorporate lessons learned into planning.

Resource mobilization and fundraising

Lead on the development of proposals for multi-country and country-level funding opportunities, coordinating input from cross-functional and cross-country teams.

Program reporting and financial management

Work with the senior associate and finance manager to prepare and finalise the periodic program and financial reports to key donors.

Work with the finance manager to develop annual budget revisions for donors, as well as forecasts and re-forecasts for the program; understand and flag the implications of over-spend or under-spend, and track obligations, commitments, and expenditure of funds in detail.

People management

Directly manage and mentor a small team of associates and senior associates, ensuring appropriate workload distribution, training, and performance feedback; bring individuals together to function as a cohesive and productive unit; provide guidance to other managers on staffing decisions and development plans where relevant.

Coach and support the professional development of associates and senior associates on the team, providing structured feedback and contributing to succession planning.

Lead cross-functional coordination across CHAI’s matrix, including with Global Diagnostics Team, Analytics and Implementation Research, Global Markets Team, health financing, and HPV vaccination teams.

Program strategy

Direct the team in shaping materials and key messages for senior stakeholders; support development and tailoring of program presentations at global and country level, translating technical content into accessible formats suited to relevant audiences for fundraising, internal and external strategy discussions, and dissemination of program learnings.

Support refinement of CHAI’s screening and treatment program strategy and CHAI’s integrated cervical elimination strategy; advise senior management on program objectives and strategy to achieve results.

Contribute to ideation and design of data visualizations and technical presentation of program data.

Evaluate the program’s current network of partners and technical advisors for relevance and effectiveness; identify and initiate new connections with senior external stakeholders that facilitate achievement of strategic goals, including collaborating with senior-level technical staff external to CHAI.

Additional responsibilities

Represent CHAI in WHO’s cervical cancer Guidelines Development Group, compile relevant updates from CHAI country global teams to feed into the GDG meetings, and report back progress and updates from GDG to program senior management.

Take initiative to address emerging priorities and respond to evolving program needs.

Undertake additional tasks as requested by the line manager to advance program objectives.

Qualifications

We seek an experienced and highly motivated program manager who is passionate about eliminating cervical cancer. An ideal candidate will be described as:

Strong strategic and analytical thinker: You understand the big picture and can translate complex challenges into clear, actionable workplans. You are comfortable working with large amounts of quantitative and qualitative data and can extract logical conclusions and recommendations to guide program direction.

Effective project and people management skills: You are adept at managing complex, multi-workstream initiatives from design to completion with clarity and accountability. You can guide and develop junior team members, foster collaboration across a matrixed organization, and ensure high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.

Entrepreneurial mindset: You are resourceful, proactive, and driven to find solutions, with a strong bias for action and a track record of delivering results in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.

Excellent interpersonal and relationship management skills: You have strong written and oral communication skills and can work effectively with a wide array of internal and external partners. You can respectfully and effectively navigate varied and sensitive stakeholder environments, including in-country teams and senior leaders.

Senior Program Manager, Cervical Cancer  at CHAI - The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.: (Deadline 24 Aug 2027)

Job Description

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Program Overview

More than 300,000 women die of cervical cancer each year, despite the availability of proven prevention interventions that can dramatically reduce the burden of disease. Over 90% of these deaths occur among women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to high-quality prevention services has historically been limited. In 2018, the WHO issued a Global Call to Action Towards Cervical Cancer Elimination, and in 2020, the Member States of the World Health Assembly adopted a Cervical Cancer Elimination Strategy, setting targets to reach 70% screening coverage and 90% treatment coverage of screen-positive women by 2030.

CHAI’s cervical cancer program works to reduce cervical cancer incidence in LMICs by expanding access to secondary prevention services, thereby preventing mortality and morbidity while lowering cancer treatment costs for health systems. The program complements CHAI’s HPV vaccines work, which supports LMICs to introduce and routinize HPV vaccination for adolescent girls (primary prevention).

The program’s approach rests on three interconnected areas of work: (1) supporting Ministries of Health to introduce optimal tools, integrate services into routine healthcare, update policy, build workforce capacity, and strengthen health systems for scale-up; (2) market shaping to improve the access and affordability of existing and new technologies for screening and precancer treatment; (3) advancing innovation, including AI-based screening, to enable same-day screening and treatment.

The program has supported over 12 countries since 2019 to scale screening and treatment services, reaching more than 1.4 million women, while working to ensure high linkage to treatment and referral, improving the affordability and access of critical tools, and advancing the development of AI-assisted tools for screening. CHAI is now supporting governments to build nationally owned costed elimination plans, identifying sustainability pathways, and bringing low-cost AI-assisted screening tools to market.

Position Overview

The Senior Program Manager (SPM) holds day-to-day operational and technical leadership across country support, costing and financing, and diagnostics strategy and execution. The SPM guides associates, senior associates on the team, quality-assures outputs before Director reviews, and represents the program in technical coordination with CHAI's global diagnostics team and other teams across the matrix. The role combines people management, technical review, and direct workstream ownership, and acts as the critical link between country-facing staff and Director-level strategy and donor engagement.

The SPM works closely with the program’s country teams and CHAI’s global diagnostics, markets, health financing, AIR/research, and HPV vaccines teams.

 

The role manages some senior relationships, including at Unitaid, WHO, and other major donors, and is recognized as a subject-matter expert in cervical cancer prevention.

The base location is flexible with a preference for the role to be based in a program country, pending country leadership approval. An estimated 20% of international travel time is expected.

Responsibilities

Country support and cross-country learning

  • Guide associates and senior associates on the team in responding to country requests across relevant functional areas, including elimination plans, work plans, technical reports, and case studies.
  • Review and quality-assure country support outputs produced by associates and senior associates before Director review, including elimination plans, technical reports, donor reports, learning agenda pieces, memos, decks, case studies etc. Provide structured, actionable technical feedback to strengthen outputs.
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for country teams before issues reach the Director; quickly identify critical problems, break down and prioritize different parts of complex challenges, and apply lessons and best practices to redirect activities effectively.
  • Monitor the volume and pattern of country support requests and propose the team structure best suited to manage demand, whether organized around dedicated country assignments or around functional specialization.

Costing and financing workstream leadership

  • Provide technical and managerial oversight on the costing workstream, including on methodology, data quality, and consistency of costing outputs across programme countries. Guide the Associate serving as the costing focal point to deliver high-quality analyses aligned with the programme's broader elimination planning and financing strategy. (This workstream is expected to conclude within the next 6-9 months.)
  • Take on ownership of the cervical cancer financing workstream, with guidance from CHAI's global health financing team. Support countries to identify sustainable financing pathways for scale-up, conduct financing analyses, translate costing outputs into formats suitable for donor reporting and national planning, and develop a toolkit of financing approaches that can be adapted across settings.
  • Maximize the use of data to identify problems in financing and costing approaches, monitor progress, and develop effective, evidence-based solutions; apply lessons and best practices from across the program to inform or redirect activities.
  • Lead on creation of the learning agenda pieces for the costing and financing workstreams. Lead the development of cross-country learning products, work closely with the Senior Associate to track progress on other learning agenda commitments, provide technical reviews, and coordinate the dissemination and socialization of outputs with the communications team.
 

Diagnostics strategy and AI-assisted screening

  • Refine the program's diagnostics strategy, aligning country needs with global market-shaping priorities for screening and precancer treatment technologies, including new technologies entering the market — AI-assisted screening tools and near point of care HPV tests.
  • Work closely with the Global Diagnostics Team to ensure country-level and supplier-facing inputs are reflected in the program’s diagnostic strategy; apply knowledge across disciplines to inform approaches that bridge product, policy, and country adoption.
  • Flag country-level constraints or opportunities that should inform diagnostic tool selection, procurement pathways, or rollout sequencing.
  • Support country teams in scoping and planning for the deployment of AI-assisted screening tools. This would involve working closely with Global Markets team, global project manager for AI-assisted screening tools and the country teams to develop detailed, sequenced work plans that lay the operational groundwork for in-country introduction of such tools, covering regulatory approval pathways, digital health integration requirements, procurement and supply chain considerations, and service delivery readiness. Engage relevant CHAI teams with prior experience rolling out new health technologies to incorporate lessons learned into planning.

Resource mobilization and fundraising

  • Lead on the development of proposals for multi-country and country-level funding opportunities, coordinating input from cross-functional and cross-country teams.

Program reporting and financial management

  • Work with the senior associate and finance manager to prepare and finalise the periodic program and financial reports to key donors.
  • Work with the finance manager to develop annual budget revisions for donors, as well as forecasts and re-forecasts for the program; understand and flag the implications of over-spend or under-spend, and track obligations, commitments, and expenditure of funds in detail.

People management

  • Directly manage and mentor a small team of associates and senior associates, ensuring appropriate workload distribution, training, and performance feedback; bring individuals together to function as a cohesive and productive unit; provide guidance to other managers on staffing decisions and development plans where relevant.
  • Coach and support the professional development of associates and senior associates on the team, providing structured feedback and contributing to succession planning.
  • Lead cross-functional coordination across CHAI’s matrix, including with Global Diagnostics Team, Analytics and Implementation Research, Global Markets Team, health financing, and HPV vaccination teams.

Program strategy

  • Direct the team in shaping materials and key messages for senior stakeholders; support development and tailoring of program presentations at global and country level, translating technical content into accessible formats suited to relevant audiences for fundraising, internal and external strategy discussions, and dissemination of program learnings.
  • Support refinement of CHAI’s screening and treatment program strategy and CHAI’s integrated cervical elimination strategy; advise senior management on program objectives and strategy to achieve results.
  • Contribute to ideation and design of data visualizations and technical presentation of program data.
  • Evaluate the program’s current network of partners and technical advisors for relevance and effectiveness; identify and initiate new connections with senior external stakeholders that facilitate achievement of strategic goals, including collaborating with senior-level technical staff external to CHAI.

Additional responsibilities

  • Represent CHAI in WHO’s cervical cancer Guidelines Development Group, compile relevant updates from CHAI country global teams to feed into the GDG meetings, and report back progress and updates from GDG to program senior management.
  • Take initiative to address emerging priorities and respond to evolving program needs.
  • Undertake additional tasks as requested by the line manager to advance program objectives.

Qualifications

We seek an experienced and highly motivated program manager who is passionate about eliminating cervical cancer. An ideal candidate will be described as:

  • Strong strategic and analytical thinker: You understand the big picture and can translate complex challenges into clear, actionable workplans. You are comfortable working with large amounts of quantitative and qualitative data and can extract logical conclusions and recommendations to guide program direction.
  • Effective project and people management skills: You are adept at managing complex, multi-workstream initiatives from design to completion with clarity and accountability. You can guide and develop junior team members, foster collaboration across a matrixed organization, and ensure high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset: You are resourceful, proactive, and driven to find solutions, with a strong bias for action and a track record of delivering results in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship management skills: You have strong written and oral communication skills and can work effectively with a wide array of internal and external partners. You can respectfully and effectively navigate varied and sensitive stakeholder environments, including in-country teams and senior leaders.
  • Fundraising and resource mobilization experience: You are comfortable contributing to proposals and concept notes, coordinating input across teams, and supporting efforts to mobilize resources for program expansion.
  • Results driven: You remain engaged and motivated until a task is successfully completed, and you hold yourself and others accountable for delivering high-quality work

Experience:

  • Demonstrated experience leading global or multi-country teams and managing complex, high-value grant portfolios.
  • Proven track record in country programs, product access, or health financing within LMIC contexts.
  • Recognized expertise in the program’s technical area.
  • Excellent relationship management skills, including experience navigating senior, political, and multilateral stakeholder relationships.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience with creating and delivering high-quality presentations/ decks, with the ability to represent CHAI at high levels externally.

ndangira.title_raw: Rwanda Contracts Coordinator at One Acre Fund: (Deadline 14-11-2026)
ndangira.description:
Rwanda Contracts Coordinator at One Acre Fund: (Deadline 14-11-2026)

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

About the Role

Seeking an exceptional procurement and contracts professional with 2+ years of experience to increase our impact on farmers by driving cost-saving and coordinating contracting activities for the procurement department.

Responsibilities

Tender Management

Lead end-to-end tendering and contract execution for high-value goods and services by collaborating on departmental procurement plans, establishing 0–6 month strategic targets, setting price baselines to negotiate maximum cost savings, and continually optimizing sourcing processes for higher efficiency.

Contract Planning

Analyze annual spend across key categories to establish a quarterly-reviewed tender calendar while conducting market research to boost competition and contract effectiveness.

Contract Management

Oversee full contract lifecycles and LTAs by tracking price tolerances, managing change control systems, analyzing market risks, and reporting cost savings.

Supplier Performance Management

Conduct bi-annual vendor evaluations and monthly meetings with top suppliers to create performance improvement plans and enforce contractual commitments.

Stakeholder management

Act as the key liaison between external suppliers and One Acre Fund while directly supporting internal team procurement needs.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Contract management & procurement sourcing experience 

Data analysis & cost optimization 

Stakeholder & vendor management 

Degree in Procurement/Supply Chain or Law

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off 

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

Application Deadline

14 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Responsibilities

Lead National Performance Trial Design & Execution

Design and implement high-quality National Performance Trials (NPTs), ensuring scientifically robust experimental designs and field protocols.

Oversee trial implementation from planting through harvest, working closely with field teams to ensure accurate data collection and adherence to research standards.

Maintain compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), institutional guidelines, and international research best practices.

Deliver Advanced Data Analysis & Research Insights

Develop standardized data collection tools and quality assurance protocols for research teams.

Analyze complex trial data using statistical software to generate reliable insights and recommendations.

Create clear data visualizations, dashboards, and technical outputs that support evidence-based decision-making.

Build Research Capacity & Technical Expertise

Deliver training on experimental design, data management, and statistical analysis within the Seed Technology & Business (STB) Program.

Mentor trainees and provide technical guidance on research proposals, trial design, and data interpretation.

Promote best practices in agricultural research and strengthen the technical capacity of field and research teams.

Communicate Research Findings & Support Innovation

Prepare high-quality technical reports, presentations, and research briefs for internal and external stakeholders.

Translate scientific findings into practical recommendations for seed production, variety evaluation, and industry partners.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve research tools, data systems, and operational processes.

Drive Continuous Improvement in Research Quality

Identify opportunities to strengthen trial methodologies, data quality, and analytical approaches.

Support the adoption of digital tools and innovative solutions that improve research efficiency and decision-making.

Contribute to advancing national seed research and variety evaluation through continuous learning and scientific excellence.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Bachelor's or advanced degree in Agriculture, Plant Science, Statistics, Biometry, Agronomy, Seed Science, or a related field.

At least 2 years of experience in agricultural research, trial management, or applied statistical analysis.

Experience with agricultural research reporting and data analysis is a strong advantage.

Advanced analytical skills with experience using statistical software such as R, Genstat, SAS, STATA, or similar.

Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple research activities simultaneously.

Strong understanding of experimental design, quantitative and qualitative research methods, and data quality assurance.

Fluency in Kinyarwanda and English.

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

About the Role

You will own the way the Product team works, including discovering and driving efficiencies through AI adoption, administering the product toolkit, process design and adoption, and use of data. If our ways of working aren't maximizing Product value add, it is up to you to fix it.

Responsibilities

Tooling & Infrastructure Administration (40%)

Stack Ownership: Act as the primary administrator for the Product Department’s software stack (e.g., Dragonboat, Figma, Matomo, Notion). Manage configurations, user permissions, licenses, and vendor relationships.

AI Adoption: Drive smart adoption of AI tools/agents to improve Product’s confidence in the value add of new features and to automate workflows.

Workflow Configuration: Build and maintain standardized approaches to roadmaps, workflows, and automations to ensure all Domain teams (Field, HQ, CorpTech) operate with consistent visibility.

Troubleshooting: Serve as the first line of support for PMs facing technical blockers with internal tools.

Data Governance & SROI Tracking (30%)

Troubleshooting: Serve as the first line of support for PMs facing technical blockers with internal tools.

Impact measurement: Work with PMs to refine their product metrics to ensure they’re strategically aligned, automated, and accurate.

Data Integrity: Audit analytics tools (e.g., Matomo) to ensure new features are launched with correct event tracking. Flag data quality issues to Engineering.

Reporting: Own comprehensive reporting, surfacing critical insights on Product impact (e.g., BVMs) and processes (e.g., Roadmap Hygiene) to track progress against targets.

Process Enablement & Logistics (30%)

KPI Tracking: Assist the Dir. of Product with capturing and sharing Product team KPIs, working with Product Managers to ensure accuracy and help drive overall team performance towards targets

Onboarding: Lead the technical onboarding for new Product hires, ensuring they are trained on our specific templates, tool stack, and "Way of Working."

Knowledge Management: Maintain the department's internal documentation library (Wiki/Drive) to ensure the "Standard" defined by the Principal is accessible and up-to-date.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Soft Skills

Service Mindset: Finds satisfaction in "unblocking" others and building the stage for other PMs to shine.

Hyper-Organized: Loves checklists, documentation, and bringing order to chaos.

Influence without Authority: Can drive adoption and compliance with Senior PMs without being their direct manager.

Hard Skills

Tool Administration: Advanced proficiency in configuring PDLC tools (Dragonboat) and documentation platforms (Notion/Confluence).

Data Fluency: Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills (Pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, cross-sheet formulas) for SROI modeling. Familiarity with web analytics (Matomo/GA).

Knowledge

Product Lifecycle: Understanding of how software is built (Agile/Scrum basics) to effectively support the PM workflow.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Nairobi, Kenya or Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Contract Duration

2 Years

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya, Rwanda, Burundi, Malawi, Zambia, Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Uganda Ethiopia and Nigeria.

Application Deadline

03 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

About the Role

By 2030, our organisation will serve 10 million farm families annually. This growth will be fuelled by fundraising, and at One Acre Fund, our fundraising relies on industry-leading grant and partnership management. We have a 10-person grant management team within our larger Business Development department, responsible for stewarding our highest-value donor partnerships, and are now looking for new Strategic Partnerships Senior Associates / Managers to join this team.

These roles will manage some of our highest-value donor partnerships, leading the coordination and monitoring of grant-funded activities. All roles will report to leaders within our Global Business Development team, while closely coordinating with leaders for the relevant programs. All roles will also interact closely across 1AF’s programming, building deep fluency with our approach to smallholder agriculture: equipping farmers with high-quality products/services to increase their harvests and profits, build their climate resilience, and improve their long-term livelihoods.

Specific roles will have major emphasis areas based on the nature of each donor partnership, helping the organisation pioneer new approaches to thematic priorities including conservation agriculture, engaging women and youth farmers, and smallholder insurance.

Responsibilities

Drive thematic partnerships happening in the field: You will bring an ambitious vision of smallholder prosperity to life in new thematic areas for the organisation, helping us build the capacity to deliver impact to smallholders through conservation agriculture, women/youth engagement, and/or smallholder insurance:

Project Management and Coordination: Partner with program teams to set goals, design and run project activities, anticipate challenges, and keep every part of the plan moving forward smoothly.

Collaborative Problem Solving: Work closely with program staff to tackle day-to-day and long-term challenges, bringing real-world insights directly to org leadership and the donor.

Program Fluency: Spend dedicated time in the field with farmers and staff to fully understand work and ensure that all we do in the partnership remains tailored to what farmers really need.

Own, manage and/or support key donor relationships: You will ensure One Acre Fund builds and maintains an excellent relationship with our partners, translating field impact into clear, compelling narratives and keeping our partners deeply connected to our progress:

Donor Engagement: Act as the main point of contact for all funder communications, seamlessly bridging the gap between donors and field teams in whatever ways are needed, including regular communications, coordinating visits, and more as required.

Storytelling and Reporting: Through deep program fluency, deliver clear, high-quality narrative and financial updates that demonstrate to our partners the true impact of their support.

Grant Administration: Manage the essential day-to-day details of the funding, including accurate data tracking, invoices, and otherwise ensuring all grant operations are running smoothly and on time.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Bachelor's degree in International Development, Public Policy, Business, Economics, or a related field.

5-10 years of professional experience in international development, strategic partnerships, grant management, consulting, or project management, depending on role level.

Experience in a public-facing role and with managing external stakeholders, preferred.

Strong writing and communication skills.

Excellent organisational skills with a willingness to take initiative and be proactive.

Proven negotiation and problem-solving skills.

Comfortable with data and working in Google Sheets, preferred.

Fluency in English required.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda, Nairobi, Kenya or the United States (Must be on the East Coast, with a strong preference for New York City).

After you apply, we will notify you which opening/s you are being considered for based on your experience and existing work eligibility for each location as follows:

Kigali, Rwanda: One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

Nairobi, Kenya: Open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

US: Open to citizens or permanent residents of the U.S.

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

Contract Duration

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

Travel Requirement

At least two weeks per year. Candidates based in the US should expect to spend four weeks visiting our programs in their first year, with a minimum of two weeks annual travel expected thereafter.

Eligibility

This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, or Burundi are strongly preferred.

Application Deadline

23 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

Bachelor's degree in Seed science, Agriculture, Agroforestry, and related fields

ndangira.description:
50 Internship Program Opportunities at African Union (AU): Deadline 31 December 2026

About the African Union

The African Union (AU) is a Pan-African organization established to promote unity, integration, peace, and sustainable development across Africa. Headquartered in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the AU works closely with its member states to advance economic growth, good governance, education, infrastructure, health, and regional cooperation.

Internship Program Overview

The African Union Commission invites qualified citizens of AU Member States to apply for its Internship Program. This program offers young graduates and final-year students an opportunity to gain practical experience, strengthen professional skills, and learn about the operations of one of Africa’s leading institutions.

The internship is a full-time learning opportunity designed to provide exposure to various AU departments while helping participants build leadership and career development skills.

Areas of Placement

Interns may be assigned to various AU departments and offices, including:

Agriculture and Rural Development

Education, Science and Innovation

Infrastructure and Energy

Political Affairs, Peace and Security

Health and Social Development

Human Resources Management

Information and Communication

Finance and Administration

Women, Gender and Youth

Legal Affairs

Strategic Planning

NEPAD

Protocol and Partnerships

Information Systems and Technology

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must:

Be citizens of an African Union Member State.

Be in the final year of a Bachelor's Degree program, OR

Hold a Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree in a relevant field.

Be fluent in at least one AU working language (English, French, Arabic, or Portuguese).

Be 32 years old or younger at the time of selection.

Demonstrate integrity, professionalism, and good conduct.

Have no serious criminal record.

No prior work experience is required.

Required Skills

Candidates should have:

Computer skills in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

Good communication and interpersonal skills.

Ability to work in multicultural environments.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Knowledge of email and internet applications.

Internship Duration

The internship is offered for three (3) months and may be renewed once depending on performance and departmental needs.

Important Information

The African Union does not provide salary or stipend for interns.

Travel, accommodation, and living expenses are the responsibility of the intern.

Interns must have their own medical insurance coverage during the internship period.

The AU may assist successful candidates in obtaining visas where necessary.

Required Documents

Applicants must submit:

Motivation Letter

Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV)

Copy of Passport or National ID

Academic Certificates

Recommendation Letter from their Institution

Any other supporting documents requested during application

Application Deadline

Deadline: 31 December 2026

Interested candidates should submit their applications online through the African Union recruitment portal before the deadline.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE AND APPLY
