ndangira.title: Professional Internships Program in Rwanda at  Rwanda Development Board
ndangira.title_raw: Professional Internships Program in Rwanda at  Rwanda Development Board: (Deadline: 2030-12-31)
ndangira.description:
Professional Internships Program in Rwanda

About the Internship Program

The Professional Internship Program in Rwanda was adopted in 2009 with the aim of equipping fresh graduates with practical skills and professional experience needed to make a successful transition from school to the labour market.

The program is designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical work experience by giving Rwandan graduates an opportunity to apply what they learned in school in a real working environment.

Through the program, interns are placed in public institutions, private companies, and civil society organizations that are related to their fields of study. This enables young graduates to gain valuable professional experience, develop workplace skills, and improve their chances of securing employment.

In general, the internship lasts for six (6) months. However, for technical fields such as agriculture and other areas that require extended practical training, the internship period may be extended to up to twelve (12) months.

Internship Program Objectives
The Internship Program aims to:

Equip interns with practical skills that facilitate the transition from school to the labour market.

Strengthen graduates’ practical capacity by connecting theoretical knowledge gained in school with real-world workplace experience.

Develop professionalism and workplace skills, including communication, interpersonal, teamwork, and organizational skills.

Promote positive work ethics among young graduates while developing effective work competencies and employability skills required in the workforce.

Provide valuable professional experience that improves graduates’ employability and competitiveness in the labour market.

Benefits of the Internship Program

Participating in the Internship Program provides graduates with several important benefits, including:

Practical experience: Interns have the opportunity to put their academic knowledge into practice and learn through hands-on work.

Professional development: The program helps participants develop professionalism, communication, interpersonal, teamwork, and organizational skills.

Industry knowledge: Interns gain practical knowledge and expertise related to the subjects and careers they studied in school.

Smooth transition to employment: The internship helps graduates become familiar with workplace expectations and makes the transition from school to employment easier.

Improved employability: The practical experience gained during the internship can strengthen a graduate’s CV and increase their chances of finding employment.

Eligibility
The Internship Program is open to Rwandan fresh graduates who have completed their studies at:

Higher Learning Institutions (HLIs) in Rwanda or abroad

TVET institutions

IPRCs in Rwanda

Applicants should be graduates who need to strengthen their employability skills, practical knowledge, and professional experience.

Internship Duration

The standard internship period is six (6) months.

For fields that require more extensive practical training, particularly technical fields such as agriculture, the internship period may be extended to up to twelve (12) months, depending on the nature of the program and training requirements.

Application Process

Applications for the Internship Program are completed online.

Eligible applicants can follow these steps:

Step 1: Visit the Internship Portal

Go to the official internship application portal:

internship.rw

Step 2: Click “Apply Now”

Select the Apply Now option to begin your application.

Step 3: Create an Account

If you are applying for the first time, create an account on the platform and provide the required information.

Step 4: Complete Your Application

Fill in the application form carefully and submit the required information and documents.

Applicants who need assistance can also contact the RDB Internship Office or call 1415 for support.

Why Apply for the Internship Program?

The Internship Program provides fresh graduates with an opportunity to move beyond classroom learning and gain practical experience in a professional environment.

For graduates looking to improve their skills, build professional networks, strengthen their CV, and increase their chances of employment, an internship can be an important first step toward building a successful career.

Key Information

Program: Professional Internship Program
Target: Rwandan fresh graduates
Eligible Institutions: HLIs, TVET and IPRCs in Rwanda or abroad
Standard Duration: 6 months
Extended Duration: Up to 12 months for certain technical fields
Application: Online
Support: RDB Internship Office / Call 1415

Application Process

Applications for the Professional Internship Program are submitted online through the official internship portal.

Eligible applicants can follow these steps:

Visit the official internship portal:
https://internship.rw/

Click on “Apply for Internship”.

If you are a first-time applicant, create an account.

Complete your profile and provide the required information.

Submit your internship application through the online system.

Applicants who need assistance can contact the Internship Secretariat through the support channels provided on the official portal.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE

ndangira.title_raw: AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRES N° 09/RIM Plc/2026 – ACHAT DES IMPRIMÉS | DATE LIMITE : 03/10/2026
ndangira.description:
AVIS  D’APPEL  D’OFFRES N° 09 /RIM Plc /2026

ACHAT  DES  IMPRIMES 

1.       RIM  Plc  lance un appel d’offres public pour l’achat des imprimés 

2.       La participation à la concurrence est ouverte à égalité de conditions à toutes les personnes physiques ou sociétés spécialisées dans le domaine. 

3.       Les dossiers d’Appel d’offres rédigés en Français et l’échantillon pour chaque article peuvent être obtenus  au Siège de RIM Plc pendant les jours ouvrables, à partir du 25/09/2026 à 8h00’ sur présentation d’un bordereau de versement d’un montant de Dix mille 10,000 Frw sur le compte no 4075200000808/ RWF ouvert à l’EQUITY BANK   au nom de RIM Ltd.   

4.       La sélection  sera faite par la méthode de QUALITE-COUT (QCBS)  conformément aux procédures décrites dans le présent DAO.

5.       Le fournisseur le mieux offrant fera la livraison des imprimés au RIM Plc sur toute l’année et en respectant les prix de l’offre.

6.Les offres techniques et financières bien dactylographiées en français, convenablement reliées, en deux (2) exemplaires dont un original et une copie doivent parvenir, datées et cachetées sous plis fermés au Siège de RIM Plc au plus tard le  03/10/2026 à 17h00’

          Les offres doivent porter la mention :  

AVIS D’APPEL D’OFFRES N° 09 /RIM PLC/2026 SOUMISSION POUR L’ACHAT DES IMPRIMES A OUVRIR UNIQUEMENT EN SEANCE PUBLIQUE  DU  06/10/2026  A 11H00’   

6.       L’ouverture des offres aura lieu en présence des soumissionnaires ou de leurs représentants souhaitant y assister dans les locaux du RIM Plc, le 06/10/2026 à 11h00’

Fait à Kigali, le 23/09/2026

              GATERA NSANZIMFURA  Damien

              Directeur Général                                                                                   

📄 Download COMMUNIQUE D'APPEL D'OFFRE.

ndangira.title: KAUST Scholarship 2027 in Saudi Arabia Fully Funded Master’s and PhD Opportunity Deadline 27 September 2026
ndangira.title_raw: KAUST Scholarship 2027 in Saudi Arabia Fully Funded Master’s and PhD Opportunity Deadline 27 September 2026
ndangira.description:
KAUST Scholarship 2027 in Saudi Arabia Fully Funded Master’s and PhD Opportunity Deadline 27 September 2026

King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) offers fully funded graduate study opportunities for international students who want to pursue advanced studies and research in science, engineering, technology, and related fields in Saudi Arabia.

The KAUST graduate programmes provide students with access to an international research environment, experienced faculty members, advanced research facilities, and opportunities to participate in cutting-edge research.

For the 2027 academic year, KAUST offers opportunities for qualified international applicants to apply for Master’s, MS/PhD, and PhD programmes, depending on the admission round.

KAUST Scholarship 2027 Quick Facts

University: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

Country: Saudi Arabia

Study Level: Master’s and PhD

Programmes: MS, MS/PhD and PhD

Scholarship Type: Fully Funded

Academic Year: 2027

Application Method: Online

Spring 2027 Deadline: 27 September 2026

Fall 2027 Round 2 Deadline: 3 January 2027

About KAUST

King Abdullah University of Science and Technology is a research-focused university in Saudi Arabia offering graduate education in science, engineering, technology, and related disciplines.

The university provides an international academic environment where graduate students work with faculty members and researchers on advanced scientific and technological research.

KAUST offers graduate programmes leading to Master’s and doctoral degrees, with students having access to modern laboratories, research facilities, and an international research community.

KAUST Scholarship Benefits

KAUST graduate students admitted with the university's fellowship support can receive comprehensive financial assistance.

The support may include:

Full tuition fee support

Monthly stipend

On-campus housing

Medical and dental coverage

Relocation support

Access to advanced research facilities

Research opportunities with KAUST faculty and researchers

The exact terms and conditions of financial support are determined by KAUST and the student's admission and funding arrangements.

Eligibility Requirements

Eligibility requirements depend on the graduate programme selected.

Generally, applicants should meet the following requirements:

Applicants should hold a relevant Bachelor’s degree when applying for a Master’s programme.

Applicants applying for a PhD programme should generally hold a relevant Master’s degree or equivalent qualification.

Applicants must meet the academic requirements of the selected programme.

KAUST states that the minimum acceptable GPA is 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.

However, applicants who are admitted to KAUST typically have stronger academic records than the minimum requirement.

Applicants are generally required to demonstrate English language proficiency through an official TOEFL or IELTS score, unless they qualify for an applicable exemption.

Applicants should also satisfy any additional requirements established by their selected graduate programme.

Available Graduate Programmes

KAUST offers graduate programmes in a wide range of scientific and engineering disciplines.

Applicants can explore programmes related to areas such as:

Engineering

Computer Science

Artificial Intelligence

Environmental Science

Marine Science

Energy

Materials Science

Chemical Science

Physical Science

Biological Science

Applicants should review the current programme list and specific admission requirements before applying.

KAUST Admission Deadlines for 2027

KAUST has different application rounds for Spring and Fall 2027 admission.

Spring 2027 Admission

For Spring 2027 admission, applications are open only to PhD applicants.

Application Deadline: 27 September 2026

Admission Decisions: 8 November 2026

Semester Begins: 17 January 2027

Fall 2027 Admission

For Fall 2027 admission, applications are open to MS, MS/PhD, and PhD applicants.

Round 2 Opens: 28 September 2026

Round 2 Deadline: 3 January 2027

Admission Decisions: 14 February 2027

Fall Semester Begins: 29 August 2027

KAUST notes that admission dates are tentative and may be subject to change. Applicants should therefore check the official admission timeline before submitting their applications.

Application Requirements

Applicants should prepare the required documents before starting the online application.

Depending on the programme, applicants may be required to provide:

Academic transcripts

Degree certificates

Curriculum Vitae

Statement of purpose

Letters of recommendation

English language test results where required

Passport or identification document

Other programme-specific supporting documents

Applicants should carefully review the requirements of their selected graduate programme to ensure that all required documents are included.

How to Apply

Applicants can apply online through the KAUST graduate admission portal.

The application process generally involves the following steps:

Select a suitable KAUST graduate programme.

Review the admission and programme-specific requirements.

Create an account on the KAUST application portal.

Complete the online application form.

Upload all required supporting documents.

Submit the application before the relevant deadline.

Monitor the application portal and email for updates.

After submission, applications are reviewed by the relevant academic and admissions teams. Selected applicants may be invited for an academic interview or additional assessment before a final admission decision is made.

Important Information for Applicants

Applicants should carefully select the admission round that matches their intended programme and start date.

For Spring 2027, only PhD applicants can apply.

For Fall 2027, applicants can apply for MS, MS/PhD, and PhD programmes.

Applicants should also note that meeting the minimum GPA requirement does not guarantee admission. KAUST is a highly competitive research university, and applications are evaluated based on the applicant's academic record, research potential, qualifications, and overall application.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the KAUST Scholarship fully funded?

KAUST graduate students may receive comprehensive financial support that can include tuition, a monthly stipend, housing, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support, subject to the applicable funding arrangements.

Who can apply for KAUST?

International students who meet the academic, English language, and programme-specific admission requirements can apply for eligible KAUST graduate programmes.

Can I apply for a Master’s degree?

Yes. Master’s applicants can apply during the Fall 2027 admission cycle for eligible MS and MS/PhD programmes.

Can I apply for a PhD?

Yes. PhD applicants can apply for both the Spring and Fall 2027 admission cycles, subject to the programme and application round requirements.

What is the minimum GPA?

KAUST states a minimum GPA requirement of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. However, successful applicants generally have stronger academic records.

What is the deadline for Spring 2027?

The Spring 2027 application deadline is 27 September 2026.

What is the deadline for Fall 2027?

The Fall 2027 Round 2 application deadline is 3 January 2027.

Conclusion

The KAUST Scholarship 2027 provides an excellent opportunity for qualified international students seeking fully funded graduate education and advanced research experience in Saudi Arabia.

The university offers Master’s and PhD programmes in science, engineering, technology, and related disciplines within a highly international research environment.

Applicants interested in Spring 2027 PhD admission should submit their applications before 27 September 2026, while applicants targeting Fall 2027 should follow the relevant admission round and deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to prepare their documents early and verify the latest requirements and deadlines on the official KAUST admission website before applying.

Organizational background

Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is a national organization committed to promote the rights, inclusion, education, empowerment and socio-economic well-being of blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda.

The Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is a non-governmental organization that was founded in August 1994 as a National unified voice for persons with visual impairment. After registering with the Rwanda Governance Board under the legal personality number 60/05 on 16/03/1995, and complies with the new law No 058/2024 of 20/06/2024 and related regulations. RUB works towards the improvement of the situation of blind people through education and rehabilitation to facilitate meaningful equality and integration. RUB holds membership in 2 National umbrellas including UPHLS and NUDOR and also affiliated to the African Union of the Blind (AFUB) and the World Blind Union (WBU). The organization has 64 well established branches in all districts of the country and all those branches managed by persons with visual impairment themselves. RUB' activities aim at improving the living conditions of Blind and Partially Sighted (BPS) persons through advocacy, promoting the education of blind and partially sighted persons, capacity development of members and rehabilitation program/service.

1.1. Vision

The vision of RUB is to ‘achieve a situation where people with visual impairment enjoy the same rights as other citizens, receive rehabilitation and education and have equal access to employment’.

1.2. Mission

RUB's mission is to ‘work towards the improvement of the situation of people with visual impairment through rehabilitation and education to facilitate meaningful equality and integration into the society’.

1.3. Objectives

With the purpose of improving the living condition of Blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda, RUB sets the following objectives to guides its strategic implementations:

Bring together persons with visual impairment in a national organization to promote their fundamental rights;

Raise awareness on needs, potentials, and aspirations of persons with visual impairment in Rwanda;

Advocate for access to education and rehabilitation of persons with visual impairment through dialogue with the government and other partners in development;

Seek support to provide adequate and appropriate services to persons with visual impairment;

Promote prevention of visual impairment through dialogue with relevant authorities;

Promote the inclusion of persons with visual impairment in sport and cultural activities.

About project

Under support from the Marga Schulze Foundation through CBM, RUB is implementing a multi-year project 2026-2028 to advance educational inclusion and equitable learning opportunities for blind and partially sighted girls and women in Rwanda.

The project recognizes that girls and women with disabilities experience multiple and intersecting barriers to education. These may include inaccessible learning environments and materials, limited availability of appropriate support, negative social attitudes, inadequate teacher preparation, financial constraints, and limited opportunities for participation in decisions that affect their education and future.

Children with disabilities in Rwanda continue to face significant barriers to accessing, participating in, and completing education. Girls with disabilities may experience additional barriers because of the intersection of disability and gender. These challenges can be particularly pronounced in rural and emergency-affected communities.

The proposed project therefore seeks to move beyond simply increasing access to schools. It aims to support meaningful participation, retention, learning, progression and empowerment, while strengthening schools and communities to become more inclusive of all learners.

A central element of the project will be the development and testing of practical approaches to inclusive education that can generate evidence and learning for wider application in Rwanda.

2.1 Overall Objective

To identify, support and empower girls and boys with disabilities, both in and out of school, particularly in rural and emergency-affected areas of Rwanda, with a specific focus on improving educational opportunities and outcomes for girls and women with visual impairments.

2.2 Specific Objectives

Identify girls and boys with disabilities who are in and out of school across selected rural and emergency-affected contexts in Rwanda and assess their individual and educational support needs.

Provide identified girls and women with visual impairments with appropriate and comprehensive support to enhance their enrolment, participation, retention, learning and progression.

Support selected schools to develop and implement a holistic approach to inclusion that enables all learners, including learners with disabilities, to participate and learn equitably.

Empower women with visual impairments with knowledge, skills and opportunities in human rights, social justice and advocacy, enabling them to contribute to policy, practice and decision-making on disability inclusion and gender equity.

RUB is therefore inviting qualified Rwandans with or without disabilities to apply for this opportunity.

Position Information

3.1 Special needs education coordinator (SNECO)

Position: Special Needs Education Coordinator (SNECO)

Main Purpose of the Position: The Special Needs Education Coordinator will be responsible for coordinating and providing technical expertise for RUB's special and inclusive education interventions.The position will work closely with learners, families, teachers, school administration, local authorities, organizations of persons with disabilities, and other stakeholders to promote inclusive and accessible education for Blind and Partially Sighted learners and other special educational needs.

Key Responsibilities

SNECO will:

Ensure the implementation and coordination of RUB's special and inclusive education programmes.

Improve access to quality and accessible education for blind and partially sighted learners.

Strengthen the capacity of teachers, schools, parents, and other stakeholders to support learners with disabilities.

Promote the use of Braille, assistive technology, accessible learning materials, and inclusive teaching approaches.

Strengthen collaboration between RUB and relevant education stakeholders.

Contribute to evidence-based advocacy and policy engagement on inclusive education.

Monitor and document education programme results, lessons learned, and good practices.

Qualifications

In academic Qualifications, applicants should meet the following requirements:

A Bachelor's degree in Special Needs Education, Inclusive Education, Education, Disability Studies, Educational Psychology, or a related field

Professional Experience

At least three (3) years of relevant professional experience in special needs education, inclusive education, disability programming, or a related area.

Demonstrated experience working with blind and partially sighted learners is highly desirable.

Knowledge of inclusive education policies, approaches, and practices.

Knowledge of Braille, assistive technology, and accessible learning materials is an advantage.

Experience in training, mentoring, programme coordination, monitoring, and reporting

Experience in an NGO, civil society organization, organizations of persons with disabilities

The candidate should demonstrate:

Strong knowledge of special and inclusive education.

Excellent programme coordination and organizational skills.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

Ability to work effectively with persons with disabilities and diverse stakeholders.

Required Skills and Competencies

Good analytical, report-writing, and documentation skills.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Strong computer skills, particularly Microsoft Office applications.

Good advocacy and stakeholder engagement skills.

Commitment to disability rights, equality, inclusion, and safeguarding.

Knowledge of Braille is an added advantage

3.1 finance officer

Position

Finance Officer

Main Purpose of the Position

The Finance Officer will be responsible for supporting the effective management of RUB's financial resources and ensuring that financial transactions, accounting records, budgets, financial reports, and donor funds are properly managed and accounted for.

Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will contribute to strong financial controls, transparency, accountability, and compliance with RUB policies, donor requirements, and applicable laws and regulations in Rwanda.The Finance Officer will:

Maintain accurate and up-to-date accounting records.

Record and process financial transactions in a timely and accurate manner.

Prepare payment vouchers and ensure adequate supporting documentation and authorization.

Maintain cashbooks, ledgers, accounts payable and receivable records.

Conduct regular bank, cash, and ledger reconciliations.

Support the preparation and monitoring of annual and project budgets.

Prepare monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor financial reports.

Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and provide variance analysis.

Maintain accurate financial records for donor-funded projects.

Monitor donor expenditure and compliance with grant agreements.

Support payroll preparation and applicable statutory obligations.

Maintain proper controls over cash, bank accounts, petty cash, and organizational assets.

Support internal and external audits and follow up on audit recommendations.

Ensure compliance with RUB financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.

Identify financial risks and recommend appropriate corrective measures.

Provide financial guidance and support to program and management teams.

Maintain confidential and well-organized financial documentation.

Report suspected fraud, financial irregularities, or misuse of funds through appropriate channels.

Qualifications

In academic Qualifications, applicants should meet the following requirements:

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field from a recognized institution.

Professional Experience

At least three (3) years of relevant professional experience in accounting or financial management.

Experience in an NGO, civil society organization, organizations of persons with disabilities, or donor-funded project is an advantage.

Demonstrated experience in budgeting, financial operations, reporting, and audit preparation.

Experience in donor financial reporting and grant management is highly desirable.

The candidate should demonstrate:

Strong accounting and financial management skills.

Excellent numerical and analytical abilities.

Good knowledge of budgeting and financial reporting.

Required Skills and Competencies

Knowledge of internal controls and audit processes.

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and accounting software.

Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

Excellent organizational and time-management skills.

Ability to work independently and meet deadlines.

Good communication and interpersonal skills.

High levels of integrity, confidentiality, and professionalism.

Commitment to accountability, transparency, inclusion, and disability rights.

greatrwandajobs.description_html:
Organizational background

Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is a national organization committed to promote the rights, inclusion, education, empowerment and socio-economic well-being of blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda.

The Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) is a non-governmental organization that was founded in August 1994 as a National unified voice for persons with visual impairment. After registering with the Rwanda Governance Board under the legal personality number 60/05 on 16/03/1995, and complies with the new law No 058/2024 of 20/06/2024 and related regulations. RUB works towards the improvement of the situation of blind people through education and rehabilitation to facilitate meaningful equality and integration. RUB holds membership in 2 National umbrellas including UPHLS and NUDOR and also affiliated to the African Union of the Blind (AFUB) and the World Blind Union (WBU). The organization has 64 well established branches in all districts of the country and all those branches managed by persons with visual impairment themselves. RUB activities aim at improving the living conditions of Blind and Partially Sighted (BPS) persons through advocacy, promoting the education of blind and partially sighted persons, capacity development of members and rehabilitation program/service.

1.1. Vision

The vision of RUB is to ‘achieve a situation where people with visual impairment enjoy the same rights as other citizens, receive rehabilitation and education and have equal access to employment’.

1.2. Mission

RUB's mission is to ‘work towards the improvement of the situation of people with visual impairment through rehabilitation and education to facilitate meaningful equality and integration into the society’.

1.3. Objectives

With the purpose of improving the living condition of Blind and partially sighted persons in Rwanda, RUB sets the following objectives to guides its strategic implementations:

  • Bring together persons with visual impairment in a national organization to promote their fundamental rights;
  • Raise awareness on needs, potentials, and aspirations of persons with visual impairment in Rwanda;
  • Advocate for access to education and rehabilitation of persons with visual impairment through dialogue with the government and other partners in development;
  • Seek support to provide adequate and appropriate services to persons with visual impairment;
  • Promote prevention of visual impairment through dialogue with relevant authorities;
  • Promote the inclusion of persons with visual impairment in sport and cultural activities.

About project

Under support from the Marga Schulze Foundation through CBM, RUB is implementing a multi-year project 2026-2028 to advance educational inclusion and equitable learning opportunities for blind and partially sighted girls and women in Rwanda.

The project recognizes that girls and women with disabilities experience multiple and intersecting barriers to education. These may include inaccessible learning environments and materials, limited availability of appropriate support, negative social attitudes, inadequate teacher preparation, financial constraints, and limited opportunities for participation in decisions that affect their education and future.

Children with disabilities in Rwanda continue to face significant barriers to accessing, participating in, and completing education. Girls with disabilities may experience additional barriers because of the intersection of disability and gender. These challenges can be particularly pronounced in rural and emergency-affected communities.

The proposed project therefore seeks to move beyond simply increasing access to schools. It aims to support meaningful participation, retention, learning, progression and empowerment, while strengthening schools and communities to become more inclusive of all learners.

A central element of the project will be the development and testing of practical approaches to inclusive education that can generate evidence and learning for wider application in Rwanda.

2.1 Overall Objective

To identify, support and empower girls and boys with disabilities, both in and out of school, particularly in rural and emergency-affected areas of Rwanda, with a specific focus on improving educational opportunities and outcomes for girls and women with visual impairments.

2.2 Specific Objectives

  • Identify girls and boys with disabilities who are in and out of school across selected rural and emergency-affected contexts in Rwanda and assess their individual and educational support needs.
  • Provide identified girls and women with visual impairments with appropriate and comprehensive support to enhance their enrolment, participation, retention, learning and progression.
  • Support selected schools to develop and implement a holistic approach to inclusion that enables all learners, including learners with disabilities, to participate and learn equitably.
  • Empower women with visual impairments with knowledge, skills and opportunities in human rights, social justice and advocacy, enabling them to contribute to policy, practice and decision-making on disability inclusion and gender equity.

RUB is therefore inviting qualified Rwandans with or without disabilities to apply for this opportunity.

Position Information

3.1 finance officer

Position

Finance Officer

Main Purpose of the Position

The Finance Officer will be responsible for supporting the effective management of RUB's financial resources and ensuring that financial transactions, accounting records, budgets, financial reports, and donor funds are properly managed and accounted for.

Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will contribute to strong financial controls, transparency, accountability, and compliance with RUB policies, donor requirements, and applicable laws and regulations in Rwanda.The Finance Officer will:

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date accounting records.
  • Record and process financial transactions in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Prepare payment vouchers and ensure adequate supporting documentation and authorization.
  • Maintain cashbooks, ledgers, accounts payable and receivable records.
  • Conduct regular bank, cash, and ledger reconciliations.
  • Support the preparation and monitoring of annual and project budgets.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor financial reports.
  • Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and provide variance analysis.
  • Maintain accurate financial records for donor-funded projects.
  • Monitor donor expenditure and compliance with grant agreements.
  • Support payroll preparation and applicable statutory obligations.
  • Maintain proper controls over cash, bank accounts, petty cash, and organizational assets.
  • Support internal and external audits and follow up on audit recommendations.
  • Ensure compliance with RUB financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.
  • Identify financial risks and recommend appropriate corrective measures.
  • Provide financial guidance and support to program and management teams.
  • Maintain confidential and well-organized financial documentation.
  • Report suspected fraud, financial irregularities, or misuse of funds through appropriate channels.

Qualifications

In academic Qualifications, applicants should meet the following requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field from a recognized institution.

Professional Experience

  • At least three (3) years of relevant professional experience in accounting or financial management.
  • Experience in an NGO, civil society organization, organizations of persons with disabilities, or donor-funded project is an advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience in budgeting, financial operations, reporting, and audit preparation.
  • Experience in donor financial reporting and grant management is highly desirable.

The candidate should demonstrate:

  • Strong accounting and financial management skills.
  • Excellent numerical and analytical abilities.
  • Good knowledge of budgeting and financial reporting.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Knowledge of internal controls and audit processes.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and accounting software.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.

  • Commitment to accountability, transparency, inclusion, and disability rights.

greatrwandajobs.title: Accountant Receivable job at Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course
greatrwandajobs.description:
Job Purpose:

The Accountant Receivables is responsible for managing all accounts receivable functions of Rwanda Ultimate Golf Course Ltd. This includes billing, posting payments, reconciling customer accounts, monitoring outstanding balances, and ensuring timely collection of revenues from members, guests, and corporate clients. The role also supports accuracy in reporting and coordination with operational departments to maintain financial integrity and excellent customer service.

Key Responsibilities

Prepare and issue invoices for all sales transactions, including F&B, golf, membership, accommodation, wellness, and corporate events.

Record and reconcile daily revenue from point-of-sale systems (e.g., MICROS) and Property Management Systems (PMS).

Post customer payments accurately and in a timely manner.

Maintain up-to-date accounts receivable records, ensuring accuracy and completeness of customer ledgers.

Follow up on outstanding payments and ensure collections are made within agreed credit terms.

Monitor member accounts and prepare monthly statements for distribution.

Liaise with the Membership, F&B, Golf, and Commercial departments to confirm billing details and resolve discrepancies.

Work closely with the Chief Accountant and finance director to reconcile revenues and receivables at month-end.

Coordinate with the Front Office and Cashiers to ensure accurate posting of guest folios and event charges.

Support management with data for financial reports, audits, and budgeting exercises.

Ensure all receivable transactions comply with company financial policies and internal controls.

Assist in maintaining proper documentation for all billing and collection activities.

Prepare reports on overdue accounts and recommend actions for collection or escalation.

Participate in the monthly and year-end closing process.

Prepare aging analysis of accounts receivable and highlight delinquent accounts.

Support periodic revenue reconciliation between POS, PMS, and accounting systems.

Generate customer account summaries and assist in financial statement preparation.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Professional certification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) is an added advantage.

Minimum of 3 years’ experience in accounting, preferably in hospitality, leisure, or service-oriented industries.

Solid understanding of accounting principles, billing, and collections processes.

Proficiency in accounting software (e.g., Sage, QuickBooks, or ERP systems).

Experience with hospitality systems such as MICROS POS, Opera / Protel / Cloudbeds PMS, and membership billing platforms is an asset.

Key Skills & Competencies

Strong analytical and numerical skills with attention to detail.

Excellent communication and customer service skills for interacting with clients and members.

Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams (Finance, F&B, Golf, Commercial, Guest Experience).

High integrity, confidentiality, and commitment to accuracy.

Time management and ability to handle multiple priorities under tight deadlines.

Strong problem-solving and reconciliation abilities.

greatrwandajobs.title: Agriculture Associate job at Gardens for Health International
greatrwandajobs.description:
About the Organization

Gardens for Health International bridges the disconnect between food, agriculture, and nutrition. For over a decade, Gardens for Health International (GHI) has implemented nutrition-sensitive agriculture programs to combat childhood malnutrition in Rwanda. We equip families and communities with the knowledge, resources and support they need to meet their nutritional needs. GHI’s core program works in collaboration with government-run health centers to identify and support rural families struggling with malnutrition. In addition to this core program, GHI collaborates with a variety of governmental and non-governmental partners to bring our expertise to new settings and new populations, such as primary schools and refugee camps. We are an impact-driven organization with a deep commitment to ensuring that every program we design meets and responds to the unique needs of the communities we serve. Our team is flexible, innovative, and passionate about sparking lasting change.

About the Role

The Agriculture Associate will be in charge of the overseeing of the agriculture related partnerships on the farm. He/She will ensure the farm is growing crops according to the farm strategy and GHI vision, that the farm is well-maintained and healthy, and that all farm tasks related to the program are completed on time.

He/She will also participate in the farm tours along with the Ag team to organization, visitors and donors. He/She will also build capacity of farm technicians on the permaculture and conservation agriculture principles and practices. He/She will be assisting to the development of different reports to farm project partners and represent the farm to external partners.

Overview of the Role

Position: Agriculture Associate

Place of Work: Ndera, Gasabo with travel to the field as required

Staff reporting to this position: None

Reports to: Agriculture Coordinator

Roles and Responsibilities

Works alongside with farm technicians to implement the planned activities at the farm

Record all farm data including farm produce into Commcare

Lead homemade pesticide preparation, ensure its quality and research on types of pests which can be managed by such pesticide

Lead manure production from the farm and check quality depends on the techniques applied.

Lead seeds’ saving and advise farm team accordingly to ensure the quality of seeds

Preparation of crop plan and lead its’ implementation on seasonal basis

Lead farm related trials, records keeping and reporting

Collaborate with the farm livestock technician to monitor and manage livestock farming activities 

Conducts agricultural trainings for fellow farm technicians on permaculture principles practices

Monitoring the on-going farm activities and preparing farm expense requests and monthly budgets

Work with the farm technicians to hire part-time workers and distributes assignments and payment to them

Work closely with the farm technicians ensuring that all equipment, machinery and facilities are kept to an optimum level.

Broader role at GHI

Conducts farm tours for visitors and educates permanent staff and fellows about the farm

Provide support to the Ag Team in various ways, including curriculum development and external trainings as needed.

Qualifications and experience:

Bachelors’ degree in Agriculture, Crop Production or other related fields.

At least one year of experience preferably in Organic farming, Conservation agriculture, and Climate smart agriculture.

Having technical expertise in livestock husbandry will be an added value.

Fluency in spoken and written English and Kinyarwanda.

Ability to multitask, priorities, and manage time efficiently

Excellent communication skills

Accurate attention to details

Goal-oriented, organized team player

Ability to work well with management and staff at all levels

Passion for Gardens for Health’s vision and values, with a commitment to serving the organization mission

Equal Employment Opportunity

Gardens for Health International is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer fully dedicated to achieving a diverse staff. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage and welcome all interested potential applicants, regardless of background or prior experience volunteering with Gardens for Health International, to apply.

Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)

Gardens for Health International has zero – tolerance policy for exploitative and abusive relationships. Gardens for Health International will ensure the fulfillment of our moral obligation to protect minor children and other vulnerable members of society from abuse, exploitation, neglect, and other forms of violence.

Child Safeguarding: 

Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

Health and Safety:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with GHI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

greatrwandajobs.title: Planning MEAL Officer job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Context of the position: 

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Planning MEAL Officer.

Job Purpose: 

The job holder plays a leading role in the programs and projects implementation of a comprehensive Monitoring and Evaluation system. S/He leads and coordinates Planning and M&E activities at program area. 

In collaboration with program area’s colleagues, S/he also designs and implements strategies that lead to high-quality results, Support in development of concept notes and proposal writing. S/he builds the capacity of program staffs on Result-Based Management (RBM) approach and drives program area learning and adaptive management.

S/he assists the Head of Program Area in preparing quarterly, biannual and annual reports, maintain the MEAL system that informs program planning, measures result against objectives PRODIGI and PDB2), collects and analyses different data for reporting and informed decision making.

Main clients: 

Head of Program Area 

Research and RBM Snr. Manager 

Grants MEL Manager 

Project Staff 

Director of Program Quality, Safeguarding and Partnership development 

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities: 

Ensures the strict implementation of the organization’s M&E guide, tools and templates across the program area;

Leads and actively participates in planning, monitoring, reporting, evaluation and research activities to be carried out in the program area and ensure that it is conducted in line with agreed ethical principles.

Coordinates the results-based management planning and reporting process 

Promote impact reporting by leading quality documentation of stories of change, best practices and lesson learned. 

Provides direct technical support to program staffs to prepare project M&E plans 

Provides technical guidance for programs baselines and evaluations studies 

Supports program area’s strategic and annual plan preparation process including clear target setting, development of M&E indicators as well as plan alignment with the national annual and strategic plan.

Leads in the development/ enhancement of data collection and monitoring tools for child, youth, family and community development within the Program Area;

Maintain and regularly update the program area’s database. 

Develops and strengthens monitoring and evaluation procedures as well as impact indicators for the project success;

Monitors and analyses the project performance focusing on quality and sustainability of the project results;

Advises and suggests strategies to the Program Area team for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of Program Area programmes;

In close collaboration with Research and RBM Sr manager and Head of Program Area, identify capacity gaps and build the capacity of the Program Area staff on programme quality. 

Monitor cross-cutting themes (child safeguarding, advocacy, gender equality and disability inclusion, etc.) are integrated in programs. 

Formal qualifications and Experience requirements: 

Bachelor’s degree in project management, business administration and management, economics, development studies with emphasis on development issues and risk management issues or a related field;

A minimum of three years of experience in project M&E, a documented track record of planning, monitoring and evaluation;

Required Skills: 

Strong analytical skills.

Language Proficiency: English & Kinyarwanda, French (optional

Excellent interpersonal skills and team player.

Experience with an international Non-Governmental Organization would be an asset

Ability to generate learning and program evidence for quality improvement and decision making.

greatrwandajobs.title: Mine Supervisor job at Trinity Musha Mines Ltd
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

Trinity Musha Mines Ltd is a Mining company focused on the production and exploration of Tin, Tantalum, and Lithium in Rwanda. Trinity Musha is currently inviting suitable candidates to apply for the following position:

Job Brief

The Mine Supervisor is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the day-to-day mining operations to ensure safe, efficient, and productive mining activities within the designated area.

Responsibilities

The Mine Supervisor has the following responsibilities and duties:

Supervise Mining Operations: Coordinate and direct mining activities, including drilling, blasting, excavation, hauling, and ore processing, to meet production targets and quality standards. Allocate resources, such as manpower, equipment, and materials, to optimize efficiency and productivity. Monitor production schedules, equipment performance, and ore grades to identify and address operational issues or bottlenecks. Supports the Mining Team Leaders to ensure that production team delivers on the daily planned production and necessary measures are taken whenever the production targets are not met. Observe and enforce any code of practice, instructions, procedures, directives, permissions, exemptions etc. issued by the Mine Manager or any other person authorized to do so.

Ensure Health and Safety Compliance: Inspect all other workings, in your area of responsibility, at least once a week. Be responsible for the proper discipline of all persons working under your charge. Provide and maintain a working environment that is safe and without risk to the health and safety of employees within your area of responsibility. Identify relevant hazards and assess the related risks within your area of responsibility. Implement and enforce safety protocols, procedures, and regulations to minimize risks and prevent accidents or injuries. Conduct regular safety inspections, hazard assessments, and safety training sessions for mining personnel. Investigate incidents or near misses, report findings, and recommend corrective actions to improve safety performance. Ensure adherence to the SHEC laws, regulations and policies.

Maintain Equipment and Infrastructure: Oversee maintenance and repair activities for mining equipment, vehicles, and infrastructure to ensure operational reliability and longevity. Schedule preventive maintenance tasks, inspections, and repairs to minimize downtime and maximize equipment availability. Coordinate with maintenance staff and suppliers to procure spare parts, components, and consumables as needed.

Management of Personnel: Ensure that people under your supervision adhere to HR Policies and Procedures. Provide Employees within your area of responsibility with any information, instructions or supervision that is necessary to enable them to perform their work professionally, safely and without risks. Consider Employees’ training and capabilities before assigning tasks to them. Ensure that all persons working under your charge are fully trained on job training or otherwise in their tasks. Responsible for staffing needs of the area of responsibility. Supervise and mentor mining staff, including operators and labourers, to ensure adherence to company policies, procedures, and performance standards. Provide leadership, guidance, and support to promote teamwork, motivation, and professional development among team members. Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and address disciplinary issues or concerns in accordance with HR policies.

Environmental Monitor and Compliance: Ensure compliance with environmental regulations, permits, and standards governing mining operations, waste management, and land reclamation. Implement environmental management practices, such as erosion control, water management, and rehabilitation measures, to minimize environmental impacts.

Data Collection and Reporting: Record in ink in your logbook the following during or at the conclusion of your shift: The designation of every working place or other working place inspected by yourself during your shift. Particularly of any unsatisfactory conditions of working places, traveling ways or other workings in your area of responsibility as observed by yourself or reported to you by the Mine team leader or any other person, specifically in respect of ground conditions and where safety of people are concerned. Any instructions given by you to secure the health and safety of persons under your charge and adhered to. Give regular reports on the Production, HSEC, Security and HR to the Section team leader / Site manager for your designated area of responsibility. Prepare regular reports, dashboards, and presentations for management review, highlighting key operational KPIs, trends, and challenges.

Qualifications and Experience

The Mine Supervisor should have the following education, experience and skills:

Bachelor’s degree/Advanced diploma in mining Engineering

At least 3 years Certification in mining from a competent mining school

Experience of at least 3 years in the field.

Physical fitness.

Excellent Communication skills (English preferable)

Willing to work overtime

Good supervisor skills and be able to delegate different work to workers/Team work spirit

Equal Opportunity Employer

Trinity Musha Mines Ltd values diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, ethnicity, disability, or background.

greatrwandajobs.title: Driver job at National Industrial Research and Development Agency
greatrwandajobs.company: National Industrial Research And Development Agency
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background information about the job or company (e.g., role context, company overview)

The national industrial research and development agency (NIRDA) is seeking to fill the position of Driver. This is a Level 10.II position with 2 posts available under contract.

Responsibilities or duties

Complete appropriate tripsheets as required by line manager to record officially each transport.

Effective communicates with dispatch recording schedule progress and receive instructions.

Ensure that there is availability of all the required documents/suppliers including vehicle insurance.

Ensure the road safety compliance.

Inform logistics officer of any major repairs to be carried out.

Maintain a professional image and attitude in regards to the staff.

Safeguard all vehicle accessories (e.g. Jack, First aid kit, tools, etc.).

Maintain cleanness of the vehicles.

Provide reliable and secure driving services.

Report accident or other emergency facts.

Solve minor technical problems for vehicles.

Perform any other related tasks as assigned by the supervisor.

Qualifications or requirements (e.g., education, skills)

The job requires the ability to complete tripsheets, communicate effectively with dispatch, ensure vehicle documentation and road safety compliance, report repairs and incidents, maintain a professional image, safeguard vehicle accessories, keep vehicles clean, provide reliable driving services, and solve minor technical problems.

Experience needed

Experience in driving and related tasks is implied by the responsibilities.

Any other provided details (e.g., benefits, work environment, team info, or additional notes)

Exams to be conducted include Psychometric Test, Written, and Oral. The position reports to the Director of Administration & Finance Unit.

Job Description

This description has been adapted for JobNziza readers to provide a clearer overview of the opportunity.

BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.

Position: Technical Sector Officer - Community Mobilization

Job Location: Ruhango District, Rwanda

About the AIM Program:

The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to enhance lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway.

About the Role:

The Technical assist Officer, Community Mobilization (TSO-CM) will assist the Technical Coordinator Community Mobilization in planning and implementing social empowerment and community engagement activities, including gender and social inclusion, disability inclusion, SRHR, SGBV, community dialogues, and grassroots-level advocacy. They will also contribute to staff capacity development through targeted training and supervision. Additionally, the TSO-CM will deliver technical assistance, assist, and quality control in implementing SGBV and SRHR community-based case management and referral systems.

The TSO-CM will collaborate with the country program team, AIM central team, BI technical anchors, and Technical Coordinators to enhance program quality, contextualize training modules, and train staff on new materials and tools. They will ensure effective delivery of gender equality and social inclusion (GESI), disability inclusion (DI), Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), enabling environment and advocacy components are integrated into the overall AIM programmatic operations.

The ideal candidate for this role is one who is proactive, passionate, resourceful, and enjoys being a team player.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Technical Support

assist AIM field team in inception phase activities (community mobilization and inception meetings, transect walks, surveys, YDC formation).

Train regional staff on GESI, GBV, disability inclusion, domestic violence reporting, and women's rights advocacy; enhance PA/mentor capacity on GESI, community mobilization, SRHR, and GBV sessions.

assist social and behaviour change communication (SBCC) planning, monitoring, and evaluation and coordinating with the project team.

guide the implementation of SBCC dialogue sessions at the community level, targeting local, religious, and cultural leaders, as well as other duty bearers.

Guide community leaders in developing action plans based on commitments made during SBCC dialogue sessions. assist tracking and follow-up on these action plans to ensure progress and accountability.

detect and adapt safe, accessible club spaces with reasonable accommodations and gender-segregated infrastructure (restrooms, dignity kits, baby changing stations), prioritizing marginalized groups including PWDs.

assist coordination with stakeholders (government, INGOs, CSOs, YDC members, and service providers) for social empowerment and enabling environment interventions.

Participate in regional GESI, SRHR, and SGBV working groups, advocating for women's and girls' rights.

Mentor and assist youth advocates in developing, implementing & monitoring advocacy action plans, overseeing practical implementation (events, stakeholder meetings, logistics, linkage to CSO networks and technical working groups).

guide community action planning sessions to create community action plans, consolidate commitments and ensure community-led solutions.

Organize action planning and handover meetings at the end of each cohort to secure firm commitments from local leaders and ensure the sustainability of the outcomes.

2. Coordination, Planning and Partnership

assist coordination with a range of stakeholders, including government entities, INGOs, CSOs, YDC members, and service providers at the sub-national level, to assist interventions as well as the program’s grassroots advocacy and partnerships work.

organize and consolidate the mapping of SRHR and SGBV service providers at the regional level.

Organize events for the celebration of international observance days such as International Women's Day, the 16 Days of Activism, and International Day of the Girl Child in the regions.

Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments in youth advocacy action plans.

3. Reporting, Documentation and Communication

Contribute to program reports and deliverables as required and demonstrate the status of GESI and grassroots-level advocacy activities towards achieving expected results.

Quality management, checks, and assurance in the SGBV case recording database to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and timely reports.

detect and document best practices, most significant change stories, and share this knowledge with colleagues. Ensure quality reporting on enabling environments, community mobilization, and GESI indicators, and document good practices.

assist regional managers, branch managers and programme assistants regularly to ensure timely and high-quality programmatic data entry and reporting in relevant manual and digital MIS (BInsight) by the Program Assistants, and mentors.

assist documentation of program wins and success stories / case studies

Ensure timely preparation and submission of programmatic management information system (MIS), financial and donor reports.

4. Policy and Strategy Compliance

Popularize the Enabling Environment Strategy, GESI policies and SGBV, SRHR and disability inclusion guidelines among the frontline staff through orientations and trainings

help with policy-related materials development and localization.

Safeguarding responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation.

Act as a key source of assist, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.

Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.

Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so.

Major Challenges:

Access of hard to reach locations in the communities AIM serves

Buy-in for advocacy, GESI & SRHR work at the respective regions

Managing coordination among several team members within the BRAC family.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

Timely achievement of project activities.

Efficient case management and referral systems.

Effective staff capacity building on advocacy, GESI, SRHR, DI and SGBV.

Effective implementation of resources and tools.

Functional SGBV & SRH case management referral mechanism and database.

Strong partnerships established.

Effective implementation of youth advocacy action plans.

Community dialogues delivered using GESI-responsive SBCC messages and tools.

Individual/specific KPIs as agreed with supervisor.

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree / Graduate or Post graduate in International Development, Gender, Sociology, Anthropology, Social Sciences or any other related fields.

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Training materials development, staff capacity building, and facilitation skills

Computer literacy and presentation skills

Report writing and documentation of Most Significant Change Stories

Proactive, self-starter and independent worker with the ability to assist large teams

Demonstrate commitment to community mobilization work around education, GESI, SRHR, and advocacy work, applying rights-based, human-centered, and survivor-centered approaches.

Exhibit empathy and positive interpersonal skills, including cultural competence.

Experience Requirements:

3-5 years of relevant experience in gender equality, social inclusion, SGBV, community engagement, and advocacy.

Previous experience in providing technical assistance, especially related to advocacy, community engagement and empowerment-related activities, training module development and execution, and training facilitation.

Experience working in integrated programs targeted for adolescent girls and young women is a plus.

Previous experience in the development of SBCC messages, tools, and materials for community-based dialogues and other activities.

Experience in conducting advocacy, community mobilization and engagement activities is also an added advantage.

Employment type: Regular/Fixed-Term

About BRAC International:

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organization, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the assist and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to assist a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 16 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit (www.bracinternational.org)

Our Core Values:

Integrity: We approach our collaborate with honesty and integrity.

Innovation: We innovate and iterate to enhance our impact.

Inclusiveness: We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most.

Effectiveness: We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty.

Position: Technical Sector Officer - Education

Job Location: Ruhango District Rwanda

About the AIM Program:

The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to enhance lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway.

About the AIM Education Pathway:

The AIM Education pathway is designed to increase access to and completion of quality secondary education for adolescent girls, aged 12-17, across the AIM countries: Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to assist adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to enhance gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students.

This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better produce young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community assist, and weak school governance systems.

About the Role:

The Technical Sector Officer (TSO) - Education will assist the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in planning, implementing, and ensuring the quality delivery of the AIM education pathway.

They will be tasked with technical & implementation-related tasks under AIM education pathway, i,e. facilitating training, reviewing content and curriculum and adapting it to their context, and supporting teachers' professional development as well as school leadership's school improvement planning processes. They will also contribute to staff capacity development through targeted training and supervision.

The TSO-Education will collaborate with the region & country level program team, other sectral TSOs for any technical need/query, to enhance program quality, contextualize training modules, and train staff on new materials and tools. They will ensure effective delivery of gender responsive training for the teachers and school management and assist creating an enabling learning environment in the AIM supported secondary schools. S/he will Also ensure effective delivery of parental engagement to help with increasing access to and completion of quality secondary education for very young adolescents (VYAs) and adolescent girls (AGs) aged 12-17 years.

An ideal candidate for this role is one with strong technical skills and experience in developing and reviewing quality education curriculum content, teachers’ guides, teacher training manuals, including a strong background in training teachers and educators. S/he should have strong training skills, coordination and negotiation skills, be proactive, passionate, resourceful, and enjoy being a team player.

Key Responsibilities:

Technical Support:

assist AIM team in the inception phase activities (in delivering education messages during community mobilization and inception meetings, family meetings, YDC meetings, etc.).

Work closely with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in preparing the MoU templates for the schools.

help with obtaining Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with relevant ministries at the regional and/or district/county level, and schools.

Meet with relevant regional and district officials and share the MoU that outlines the key objectives of AIM education pathways and how Ministry of Education and the district will assist and allow access to local education departments and schools, and school records.

assist developing/reviewing/updating/adapting, existing teachers’ guide and contents for the teachers and school leadership in the country context in coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BRAC International (BI) technical anchors.

assist developing /reviewing/updating/adapting the training guide on school management and school improvement plans in close coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BI technical anchors.

assist developing a training guide for the peer mentors, assist groups, and tutoring in close coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BI technical anchors.

assist AIM program assistants (PAs) to detect Teacher Champions in the schools

assist the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education to ensure the establishment of a robust system for the smooth transfer of school-related assist costs to ensure AGs' financial assist to continue their education.

Direct Operational assist:

Facilitate training for AIM PAs, teachers, and school leadership on gender responsive pedagogy, mentorship, and tutoring.

Facilitate training for school leadership, school management/and parent-teacher associations (PTAs) on school improvement planning.

Work closely with the school administrations, head teachers, teachers and school management committees (SMCs)/PTAs for the inception and introduce the AIM education pathway activities.

assist AIM PAs to do monthly follow-ups of the AIM education pathway interventions for quality program outputs.

perform/attend different levels of staff meetings.

detect the knowledge gap of programme staff and take necessary steps for their improvement.

Coordination, Planning and Partnership and M&E:

assist coordination with a range of stakeholders, including teachers, school leadership, school management, parents' teachers association, Government education officials, to assist school-related interventions

collaborate with the identified Alternative Education providers in the region and organize to enrol eligible AIM participants

Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments of the training plans and delivery

Report back to the Government education officials/MoE as outlined in the MoU on activities done by BRAC.

Monitoring, Reporting, Documentation and Communication:

Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments of the training plans and delivery.

Contribute to program reports and deliverables as required.

detect and document best practices, most significant change stories, and share this knowledge with colleagues.

Ensure quality reporting on enabling learning environments at school, and document good practices.

assist regional managers, branch managers, and programme Officers regularly to ensure timely and high-quality programmatic data entry and reporting in the relevant manual and digital MIS (BInsight).

assist the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in the documentation of program wins and success stories / case studies

Ensure timely preparation and submission of programmatic management information system (MIS), training reports and share project progress reports regularly with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education.

Safeguarding responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation.

Act as a key source of assist, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.

Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.

Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so.

Major Challenges:

Access of hard to reach locations in the communities AIM serves

Coordination with different schools

Coordination with the BI team in different time zones

Managing coordination among several team members within the BRAC family.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

Timely achievement of project activities.

Quality of the training guides and content prepared

Efficient and quality delivery of the different AIM education pathway training.

Effective staff, teachers, and school leadership capacity building on gender responsiveness

Effective use of resources and tools.

Strong partnerships established with schools and the Government education officials

Individual/specific KPIs as agreed with the supervisor.

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree or Postgraduate in Education/ International, Development/ Gender/ Sociology/ Anthropology/ Social Sciences and/or other relevant fields

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Training materials development, staff capacity building, and facilitation skills

Computer literacy and presentation skills

Report writing and documentation of Most Significant Change Stories

Proactive, self-starter and independent worker with the ability to assist large teams

Demonstrate commitment to community mobilization work around education, GESI, SRHR, and advocacy work, applying rights-based, human-centered, and survivor-centered approaches.

Exhibit empathy and positive interpersonal skills, including cultural competence.

Experience Requirements:

3-5 years of relevant experience in education training, development of training guide, contents and curriculum, gender equality, social inclusion, community engagement, and school engagement.

Previous experience in providing technical assistance, especially related to teachers’ training module development and execution, and training facilitation

Experience working in integrated programs targeted for adolescent girls and young women is a plus.

Previous experience in the development of Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) messages, tools, and materials for community-based dialogues and other activities.

Experience in conducting advocacy, community mobilization and engagement activities is also an added advantage

Employment type: Regular/Fixed-Term

About BRAC International:

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organization, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the assist and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to assist a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 16 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit (www.bracinternational.org)

Our Core Values:

Integrity: We approach our collaborate with honesty and integrity.

Innovation: We innovate and iterate to enhance our impact.

Inclusiveness: We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most.

Effectiveness: We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty.
