greatrwandajobs.description:
COMPANY INTRODUCTION

Wicloudrwd is a global digital transformation and IT outsourcing company established in 2022, with operations across multiple international locations. The company provides technology and IT outsourcing solutions tailored to Microsoft environments, with expertise across Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Windows Commercial, and Microsoft Office 365.

Location: Kigali, Rwanda

Employment Type: Full-time

Working Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced IT Lead to oversee IT operations, infrastructure, security, compliance, team development, and technology innovation for Wicloudrwd's Kigali operations.

The successful candidate will provide strong technical and operational leadership, establish effective IT processes and controls, and ensure that IT services meet business and client requirements.

Key Responsibilities

1. IT Operations & Governance

Oversee end-to-end IT operations in Kigali.

Establish clear IT governance, roles, responsibilities, and escalation mechanisms.

Ensure timely incident reporting, coordination, and resolution for major IT issues.

Provide regular IT status, risk, and improvement reports to management.

2. Infrastructure & Service Management

Manage corporate networks (LAN/WAN/VPN), servers, cloud resources, endpoints, and collaboration tools.

Ensure office and production environments meet business SLA requirements.

Own the IT asset lifecycle, including procurement, deployment, inventory, and retirement.

Manage external vendors and service providers.

3. Information Security & Compliance

Implement and maintain IT security and compliance controls required for business lines.

Support internal audits, customer reviews, and compliance assessments.

Define and enforce IT security policies, incident response plans, and awareness programs.

Ensure appropriate access control, identity management, and data protection.

4. AI Enablement & Innovation

Identify and implement AI solutions to enhance IT operations and productivity.

Drive adoption of AI tools to optimize internal workflows and service delivery.

Collaborate with stakeholders to integrate AI into support and business processes.

5. Team Leadership & Development

Lead and manage IT teams across multiple offices.

Set clear performance objectives and accountability mechanisms.

Improve execution, professionalism, and internal service credibility of the IT function.

Build standardized processes to reduce dependency on individuals.

6. Cross-functional & International Communication

Work closely with business, compliance, security, operations, and other functional teams.

Communicate effectively in English with overseas leadership teams.

Translate technical issues into structured, business-oriented updates for non-technical stakeholders.

Qualifications & Requirements

Required

Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.

6+ years of IT experience, including 2–3 years in an IT Lead or equivalent role.

Hands-on experience in IT infrastructure and operations, with solid knowledge of ITSM and security compliance.

Practical experience applying AI in operations and/or productivity.

Technical & Professional Skills

Proven experience managing IT for multi-site or mid-to-large organizations is a plus.

Solid foundation in networking, systems, and enterprise IT environments.

Familiarity with ITSM processes, including Incident, Problem, and Change Management.

Hands-on experience with information security and compliance in international service environments.

Cloud platform experience, such as Microsoft Azure, is a strong advantage.

Leadership & Personal Attributes

Strong ownership mindset and risk awareness.

Proactive, structured, and execution-driven.

Able to lead teams with authority and credibility.

Comfortable working under high standards and client scrutiny.

AI-related Experience

Experience with one or more of the following is expected:

Generative AI and LLM tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, or Gemini.

Prompt engineering.

AI automation for operations.

AI chatbot implementation.

AI knowledge base development.

AI-enabled process automation.

AI for ticket triage in support environments.

AI workflow optimization.

AI-driven reporting.

Language Requirements

Local Language: Fluent in reading, writing, and speaking.

English: Strong professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

greatrwandajobs.title: Internal Auditor job at Letshego Rwanda Limited
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

Letshego Rwanda Limited (Letshego Rwanda) was established in Rwanda in 2004 and is a subsidiary of Letshego Holdings Limited (LHL), a pan Africa financial services group that is headquartered in Gaborone. LHL is the largest indigenous BSE-quoted company with a current market capitalization in excess of BWP 5 billion (US$ 500 million) that places it in the top 40 sub-Saharan Africa companies (excluding-South Africa). Since inception Letshego Rwanda has been operating as a regulated credit only microfinance company. In 2013, Letshego Rwanda obtained a deposit-taking microfinance license from the National Bank of Rwanda.

Letshego Holdings Limited was incorporated in 1998; it’s headquartered in Gaborone and has been publicly listed on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) since 2002. It is an inclusive finance focused group with consumer, micro-lending and deposit-taking subsidiaries across sub-Saharan Africa.

An opening has arisen within Letshego Rwanda Limited LRL for the below-mentioned position. This role is tenable at LRL. The incumbent will serve as a key member of the Country management team (CMC). The requirements of the role are outlined below:

Purpose of the Job:

To lead the identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of credit risk across the organization by developing and implementing effective risk management policies, frameworks, and tools. The Credit Risk Manager ensures that lending and credit activities align with the organization’s risk appetite and regulatory requirements while supporting sustainable business growth through sound credit risk practices and strategic risk insights

Key Accountabilities:

Develops and ensure implementation of country Internal Audit strategic and operational audit plans.

Develops and manages internal audit policy documents, guidelines, and charters for adoption at country

Implements the Assurance Model within the Country through collaboration with the Risk and Compliance functions, External Auditors and Regulators to ensure appropriate assurance coverage.

Adheres to the International Internal Audit (IIA) standards for all internal audit activities concerning positioning, people and processes, with a critical view of achieving and maintaining conformance status.

Executes approved audit plans within the Country and report to the Country Audit Committee.

Presents Internal Audit findings to the Board of Directors, Audit Committee and Country Management to determine recommendations to appropriate collective plan.

Ensures that Internal Audit reviews determine sufficient governance and control.

Implement the strategies and policies approved by the Board, develop processes that adequately identify, measure, monitor and control Risks faced by the institution.

Experience and Qualifications Required:

University degree in accounting, finance, business administration, Microfinance or Banking, Business Information Technology (BIT) or other related field.

Must have one of professional qualifications ( CPA,ACCA,CIA,CISA Or CFE).

At least 5 years of Experience.

Embrace the Group uniquenesses

The job holder shall, at all times embrace Group uniqueness’s set out below:

Simple - Straight forward and uncomplicated

Appropriate - Relevant and suitable

Accessible - Welcoming and consistent

Ethical - Honest and principled

Responsive - Receptive and compassionate

Inclusive - Embracing and proactive

Essential and Desired Competencies

Deciding and Initiating Action

Leading and Supervising

Working with People

Adhering to principles & values

Relating and Networking

Persuading and Influencing

Presenting and Communicating Information

Writing and Reporting

Learning & Researching

Planning and Organizing

Coping with Pressures and Setbacks

Commercial Thinking

Analytical

Additional Information:

Jobholder should be a person of high integrity and discretion with confidential matters. Multi-cultural awareness and the ability to interact with a wide range of differing levels and sectors of staff, society, social and business, is an essential characteristic of the person holding this position.
greatrwandajobs.description_text:
Background

Letshego Rwanda Limited (Letshego Rwanda) was established in Rwanda in 2004 and is a subsidiary of Letshego Holdings Limited (LHL), a pan Africa financial services group that is headquartered in Gaborone. LHL is the largest indigenous BSE-quoted company with a current market capitalization in excess of BWP 5 billion (US$ 500 million) that places it in the top 40 sub-Saharan Africa companies (excluding-South Africa). Since inception Letshego Rwanda has been operating as a regulated credit only microfinance company. In 2013, Letshego Rwanda obtained a deposit-taking microfinance license from the National Bank of Rwanda.

Letshego Holdings Limited was incorporated in 1998; it’s headquartered in Gaborone and has been publicly listed on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) since 2002. It is an inclusive finance focused group with consumer, micro-lending and deposit-taking subsidiaries across sub-Saharan Africa.

An opening has arisen within Letshego Rwanda Limited LRL for the below-mentioned position. This role is tenable at LRL. The incumbent will serve as a key member of the Country management team (CMC). The requirements of the role are outlined below:

Purpose of the Job:

To lead the identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of credit risk across the organization by developing and implementing effective risk management policies, frameworks, and tools. The Credit Risk Manager ensures that lending and credit activities align with the organization’s risk appetite and regulatory requirements while supporting sustainable business growth through sound credit risk practices and strategic risk insights

Key Accountabilities:

Develops and ensure implementation of country Internal Audit strategic and operational audit plans.

Develops and manages internal audit policy documents, guidelines, and charters for adoption at country

Implements the Assurance Model within the Country through collaboration with the Risk and Compliance functions, External Auditors and Regulators to ensure appropriate assurance coverage.

Adheres to the International Internal Audit (IIA) standards for all internal audit activities concerning positioning, people and processes, with a critical view of achieving and maintaining conformance status.

Executes approved audit plans within the Country and report to the Country Audit Committee.

Presents Internal Audit findings to the Board of Directors, Audit Committee and Country Management to determine recommendations to appropriate collective plan.

Ensures that Internal Audit reviews determine sufficient governance and control.

Implement the strategies and policies approved by the Board, develop processes that adequately identify, measure, monitor and control Risks faced by the institution.

Experience and Qualifications Required:

University degree in accounting, finance, business administration, Microfinance or Banking, Business Information Technology (BIT) or other related field.

Must have one of professional qualifications ( CPA,ACCA,CIA,CISA Or CFE).

At least 5 years of Experience.

Embrace the Group uniquenesses

The job holder shall, at all times embrace Group uniqueness’s set out below:

Simple - Straight forward and uncomplicated

Appropriate - Relevant and suitable

Accessible - Welcoming and consistent

Ethical - Honest and principled

Responsive - Receptive and compassionate

Inclusive - Embracing and proactive

Essential and Desired Competencies

Deciding and Initiating Action

Leading and Supervising

Working with People

Adhering to principles & values

Relating and Networking

Persuading and Influencing

Presenting and Communicating Information

Writing and Reporting

Learning & Researching

Planning and Organizing

Coping with Pressures and Setbacks

Commercial Thinking

Analytical

Additional Information:

Jobholder should be a person of high integrity and discretion with confidential matters. Multi-cultural awareness and the ability to interact with a wide range of differing levels and sectors of staff, society, social and business, is an essential characteristic of the person holding this position.

greatrwandajobs.title: People and Culture Manager job at Letshego Rwanda Limited
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

Letshego Rwanda Limited (Letshego Rwanda) was established in Rwanda in 2004 and is a subsidiary of Letshego Holdings Limited (LHL), a pan Africa financial services group that is headquartered in Gaborone. LHL is the largest indigenous BSE-quoted company with a current market capitalization in excess of BWP 5 billion (US$ 500 million) that places it in the top 40 sub-Saharan Africa companies (excluding-South Africa). Since inception Letshego Rwanda has been operating as a regulated credit only microfinance company. In 2013, Letshego Rwanda obtained a deposit-taking microfinance license from the National Bank of Rwanda.

Letshego Holdings Limited was incorporated in 1998; it’s headquartered in Gaborone and has been publicly listed on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) since 2002. It is an inclusive finance focused group with consumer, micro-lending and deposit-taking subsidiaries across sub-Saharan Africa.

An opening has arisen within Letshego Rwanda Limited LRL for the below-mentioned position. This role is tenable at LRL. The incumbent will serve as a key member of the Country management team (CMC).

Purpose of the Job:

To lead, develop, and implement country human capital management strategies that will enable an employee-oriented, high-performance culture that emphasizes quality, productivity, goal attainment, and empowerment. Responsible for developing processes and metrics that support the achievement of the country’s business goals

Key Accountabilities:

Responsible for the country human capital strategy aligned with the Group's people culture and strategy to contribute to a motivated workforce.

Forecasts resource requirements to enable business goals and objectives.

Responsible for creating a compelling Letshego employer brand that attracts diverse, experienced, and capable talent.

Ensures performance management programs, supporting systems, and processes align with strategy and goals, driving the annual country performance review process.

Responsible for talent development, succession planning, and management programs.

Responsible for competitive rewards programs to attract and retain key players in a highly competitive industry.

Responsible for the succession planning process to ensure management and professional readiness to meet the subsidiary's growth plans

Responsible for measuring metrics that support business goals, necessary aspects of human capital, and training and development.

Oversees the learning and development program in line with business requirements.

Ensures adherence to HC policies and procedures to promote a conducive working environment.

Responsible for promoting people wellness through the implementation of a wellness strategy.

Provides advice in disciplinary and grievance procedures.

Implements the strategies and policies approved by the Board, developing processes that adequately identify, measure, monitor, and control risks faced by the institution.

Key Performance Indicators:

Strategy Execution

Employee Engagement

Budget Plan vs Expenditure

Talent Attraction, Acquisition, Development, and Retention

Employee Engagement

Compensation Management

Experience and Qualifications Required:

A degree in Organizational Psychology, Human Resource Management, Business Administration or any other related field.

Master’s degree in organizational psychology, Human Resources, Business Administration, or a relevant field will be an added advantage

Minimum of 7 years of working experience in human resources management with 3 years human resource senior management role.

Membership of a professional association will be an added advantage

Note:

Selection will be conducted on a rolling basis, and Letshego reserves the right to close the recruitment process and withdraw the advertisement once a suitable candidate has been identified

Only Shortlisted candidates will be invited for interviews

greatrwandajobs.title: Legal Officer job at Gabiro Agribusiness Hub (GAH) Ltd
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

Gabiro Agribusiness Hub Ltd (GAH Ltd) is a flagship agribusiness initiative established through a partnership between the Government of Rwanda and NETAFIM Ltd, a global leader in precision irrigation solutions. Located in Nyagatare District, GAH Ltd is at the forefront of transforming Rwanda’s agricultural sector through large-scale irrigated farming, modern agribusiness infrastructure, and climate-smart agriculture. The Hub is designed to drive modern, irrigated agriculture, enhance productivity, and attract commercial farming investment.

The Hub was established to drive agricultural commercialization, enhance food security, promote technology-driven farming, and attract private sector investment into high-value agriculture. Through its integrated irrigation infrastructure and modern farming ecosystem, GAH Ltd aims to position Rwanda as a regional model for sustainable and productive agribusiness development.

About the Position

As the organization continues to scale its operations, we are seeking to recruit a competent candidate to fill the position of Legal Officer, who will be responsible for overseeing and managing the legal aspects of the company's operations. This role requires a deep understanding of corporate law, contract management, and regulatory compliance. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to provide sound legal advice and guidance to the management team.

Duties & Responsibilities

Provide legal guidance and support to the management team on a wide range of legal issues, including but not limited to contracts, corporate governance, compliance, and regulatory matters.

Review, draft, and participate in negotiation of various contracts, agreements, and legal documents to ensure they adhere to the company's policies and comply with relevant laws and regulations.

Conduct legal research and analysis to stay updated on changes in laws and regulations that may affect the company's operations, and make recommendations to ensure compliance.

Collaborate with different departments to develop and/or update existing internal policies and procedures to mitigate legal risks and ensure the company's operations align with legal standards and best practices.

Collaborate with external legal counsel, as necessary, to handle complex legal matters and represent the company's interests in legal proceedings or negotiations.

Assist in the resolution of legal disputes and litigation, including managing external legal resources and representing the company in negotiations, mediations, and arbitrations.

Work closely with other departments, such as finance, human resources, and operations, to ensure legal compliance in all aspects of the business.

Conduct legal due diligence for potential business transactions, partnerships, and acquisitions to assess and mitigate legal risks.

Prepare and deliver training sessions and workshops to educate employees on legal matters, policies, and compliance requirements.

Keep accurate and up-to-date records of all legal documents, contracts, and correspondences.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in law (LLB)) from an accredited institution.

Minimum of 4 years of experience working as a legal officer or in a similar legal role, preferably in the agricultural or agribusiness sector.

In-depth knowledge of corporate law, contract law, and regulatory compliance.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to provide strategic legal advice and solutions.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex legal issues clearly and effectively.

Proven track record of managing legal contracts and negotiations effectively.

Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.

Strong attention to detail and the ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.

Familiarity with relevant software and tools for legal research and document management.

Key Competencies

Legal Risk Management: Ability to identify, assess, and proactively mitigate legal risks arising from the company’s operations, transactions, contracts, and business relationships.

Strategic Legal Advisory: Ability to translate complex legal requirements into practical, commercially sound recommendations that support management decision-making and the company’s strategic objectives.

Contract Negotiation and Management: Strong ability to develop and negotiate agreements while protecting the company’s interests, maintaining balanced commercial relationships, and ensuring effective contract implementation.

Corporate Governance: Sound understanding of good governance principles, board and management.

greatrwandajobs.title: Finance Assistant job at Raising The Village
greatrwandajobs.description:
About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.

To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

Position Purpose is to Support the Finance Team to ensure accurate bookkeeping, budget formulation, financial analysis, monitoring, reporting and accounting/budget execution across assigned field districts. Provide financial advisory support to field officers and help maintain strong financial controls and compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain and file all financial documents (cash advances, requests, receipts) to ensure records are audit-ready and readily available.

Update finance systems with timely and accurate financial data; participate in monthly Sage project reconciliations.

Support budgeting, budget tracking and implementation of financial policies; act as finance business partner to assigned field offices.

Reconcile staff advances, petty cash and project-specific accounts (monthly) and manage weekly staff advance activity.

Post journal entries (JE), manage fuel accountability and government official payment records.

Receive, log and verify invoices before entry; process invoices via the procurement module and follow up on vendor disputes.

Review and reconcile project activity accountability; investigate and resolve discrepancies.

Oversee individual accounts for assigned field officers and follow up on outstanding accountability.

Review mobile-money transactions for compliance; initiate payments via Beyonic, verifying beneficiaries, and flagging variances.

Report any non-compliant financial practices to the Senior Finance Officer or Senior Finance & Admin Manager.

Recommend improvements to increase accuracy, efficiency and cost savings; provide financial guidance to staff to ensure adherence to procedures.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in accounting, Accounting & Finance, Business Administration (Accounting) or equivalent.

Minimum 2 years’ professional experience in accounting, bookkeeping, finance management or audit.

Practical experience with mobile money payment solutions is essential.

Familiarity with accounting software (Sage or similar) is an advantage.

CPA/ACCA partial or full qualification is an advantage.

Technical & Personal Skills

Strong numerical, analytical, and Excel skills.

Knowledge of accounting standards, financial regulations, and data privacy principles.

High integrity, discretion, and ability to manage confidential information.

Good time management and attention to detail.

Critical thinking and business service orientation.

Willingness to travel up to 30% to field districts.

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace.

Position Purpose is to Support the Finance Team to ensure accurate bookkeeping, budget formulation, financial analysis, monitoring, reporting and accounting/budget execution across assigned field districts. Provide financial advisory support to field officers and help maintain strong financial controls and compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain and file all financial documents (cash advances, requests, receipts) to ensure records are audit-ready and readily available.

Update finance systems with timely and accurate financial data; participate in monthly Sage project reconciliations.

Support budgeting, budget tracking and implementation of financial policies; act as finance business partner to assigned field offices.

Reconcile staff advances, petty cash and project-specific accounts (monthly) and manage weekly staff advance activity.

Post journal entries (JE), manage fuel accountability and government official payment records.

Receive, log and verify invoices before entry; process invoices via the procurement module and follow up on vendor disputes.

Review and reconcile project activity accountability; investigate and resolve discrepancies.

Oversee individual accounts for assigned field officers and follow up on outstanding accountability.

Review mobile-money transactions for compliance; initiate payments via Beyonic, verifying beneficiaries, and flagging variances.

Report any non-compliant financial practices to the Senior Finance Officer or Senior Finance & Admin Manager.

Recommend improvements to increase accuracy, efficiency and cost savings; provide financial guidance to staff to ensure adherence to procedures.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in accounting, Accounting & Finance, Business Administration (Accounting) or equivalent.

Minimum 2 years’ professional experience in accounting, bookkeeping, finance management or audit.

Practical experience with mobile money payment solutions is essential.

Familiarity with accounting software (Sage or similar) is an advantage.

CPA/ACCA partial or full qualification is an advantage.

Technical & Personal Skills

Strong numerical, analytical, and Excel skills.

Knowledge of accounting standards, financial regulations, and data privacy principles.

High integrity, discretion, and ability to manage confidential information.

Good time management and attention to detail.

Critical thinking and business service orientation.

Willingness to travel up to 30% to field districts.

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace.

greatrwandajobs.company: Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. ( CHAI )
greatrwandajobs.description:
About Clinton Health Access Initiative- Rwanda (CHAI)

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries.

About This Opportunity

The position of Associate, Data Scientist at Clinton Health Access Initiative- Rwanda (CHAI) located in Kigali, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

CHAI RWANDA

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT

Title: Associate, Data Scientist

Program: Health Systems Strengthening

Job Location: Kigali, Rwanda

Type: Full-Time Paid

Start date: Immediate

Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to assist them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments guide the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Programs Overview

The Government of Rwanda (GoR) strives to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by enabling equitable access to quality health services for the population as outlined in the Fourth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP IV). This commitment has been made against a backdrop of rising health care costs and uncertainty around the future availability of donor funding and calls for improved health sector sustainability. Acknowledging this, the Government aims to employ effective, equitable, efficient, and sustainable health care financing and systems strengthening, putting an emphasis on primary health care as the cornerstone of a strong and sustainable health system.

CHAI Rwanda’s Health System Strengthening (HSS) programs work on a day-to-day basis with Government leadership in the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB). The goal of those programs is to assist the Government to accelerate progress towards UHC by ensuring the sustainable delivery of quality, essential health services. This includes designing and implementing national Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms from health center level down to community health, to increase health workforce availability, to prioritize and sustainably finance essential services, and to assist improved management, financing, and delivery of quality primary health care.

Position overview

CHAI currently seeks an Associate Data Scientist to collaborate with the Ministry of Health (MOH), reporting directly to the head of data science at the National Health Intelligence Center to help enhance the quality, governance, and use of evidence on policy decision making. S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI supported initiatives.

The Associate Data Scientist is tasked with leading advanced data analytics, statistical modeling, and applied machine learning across priority public health and clinical domains. The role ensures that health data is transformed into high-quality, reliable, explainable, and decision-ready intelligence that informs AI development, policy decisions, and health system performance improvement. This role serves as the technical bridge between raw health data, AI models, and real-world decision-making, ensuring scientific rigor, reproducibility, and national-scale usability.

This is a top government priority for MOH, and the Associate, Data Scientist will therefore be seconded to the MOH/NHIC, S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI-supported initiatives.

Job responsibilities:

The key functions and deliverables of this role will include:

Advanced Data Analytics and Statistical Modeling

guide advanced descriptive, predictive, and inferential analyses across clinical, surveillance, and health systems datasets.

create and validate predictive models, risk stratification algorithms, forecasting models, epidemiological and operational analytics

Apply rigorous statistical methods, hypothesis testing, and causal inference techniques to assist decision-making.

Ensure all analytics are clinically interpretable, policy-relevant, and scientifically defensible.

Feature Engineering & Machine Learning assist

Design robust feature engineering pipelines from EMRs, HMIS, LMIS and surveillance platforms

assist AI Engineers with high-quality training datasets, feature selection, bias detection and data representativeness testing

Contribute to development of machine learning models, particularly in tabular health data, time-series forecasting and population-level risk prediction.

Data Quality, Governance and Integrity

guide implementation of data quality frameworks, completeness, consistency, accuracy and timeliness checks

Perform data audits, outlier detection, bias and missing data analysis

Ensure compliance with national health data governance standards, privacy and ethical data use policies.

keep full data documentation, metadata standards, and lineage tracking.

Health Systems Intelligence & Decision assist

create decision-assist analytics and public health dashboards for disease burden tracking,

resource allocation and service delivery optimization.

Translate analytical outputs into policy briefs, executive dashboards, technical report.

Ensure outputs are actionable, explainable, and aligned with the national health priorities.

Data Engineering assist and Pipeline optimization

Work closely with Data engineers, integration teams and AI engineers to ensure analytics assets are scalable, reproducible and production ready.

assist data pipeline optimization, ETL quality validation and real-time and batch processing readiness

Mentorship, Capacity Building & Collaboration

Mentor junior data scientists and analysts

guide internal analytics communities of practice, code reviews and methodology workshops

Serve as a technical reviewer for analytics protocols, research designs and data science deliverables

Innovation and Continuous Improvement

Stay current with advances in Machine Learning, Statistical Science, Health Analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Causal Inference trends

Propose innovative analytics and data science use cases for public health, service delivery, health financing, supply chain and logistics for pharmaceuticals and disease surveillance

Required Qualifications

MSc degree in relevant discipline (Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Operations Research, Statistics, Epidemiology, Health Informatics)

5-8 years of professional experience in the field of advanced analytics and/or applied statistics preferably with Data Science applications

Solid mathematical foundation and knowledge of a variety of statistical methods (e.g. regression, classification, clustering, experimental design, modeling, advanced forecasting)

Proven experience working with large-scale datasets, regulated data environments, preferably within a health domain.

Strong proficiency in data visualization, demonstrated experience in Python, R, SQL, and working with structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets

Ability to focus on vaguely defined problems requiring the application of a creative approach.

Strong teamworking skills

Excellent written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across teams.

Ability to mentor and guide teams in a fast-paced and changing environment.

greatrwandajobs.title: Customer Service Agent job at AC Mobility
greatrwandajobs.description:
About AC Mobility

AC Mobility is a Rwandan-based technology firm specializing in smart transport solutions,, mainly known for its Tap&Go cashless fare system for buses. Operating since 2015, they enhance urban mobi...

Who May Be Interested

Professionals seeking career advancement and individuals with relevant qualifications may be interested in this opportunity.

This opportunity is ideal for professionals interested in the role of Customer Service Agent based in Kigali, Rwanda. Qualified and motivated candidates are encouraged to apply for this full-time opportunity.

About This Opportunity

The position of Customer Service Agent at AC Mobility located in Kigali, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Common Skills Required

Communication

Leadership

Management

Excel

Customer service

Problem solving

Sales

Administration

Job Description

This description has been adapted for JobNziza readers to provide a clearer overview of the opportunity.

Job Title: Customer Service Agent

Department: Communications

Location: AC Mobility Offices, Kigali - Rwanda

Modality: Full-Time

Contract Duration: One Year

Contract Type: Fixed Term

Reporting Structure:

Direct Supervisor/Reports To: Head of Communications

Works Closely With: Solutions assist Associate

Role Overview

As the Customer Service Agent, you are tasked with providing timely, professional, and empathetic frontline assistance to AC Mobility customers across all customer-care touchpoints. The role serves as a primary point of contact for commuter enquiries, complaints, and service requests, ensuring accurate information is provided, resolving standard issues at the first point of contact, and properly documenting and escalating complex cases requiring technical or operational investigation.

Core Responsibility

To deliver customers with a reliable, reassuring, and positive assist experience by understanding their needs, delivering accurate information, achieving high first-contact resolution on routine enquiries, and ensuring unresolved issues are documented and routed efficiently through established escalation pathways.

Key Responsibilities

Frontline Customer assist: Receive, manage, and resolve incoming customer enquiries and complaints professionally, courteously, and empathetically.

Customer Information Delivery: deliver clear, precise, and up-to-date guidance regarding AC Mobility products, Tap&Go fare structures, card usage, and service procedures.

First Contact Resolution (FCR): Resolve routine, frequently occurring customer enquiries (such as balance queries, basic card issues, and system guidance) during the initial interaction.

Complaint Handling and De-escalation: Actively listen to customer grievances, defuse tense interactions with composure, and deliver appropriate assistance while upholding professional standards.

Follow-up and Communication: Contact commuters to deliver progress updates, request additional information, or confirm the successful resolution of reported issues.

CRM and Case Management: Accurately record, categorise, and oversee all customer interactions, service requests, and feedback within the company’s CRM and ticketing systems.

Tier-2 Escalation: Accurately document and escalate technical faults, transactional discrepancies, or operational challenges to the Solutions assist Associate in line with standard operating procedures.

Customer Feedback Logging: Systematically detect and flag recurring commuter pain points, agent network issues, or validator failure patterns to supervisory and technical teams.

Data Security and Confidentiality: keep absolute discretion and protect sensitive commuter identity, card data, and transaction histories in strict adherence to data protection standards.

Continuous Learning and Compliance: keep a thorough understanding of AC Mobility platforms, updates, workflows, and assigned shift rotas.

Working Relationship with the Solutions assist Associate

The Customer Service Agent provides Tier-1 frontline assist, handling initial commuter engagements and resolving routine queries using documented procedures.

Where an issue requires technical diagnosis, backend transaction verification, or cross-departmental coordination, the Agent documents the case and formally escalates it to the Solutions assist Associate.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

First Contact Resolution (FCR): Achieve ≥80% resolution rate on standard enquiries during the first interaction.

Response and Resolution Timelines: Adhere strictly to agreed customer response and ticket resolution times across all live assist channels.

Customer Satisfaction (CSAT): keep a positive customer satisfaction rating of ≥85% based on post-interaction feedback.

CRM Record Accuracy: 100% of customer interactions accurately tagged, documented, and categorised with zero critical omissions.

Escalation Accuracy: Zero critical misroutings of technical or operational tickets escalated to the Solutions assist Associate.

Schedule Adherence: High punctuality and compliance with allocated shift rotas and operational breaks.

greatrwandajobs.title: Biobank Coordinator (Administrative & Research Operations) job at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)
greatrwandajobs.description:
About University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

University of Global Health Equity is a health sciences university in Rwanda. An initiative of Partners In Health, UGHE is a private, not-for-profit, accredited institution

About This Opportunity

The position of Biobank Coordinator (Administrative & Research Operations) at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE) located in Burera, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Description

Position Title: Biobank Coordinator (Administrative & Research Operations)

Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)

Reports To: Head of Biobank 

Location: Kigali with regular travel to research sites

Contract Duration: Two year contract with possible extension for another two years

Position Summary

The Biobank coordinator will deliver operational, administrative, and research coordination assist for biobank activities and clinical trial projects. The position will ensure effective planning, implementation, documentation, and monitoring of research activities while maintaining compliance with institutional policies, ethical requirements, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and biobank quality standards.

The Coordinator will serve as a key liaison between investigators, clinical trial teams, laboratory personnel, research participants, regulatory bodies, and collaborating institutions. The role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, experience in research administration, and the ability to organize multiple activities simultaneously.

Key Responsibilities

organize daily biobank operations, including specimen collection, processing, storage, tracking, inventory, access, documentation, and compliance.

assist clinical trial implementation, including timelines, regulatory documentation, site coordination, monitoring visits, recruitment tracking, essential documents, and logistics.

organize research activities, work plans, meetings, reports, budgets, procurement, travel, and project documentation.

Ensure adherence to GCP, ethics and regulatory requirements, biobank policies, data protection, and assist audits and accreditation activities.

Serve as a coordination point among investigators, clinical teams, laboratory/biobank staff, sponsors, regulators, and research partners, ensuring effective communication and follow-up.

Required Qualifications and competence

Bachelor’s degree in Health/Biomedical/Laboratory Sciences, Public Health, Clinical Research, Life Sciences, Health Administration, or related field; Master’s degree is an advantage.

Experience: 3–5 years’ experience in clinical research, clinical trials, biobanking, laboratory research, or research administration.

Experience with research documentation, databases, regulatory/ethics submissions, and multidisciplinary teams.

Knowledge of ICH-GCP, biobank operations, sample management, and research compliance.

Experience with REDCap, CTMS, LIMS, or similar research data systems is an advantage.

Strong organizational, coordination, communication, documentation, problem-solving, and time-management skills.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to oversee confidential research information.

GCP, research ethics, clinical research, biobank, or data management certification is an advantage.

Ability to organize multiple activities, keep accurate records, meet deadlines, and assist clinical trials, audits, reporting, and research logistics.

greatrwandajobs.description:
About University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

University of Global Health Equity is a health sciences university in Rwanda. An initiative of Partners In Health, UGHE is a private, not-for-profit, accredited institution

About This Opportunity

The position of Biobank Head at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE) located in Burera, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Position Title: Biobank Head

Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)

Duty Station: UGHE-AVEGA Biobank and UGHE, Kigali. Frequent travel to the Butaro campus, Northern Province, Burera District, Rwanda

Contract Duration: Two (2) years, renewable based on performance

Position Summary

The Biobank Head provides strategic, scientific, technical, and operational leadership for the establishment and management of the UGHE-AVEGA Biobank, a core research infrastructure of the Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER). The position is tasked with leading the planning, establishment, operationalization, accreditation, and continuous improvement of the biobank to assist clinical trials, translational research, precision medicine, genomics, oncology, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and population health research.

The Head is tasked with the overall administration and day-to-day management of biobank operations, including biospecimen acquisition, processing, storage, inventory management, retrieval, distribution, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) administration, quality management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, regulatory compliance, equipment management, financial oversight, and supervision of biobank personnel.

The Biobank Head will play a pivotal leadership role in developing institutional policies, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, regulatory systems, quality assurance programs, and strategic partnerships that ensure the biobank operates in accordance with ISBER Best Practices, ISO 20387, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable national and international regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

guide the establishment and operation of the UGHE–AVEGA Biobank and align activities with UGHE/IGHER priorities.

Establish SOPs, Quality Management Systems, governance, and regulatory compliance, including preparation for ISO 20387 accreditation and ISBER Best Practices.

guide implementation and management of the LIMS and ensure secure, accurate, and traceable data management.

Oversee biospecimen management, quality, traceability, security, staffing, equipment, budgets, and daily operations.

Integrate biobanking with clinical trials and research programs and create national and international collaborations.

Build staff capacity through training, mentorship, and competency development in biobanking, GCP/GCLP, biosafety, and quality management.

Qualifications

Education

PhD (preferred) or Master's in Biobanking, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pathology, Genomics, Public Health, Clinical Research, or related field. Certification in GCLP, GCP, ISO 20387, ISO 15189, ISBER Best Practices, or QMS/Laboratory Management is a plus.

Experience

8+ years in biobank management, biomedical research, clinical laboratory management, or clinical trial assist, including 5+ years in senior leadership supervising multidisciplinary teams

Proven track record establishing or expanding a biobank/biospecimen repository — infrastructure planning, workflow development, and operations

Experience implementing LIMS and laboratory/biobank Quality Management Systems

Hands-on management of biospecimen collection, processing, cryopreservation, storage, and distribution

Equipment lifecycle management (procurement through calibration/maintenance)

Experience managing donor-funded programs, budgets, and strategic/donor reporting

Developed SOPs, quality manuals, and governance structures (Oversight/Scientific Advisory/Data Access Committees)

Prepared labs for ISO 20387, ISO 15189, or ISBER accreditation; built CAPA and audit systems

Prepared IRB/ethics/regulatory documentation; ensured compliance with biospecimen collection, storage, and export regulations

Developed informed consent, data privacy, and biobank governance frameworks

Supported regulatory inspections and audits

greatrwandajobs.title: Biobank Technician I job at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)
greatrwandajobs.description:
About University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

University of Global Health Equity is a health sciences university in Rwanda. An initiative of Partners In Health, UGHE is a private, not-for-profit, accredited institution

About This Opportunity

The position of Biobank Technician I at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE) located in Burera, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Position Title: Biobank Technician I

Department/Unit: IGHER - Biobank Program

Reports To: Biobank Head

Location: Kigali with possible travel to research sites and sample collection locations

Position type: Two-year contract with possible extension

Position Summary

The Biobank Technician I – Sample Processing is tasked with supporting the collection, receipt, processing, aliquoting, labeling, storage preparation, and quality control of biological specimens collected from clinical trials, population-based research studies, and other biomedical research projects.The position ensures that all biological samples are handled, processed, and stored according to approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), biosafety requirements, and biobank quality standards.The Biobank Technician I works closely with Clinical Research Coordinators, Principal Investigators, laboratory personnel, data management teams, and research partners to ensure specimen integrity, traceability, and compliance throughout the research lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Receive, process, label, aliquot, store, retrieve, and produce biological specimens for shipment according to approved SOPs.

Keep accurate sample identification, tracking, chain-of-custody, and inventory records.

Perform routine quality checks, document deviations, and assist CAPA, audits, and continuous quality improvement.

Operate and keep laboratory equipment, including centrifuges, biosafety cabinets, refrigerators, freezers, and pipettes.

Keep biosafety, GCLP/GCP, confidentiality, and laboratory safety standards.

Track laboratory supplies and report equipment or operational issues.

Collaborate with clinical, laboratory, data management, and research teams to assist clinical trials and research projects.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical/Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biotechnology, Biology, Biochemistry, Biomedical Sciences, or a related field.

Experience

Minimum 2 years of laboratory experience, preferably involving human biological specimens in research, clinical trials, hospitals, or diagnostic laboratories.

Skills: Knowledge of sample processing, biosafety, laboratory quality standards, documentation, and basic laboratory information systems; good computer skills.

Preferred Training: GCLP, GCP, biosafety, and research ethics certification/training.

greatrwandajobs.description:
About University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

About This Opportunity

The position of Biobank Technician II – Data Management and Cold Chain at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE) located in Burera, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Position Title: Biobank Technician II – Data Management and Cold Chain

Department/Unit: IGHER-Biobank

Reports To: Biobank Program

Location: Kigali with possible travel to research sites

Position type: Two-year contract with possible extension

Position Summary

The Biobank Technician II – Data Management and Cold Chain is tasked with maintaining accurate biobank information systems, managing specimen inventory records, monitoring storage conditions, and ensuring uninterrupted cold chain operations.The position ensures sample traceability, data integrity, specimen security, and compliance throughout the biobank lifecycle. The Technician also provides essential operational assist to clinical trial activities by maintaining trial sample accountability records, supporting monitoring visits, and ensuring accurate documentation of research specimens.

Key Responsibilities

keep accurate biobank and clinical trial sample databases, including inventory, location, processing, storage, transfers, and access history.

Reconcile physical specimens with electronic records and resolve discrepancies.

Track sample receipt, storage, retrieval, shipment, and chain of custody.

track cold-chain conditions, including −80°C freezers and liquid nitrogen systems, and respond to temperature excursions.

Generate sample inventory and accountability reports and assist audits, monitoring visits, and regulatory inspections.

keep compliance with SOPs, protocols, ethics, data protection, and quality requirements, including CAPA.

keep equipment, storage, and maintenance records and assist contingency planning.

Collaborate with laboratory, clinical, data, and research teams and assist clinical trial start-up, monitoring, and close-out activities.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Health Informatics, Biomedical/Laboratory Sciences, Data Management, Biotechnology, IT, Life Sciences, or related field.

Experience:

2–3 years’ experience in biobank operations, laboratory data management, clinical research, or health information systems.

Experience with databases, sample tracking, and electronic records.

Data management, quality assurance, Excel/database systems, cold-chain monitoring, and research documentation.

Preferred Training: GCP, GCLP, biobank, data management, or biosafety training.

Strong attention to detail, organization, accountability, problem-solving, teamwork, and commitment to data quality.

Accurate and timely inventory, complete sample traceability, reliable cold-chain monitoring, and accurate clinical trial specimen accountability.

greatrwandajobs.title: Pediatric Surgery Faculty job at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)
greatrwandajobs.description:
University of Global Health Equity is a health sciences university in Rwanda. An initiative of Partners In Health, UGHE is a private, not-for-profit, accredited institution

The position of Pediatric Surgery Faculty at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE) located in Burera, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Position: Pediatric Surgery Faculty

Job Title: Faculty, Pediatric Surgery

Reports to: Head, Department of Surgery

Group/Department: Department of Surgery / Division of Clinical Medicine, University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

Location: Primarily Butaro Campus and Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital, with frequent travel to Kigali and other teaching sites in Rwanda

Position Overview

The Faculty of Pediatric Surgery will play a key role in advancing UGHE’s mission to deliver equitable, high-quality medical education and surgical care for children. The faculty member will contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, clinical pediatric surgical service delivery, research, and global surgery initiatives focused on children’s surgical care.

The Pediatric Surgery faculty member will actively participate in clinical teaching at Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital and affiliated training sites, contribute to curriculum development in pediatric surgery, mentor students and trainees, and assist the implementation of the General Surgery Residency Program aligned with COSECSA standards, including strengthening pediatric surgical training exposure.

The ideal candidate is highly self-motivated, academically productive, and committed to surgical education, research, and strengthening pediatric surgical capacity in resource-limited settings. The individual must be organized, collaborative, adaptable, and passionate about improving access to safe, timely, and affordable surgical care for children.

Responsibilities

Undergraduate Medical Education

Contribute to curriculum, syllabus, and content development in pediatric surgery across the MBBS/MGHD curriculum.

Deliver lectures, small group sessions, simulation-based teaching, and bedside clinical instruction.

Deliver clinical supervision to medical students during surgery clerkships, with emphasis on pediatric surgical conditions.

Participate in student assessment (OSCEs, written exams, workplace-based assessments).

Supervise and mentor undergraduate research projects.

Organize pediatric surgery teaching activities with visiting and adjunct faculty.

Collaborate with affiliated hospitals to ensure effective delivery of pediatric surgical education.

Ensure quality and consistency of clinical teaching across all rotation sites.

Deliver leadership for pediatric surgery modules or thematic blocks as assigned.

Participate in direct patient care as part of clinical teaching responsibilities.

Postgraduate and Residency Education

Contribute to implementation of competency-based training aligned with COSECSA standards.

Ensure quality supervision of residents rotating through pediatric surgery.

Deliver structured clinical supervision in neonatal and pediatric surgical care.

Participate in WBAs, logbook reviews, case discussions, and operative competency assessments.

Contribute to exam preparation for COSECSA membership and fellowship examinations.

Mentor residents in clinical practice, research, leadership, and professionalism.

Participate in M&M conferences, journal clubs, and academic rounds.

Assist development of simulation-based training for pediatric surgical procedures.

Contribute to accreditation and quality assurance processes.

Assist development of pediatric surgery training pathways within UGHE programs.

Clinical Service Delivery

Assist and scale-up of comprehensive pediatric surgical services at Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital, including:

Pediatric general surgery and emergency care

Pediatric Oncologic Surgery

Strengthen systems for perioperative care of children, including anesthesia, critical care, and nutrition.

Create and execute clinical protocols, safety standards, and quality improvement initiatives.

Assist multidisciplinary care involving pediatrics, anesthesia, nursing, and allied health professionals.

Strengthen referral systems and district-level capacity for pediatric surgical care.

Participate in on-call coverage and emergency pediatric surgical services.

Research and Scholarship

Initiate and assist research in pediatric surgery, neonatal surgery, and global children’s surgery.

Create grant proposals, research publications, and technical reports.

Mentor students and residents in research activities.

Perform implementation and operational research focused on improving access to pediatric surgical care in Rwanda and similar settings.

Center for Equity in Global Surgery (CEGS) Activities

Participate in CEGS academic and administrative activities.

Contribute to global surgery conferences, seminars, and collaborations.

Build partnerships with national and international pediatric surgery programs.

Assist grant writing and resource mobilization.

Advocate for equitable access to surgical care for children.

Institutional Service and Leadership

Serve on UGHE committees as assigned.

Contribute to departmental strategy and academic program development.

Engage in community outreach and child health advocacy initiatives.

Promote interprofessional education and collaboration.

Perform other duties as assigned by UGHE leadership.

Qualifications and Skills

Mandatory

Medical degree (MD, MBBS, or equivalent) from a recognized institution.

Postgraduate qualification in Pediatric Surgery (Fellowship, MMed, or equivalent recognized specialist qualification).

Board certification or equivalent specialist recognition in Pediatric Surgery.

Eligible for medical licensure/registration in Rwanda.

Demonstrated clinical expertise in pediatric surgical care, including neonatal surgery.

Experience in teaching undergraduate and postgraduate trainees.

Demonstrated research experience.

Commitment to academic medicine and mentorship.

Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills in multidisciplinary settings.

Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

Preferred

MSc in Public Health, Global Health, or Medical Education.

Experience in health systems strengthening and surgical capacity building in low-resource settings.

Experience working in academic medical centers.

Expertise in research methods and implementation science.

Experience in competency-based medical education.

Grant writing experience and peer-reviewed publications.

Familiarity with COSECSA or similar regional training frameworks.

greatrwandajobs.title: Itangazo Ryo Kwiga Umwuga Wo Kudoda Mu Gihe Cy’amezi Atandatu (6) job at UFACO Garments Ltd
greatrwandajobs.description_html:
About This Opportunity

The position of Itangazo Ryo Kwiga Umwuga Wo Kudoda Mu Gihe Cy’amezi Atandatu (6) at UFACO Garments Ltd located in Kigali, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Common Skills Required

Training

Job Description

This description has been adapted for JobNziza readers to provide a clearer overview of the opportunity.

ITANGAZO RYO KWIGA UMWUGA WO KUDODA MU GIHE CY’AMEZI ATANDATU (6)

Ubuyobozi bwa UFACO Garments Ltd buramenyesha ababyeyi, urubyiruko ndetse n’abandi bose bifuza kwiga umwuga wo kudoda, ko bwafunguye gahunda y’amahugurwa y’igihe gito mu mwuga wo kudoda no gukora imyenda (Garment Making / Tailoring).

Amahugurwa azamara igihe kingana n’amezi atandatu (6 months), kandi abazayitabira baziga biyishyurira. Muri aya mahugurwa, abanyeshuri bazahabwa ubumenyi n’ubushobozi mu bikorwa birimo:

  • Gukoresha imashini zitandukanye zidoda;
  • Kumenya ibikoresho n’imyenda ikoreshwa mu kudoda;
  • Gupima no gufata ibipimo by’imyenda;
  • Gukata imyenda hakurikijwe ibipimo;
  • Kudoda no guteranya ibice by’imyenda;
  • Gukora amashati, amapantalo, amakanzu n’indi myambaro;
  • Gukora finishing no kugenzura ubuziranenge bw’imyenda;

Amahugurwa ngiro (practical training) azakorerwa muri UFACO Garments Ltd kugira ngo abanyeshuri babone ubumenyi bushingiye ku kazi gakorerwa mu ruganda.

IBISABWA KU BASHAKA KWIYANDIKISHA

  • Kuba bafite ubushake bwo kwiga umwuga wo kudoda;
  • Kuzana fotokopi y’Indangamuntu cyangwa ikindi cyangombwa kibanga;
  • Kuzana fotokopi y’impamyabumenyi ku bayifite;
  • Kuzuza ifishi yo kwiyandikisha;
  • Kwemera gukurikiza gahunda n’abwiriza agenga amahugurwa;
  • Kwishyura amafaranga y’amahugurwa nk’uko azagenwa na UFACO Garments Ltd.

IGIHE AMAHUGURWA AZAMARA

NB1: Amasomo azamara amezi atandatu (6) kandi azibanda cyane ku myitozo ngiro, kugira ngo uyasoje abe ashoboye gukoresha neza imashini zidoda no gukora imyenda ku rwego rw’umwuga, ku buryo ashobora kwihangira umurimo cyangwa gukorera mu nganda zikora imyenda. Abazaba barangije neza aya mahugurwa bazahabwa icyemezo (Certificate) cyemewe kandi kiriho umukono wa RTB (Rwanda TVET Board), ikigo cya Leta gifite inshingano zo guteza imbere no kugenzura imyigishirize y’imyuga n’ubumenyingiro mu Rwanda.

NB2: Itariki yo gutangira amasomo, ndetse n’andi makuru yose ajyanye n’amahugurwa bizamenyeshwa gusa abamaze kwiyandikisha. Amasomo azajya atangira mu gitondo kugeza saa munani z’amanywa (14:00). Abifuza kwiyandikisha basabwe kohereza ibyangombwa bisabwa nk’uko byavuzwe haruguru kuri izi aderesi za email: info@ufaco.top copy to agathe.nyirashimiyimana@ufaco.top. Kwiyandikisha bizarangira ku wa 30/09/2026.

greatrwandajobs.title: Project Manager job at Raising The Village
greatrwandajobs.description:
About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

The Project Manager plays a critical role in overseeing the successful implementation of multiple projects within a district, ensuring alignment with RTV’s strategic goals, project designs, and work plans. This role involves providing strong leadership, mentorship, and operational support to Team Leads and Officers, ensuring they have the necessary resources, guidance, and capacity to execute projects effectively.

In addition to people and team management, the Project Manager is responsible for office administration and operations, fostering an environment where teams are fully supported to meet program objectives. They serve as the key liaison between staff, government counterparts and management, proactively addressing challenges, streamlining processes, and ensuring smooth communication and workflow across all levels.

The ideal candidate is a results-oriented leader with strong experience in coaching and managing teams, mobilizing and coordinating with government institutions, and delivering complex, multi-sector projects in rural contexts. They are solutions-driven, highly organized, and committed to building high-performing teams that deliver sustainable, government-aligned impact for communities served by RTV. Note: The Project Manager may be based at a District Government Office and embedded with government teams to foster collaboration and strengthen partnerships.
