greatrwandajobs.title: Project Assistant job at Raising The Village
greatrwandajobs.description_html:
About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.

To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable assist of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

Role and Responsibilities

Project Implementation

  • perform project design evaluate meetings with respective partner villages and deliver feedback as required to update project designs and budgets prior to implementation;
  • organize training activities including but not limited to financial literacy and behavior and mindset change, water and health sanitation, village savings and loans associations, agriculture, livestock care and management, etc.
  • Responsible to execute RTV’s project methodologies with the purpose of increasing household income and reducing extreme poverty as per project designs;
  • create and submit list of required goods and services for project implementation to the procurement and logistics officer;
  • Responsible to verify goods/inputs prior to distribution;
  • perform project follow-up and deliver assist and guidance to community groups and individual households to ensure project compliance continuation.
  • detect potential risks and issues and deliver mitigation measures and recommendations for improvements;
  • perform regular meetings with leadership and community members on performance, participation, and perceptions of RTV based projects.

Government & Community Coordination and assist

  • Build and keep strong working relationships with Cell-level government officials (SEDOs and Executive Secretaries) to assist day-to-day RTV program activities.
  • Work closely with community leadership and assist structures including Inteko z’abaturage, Incuti z’umuryango, Abajyanama b’Ubuzima, Abajyanama b’Ubuhinzi (farmer promoters), para-social workers, community coaches, technical and village coaches, and other community actors to ensure their active participation in RTV programs.
  • Mobilize households and communities for trainings, meetings, and program activities to promote clear understanding, strong participation, and adoption of RTV program components.
  • help with delivering trainings to community and cell-level actors on RTV program methodology, M&E processes, technology use, and field protocols, under the guidance of the Project Officer or Project Manager.
  • deliver on-the-job assist and follow-up to community and government actors during implementation to help address challenges and encourage consistent participation.
  • Promote positive collaboration and trust between RTV staff, government officials, and community structures to strengthen community ownership and contribute to sustainable program impact.

Reporting and Administration

  • create and oversee work plans;
  • Complete field reporting on a weekly basis and deliver assist with information sharing for donor reporting and proposal writing as might be required;
  • Attend and participate in weekly staff meetings as well as cluster team meetings to highlight issues and success and outline next steps;
  • Complete weekly financial request, submissions and accountabilities to the Project Officer;
  • Take photographs and share them for data repository.

Monitoring and Evaluation:

  • assist field monitoring activities such as attendance tracking, basic data collection, household follow-ups, and reporting using RTV tools and systems.
  • Providing feedback and recommendations to the Project Officer and Project Manager, and the program team to enhance RTV’s way of work;
  • deliver suggestions to management on potential activities that need to be redone, reviewed or introduced to ensure sustainability of RTV projects, methodologies, and improvement in the lives of community members.

Note: Other requirements might be required by their direct supervisor and/or management.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, Social Work, Humanities, Community Development, or related field of study
  • Bachelor’s degree in agriculture is preferred but not required
  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant work experience at the village level
  • Demonstrated experience working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at Sector and Cell levels (mandatory)

Preferred Skills if any

  • Strong training & facilitation skills;
  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English;
  • Fluent in local languages where RTV works;
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs i.e. Word and Excel
  • Understanding of Community Based Development Principles
  • Organizes work effectively while remaining aware of changing priorities and deadlines;
  • Able to work independently to accomplish tasks, but also as part of a team to achieve mutual goals and objectives;
  • Able to think outside of the box to deliver plausible solutions to issues and challenges;
  • Strong work ethic, flexible, and able to build relationships with various stakeholders most notably colleagues, and community members;
  • Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment;
  • Energetic and physically able to hike high to hike high terrain;
  • Able to travel approximately 90% of time;
  • Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit (class A) and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory).

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace.

greatrwandajobs.title: Rwanda Construction Quality Assurance and Quality Check Engineer (Fixed-term) job at One Acre Fund
greatrwandajobs.description:
About the Role

Seeking a Civil/Structural Engineer (3–5+ years) to oversee RICA Seed Centre construction, ensure quality, and resolve site issues by producing and providing designs/drawings and other relevant technical specifications.

Responsibilities

Construction Quality Compliance

Review construction plans, specifications, drawings, and technical documentation to ensure compliance with approved quality standards, codes, and regulations.

Inspect construction materials upon delivery and verify quality, specifications, quantities, and conformity with approved submittals.

Conduct quality compliance checks throughout construction and maintain accurate records of inspections, findings, non-conformities, and corrective actions.

Review and/or prepare civil and structural engineering reports, drawings, and structural detailing to support quality assurance and project delivery.

Construction Process Oversight & Coordination

Conduct regular site inspections to monitor construction activities and verify compliance with approved drawings, specifications, method statements, and quality requirements.

Work closely with consultants, contractors, subcontractors, and construction teams to identify deviations and agree on appropriate corrective actions.

Monitor construction processes continuously to identify quality risks early and ensure issues are resolved before they affect project delivery.

Coordinate quality assurance activities with project teams to ensure inspections and corrective actions remain aligned with construction schedules and milestones.

Quality Control & Continuous Improvement

Develop and implement quality control procedures and testing requirements across key construction phases, including concrete, structural, material, and installation works.

Provide practical training and guidance to construction teams on quality standards, inspection procedures, testing requirements, and quality control practices.

Investigate recurring quality issues, identify root causes, and recommend preventive measures to improve construction quality and reduce rework.

Track quality performance and use inspection and testing findings to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Quality Documentation, Reporting & Administration

Establish and maintain an organised quality database covering inspection reports, test results, material approvals, non-conformities, and corrective actions.

Maintain complete and accessible project documentation, including specifications, quality control plans, inspection schedules, and compliance records.

Prepare concise quality reports that summarise inspection findings, outstanding issues, risks, corrective actions, and overall project quality performance.

Coordinate inspection and testing schedules with construction teams to minimise disruption while ensuring quality activities are completed on time.

Stakeholder Coordination & Technical Support

Facilitate clear communication between construction teams, consultants, contractors, and subcontractors on quality requirements, inspections, and corrective actions.

Provide technical recommendations on construction quality issues and support teams in resolving deviations from approved designs and specifications.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Structural Engineering or a closely related engineering field. Registration with the Institution of Engineers of Rwanda is an added advantage.

3 to 5 years of experience in construction quality assurance, quality control, site supervision, or civil/structural engineering, with demonstrated exposure to construction projects.

Strong understanding of construction principles, quality assurance and quality control procedures, building codes, specifications, and regulatory requirements.

Hands-on experience conducting site inspections, reviewing construction documentation, assessing materials, identifying non-conformities, and recommending corrective actions.

Ability to review and produce engineering drawings, technical reports, structural details, and construction documentation, with proficiency in AutoCAD or other relevant CAD tools.

Ability to work effectively with consultants, contractors, subcontractors, construction teams, and other project stakeholders.

Proficiency in English and Kinyarwanda is required.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Bugesera, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

Contract Duration

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

greatrwandajobs.title: Senior Agronomist - Conservation Agriculture (Fixed-term) job at One Acre Fund
greatrwandajobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.

Responsibilities

Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.

Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.

Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.

Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning.

Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption

Provide hands-on technical guidance to field teams delivering farmer trainings, workshops, Farmer Field Schools, and demonstration plots.

Build the capacity of field staff and local extension agents to effectively promote and support conservation agriculture adoption.

Provide timely agronomic troubleshooting to farmers and field teams addressing crop, soil, pest, and climate-related challenges.

Work with MEL and field teams to develop and implement systems that track adoption, farmer outcomes, and opportunities for scaling.

Agronomic Research, Practice Optimization & Impact

Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability.

Collaborate with R&D teams to design and oversee field assessments of soil health, crop performance, and environmental outcomes.

Analyze field evidence and farmer feedback to identify high-impact practices and recommend improvements to conservation agriculture programming.

Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models.

Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership

Build and manage strategic relationships with public, private, NGO, academic, and other technical partners supporting conservation agriculture initiatives.

Coordinate project plans, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and data sharing across internal teams and external consortium partners.

Represent the conservation agriculture program in technical discussions and ensure strong alignment between farmer needs, organizational priorities, and partner objectives.

Identify opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and resource mobilization that strengthen program quality, scale, and long-term impact.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Master’s degree in Agronomy, Agroecology, Crop Science, Soil Science, or a closely related agricultural field.

Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, conservation agriculture, regenerative agriculture, or agroecological farming systems.

Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs.

Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder projects involving government, NGOs, research institutions, academia, or private-sector partners.

Strong hands-on experience working directly with smallholder farmers and field teams, with willingness to travel extensively and spend significant time in rural settings.

Proficiency in English is required; additional regional or international languages are an advantage.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Contract Duration

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

Eligibility

This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, or Burundi are strongly preferred.

greatrwandajobs.title: Rwanda Contracts Procurement Coordinator job at One Acre Fund
greatrwandajobs.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund supplies over 1.5 million smallholder farmers with the agricultural services they need to make their farms more productive. Our 8,000+ team is drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. With operations across ten African countries, we make farmers more prosperous by providing easy access to quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, and agricultural training to enhance harvests. On average, the farmers we serve earn 40 percent more profits from their land when they enroll with One Acre Fund. To learn more about our work, look at our Why Work Here blog for more information.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007, is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to assist national efforts to enhance food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

About the Role

Seeking an exceptional procurement and contracts professional with 2+ years of experience to increase our impact on farmers by driving cost savings and coordinating contracting activities for the procurement department.

Responsibilities

Tender Management

guide end-to-end tendering and contract execution for high-value goods and services by collaborating on departmental procurement plans.

Establish 0-6 month strategic targets and set price baselines to negotiate maximum cost savings.

Continually optimise sourcing processes for higher operational efficiency.

Contract Planning & Management

Analyse annual spend across key categories to establish a quarterly-reviewed tender calendar.

perform market research to boost competition and contract effectiveness.

Oversee full contract lifecycles and Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) by tracking price tolerances and managing change control systems.

Analyse market risks and report overall cost savings.

Supplier & Stakeholder Management

perform bi-annual vendor evaluations and monthly meetings with top suppliers to create performance improvement plans and enforce contractual commitments.

Act as the key liaison between external suppliers and One Acre Fund while directly supporting internal team procurement needs.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

2–3 years of relevant experience in contract management, procurement sourcing, and end-to-end tendering operations.

Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Law, Business Administration, or a related field.

Proven ability to oversee supplier performance, negotiate agreements to maximise cost savings, and enforce contractual commitments.

Proactive problem solver skilled in data analysis, spend tracking, and sourcing process optimisation.

Strong relationship management skills with both internal stakeholders and external suppliers.

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

Contract Duration

Permanent

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

greatrwandajobs.title: Impact Division Chief of Staff job at One Acre Fund
greatrwandajobs.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we deliver high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

About the Role

The organization is seeking an exceptional strategist and communicator to enhance coordination between all of the Impact Division's workstreams. You will assist the CIO in advancing One Acre Fund's Global Impact Strategy.

Responsibilities

The Impact Division supports all One Acre Fund programs to generate more impact, wherever we work. We help the organization keep three core aspects of impact at the forefront of our work:

Improving farmer livelihoods in the short-term

Ensuring long-term viability through sustainable agricultural practices (soil health, crop diversity, etc.)

Addressing non-agricultural needs of farming households (energy, nutrition, etc.)

The role of the Impact Chief of Staff is to assist the Chief Impact Officer (CIO) in advancing our organization’s Impact Strategy. Three critical components of this role are to:

enhance coordination of many different actors to execute our Impact Strategy.

Increase the reach and effectiveness of Impact Division leadership.

guide strategic research, communications, or operational initiatives.

Specific responsibilities include:

Improving Impact Division communication & coordination around achieving goals

Goal setting and tracking. guide the annual development of OKRs aligned to organizational impact strategy; track progress against the strategic plan, OKRs, and other organizational indicators.

Coordination across the Impact Division. Ensure fluid collaboration between technical assist teams and operational teams through clear work planning and frequent, transparent communication.

Increasing the reach of Impact leadership

perform regular prioritization reviews with division leadership to ensure we’re tackling the most important problems.

Serve as the Chief Impact Officer’s “whip” by moving complex projects forward.

Represent the Division externally by pursuing early stage opportunities with partners.

Take on direct or indirect management responsibilities from division leadership, as appropriate.

Leading strategic Initiatives

guide strategic research or operational initiatives that:

Are highly important to One Acre Fund and organizational leadership

Sit outside the day-to-day purview of the current team

Specific projects will depend on the candidate's background and interests, organizational priorities, bandwidth of implicated teams, and timing. Examples could include:

Impact-focused internal campaigns

Researching a new technology or partnership

Team-building and culture initiatives

Improving impact communications & Q&A forums

Temporarily filling critical leadership gaps and recruitment of high priority roles.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Passion, Motivation, & Humility

Genuine passion for continually and sustainably improving farmer livelihoods.

Motivated by helping others. This role isn’t about individual achievements but about supporting teams across One Acre Fund to achieve our common mission.

Strong Technical Aptitude

University (or higher) degree in Agriculture or a related field (e.g. Ecology, Environmental Science, Ag Economics).

Genuine enthusiasm for learning and an openness to feedback.

Demonstrated analytical skills and ability to quickly turn around or sense-check quantitative analyses.

Excellent Communication Skills

Strong verbal and written communication across a wide range of audiences - from non-technically-trained colleagues to external experts.

Open listener; can create trust of colleagues and teams.

English fluency required. Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Kirundi, or French are a plus.

Leadership & Collaboration

Ability to understand the motivations and capacities of diverse teams, bring them together to collaborate effectively, and leverage their relative strengths.

Demonstrated leadership experience, whether at work or outside of formal employment.

High-Level Productivity

Strong organizational skills and an ability to 'keep the trains running on time’.

Systematic thinker, able to track dozens of diverse tasks and initiatives.

Demonstrated ability to deliver results quickly, whether working independently or implementing direction and advice.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda or flexible based on existing work authorization

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can assist a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

Improving farmer livelihoods in the short-term

Ensuring long-term viability through sustainable agricultural practices (soil health, crop diversity, etc.)

Addressing non-agricultural needs of farming households (energy, nutrition, etc.)

The role of the Impact Chief of Staff is to assist the Chief Impact Officer (CIO) in advancing our organization’s Impact Strategy. Three critical components of this role are to:

enhance coordination of many different actors to execute our Impact Strategy.

Increase the reach and effectiveness of Impact Division leadership.

guide strategic research, communications, or operational initiatives.

Specific responsibilities include:

Improving Impact Division communication & coordination around achieving goals

Goal setting and tracking. guide the annual development of OKRs aligned to organizational impact strategy; track progress against the strategic plan, OKRs, and other organizational indicators.

Coordination across the Impact Division. Ensure fluid collaboration between technical assist teams and operational teams through clear work planning and frequent, transparent communication.

Increasing the reach of Impact leadership

perform regular prioritization reviews with division leadership to ensure we’re tackling the most important problems.

Serve as the Chief Impact Officer’s “whip” by moving complex projects forward.

Represent the Division externally by pursuing early stage opportunities with partners.

Take on direct or indirect management responsibilities from division leadership, as appropriate.

Leading strategic Initiatives

guide strategic research or operational initiatives that:

Are highly important to One Acre Fund and organizational leadership

Sit outside the day-to-day purview of the current team

Specific projects will depend on the candidate's background and interests, organizational priorities, bandwidth of implicated teams, and timing. Examples could include:

Impact-focused internal campaigns

Researching a new technology or partnership

Team-building and culture initiatives

Improving impact communications & Q&A forums

Temporarily filling critical leadership gaps and recruitment of high priority roles.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Passion, Motivation, & Humility

Genuine passion for continually and sustainably improving farmer livelihoods.

Motivated by helping others. This role isn’t about individual achievements but about supporting teams across One Acre Fund to achieve our common mission.

Strong Technical Aptitude

University (or higher) degree in Agriculture or a related field (e.g. Ecology, Environmental Science, Ag Economics).

Genuine enthusiasm for learning and an openness to feedback.

Demonstrated analytical skills and ability to quickly turn around or sense-check quantitative analyses.

Excellent Communication Skills

Strong verbal and written communication across a wide range of audiences - from non-technically-trained colleagues to external experts.

Open listener; can create trust of colleagues and teams.

English fluency required. Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Kirundi, or French are a plus.

Leadership & Collaboration

Ability to understand the motivations and capacities of diverse teams, bring them together to collaborate effectively, and leverage their relative strengths.

Demonstrated leadership experience, whether at work or outside of formal employment.

High-Level Productivity

Strong organizational skills and an ability to 'keep the trains running on time’.

Systematic thinker, able to track dozens of diverse tasks and initiatives.

Demonstrated ability to deliver results quickly, whether working independently or implementing direction and advice.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda or flexible based on existing work authorization

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can assist a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

greatrwandajobs.title: Analyst, Office of the CFO (Fixed-term) job at One Acre Fund
greatrwandajobs.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we deliver high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

About the Role

Seeking an exceptional finance professional with experience to strengthen the CFO's office, driving strategic initiatives and turning complex data into decisions that shape Finance operations organisation-wide.

Responsibilities

Division Communications & Executive assist

Guide the drafting and delivery of Finance Division communications, including decision announcements, priority rollouts, and key organisational cycles.

Keep the Division's communications calendar and organize inputs, timelines, follow-ups, and actions with department leads.

Produce high-quality presentation decks, briefing notes, data summaries, and other materials for senior leadership.

Translate complex data, analytical findings, and team inputs into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable messages.

Division Operations & Governance

Organize the Finance Division's governance calendar, including leadership meetings, quarterly forums, annual events, and other key planning cycles.

Assist agenda development, meeting logistics, preparation of materials, and follow-up on key decisions and actions.

Track progress against divisional priorities and OKRs, identifying risks, dependencies, and areas requiring leadership attention.

Keep clear trackers and work plans to assist effective coordination and execution across the Division.

Strategic Projects & Problem Solving

Own clearly defined projects and workstreams from planning through execution and delivery.

Organize selected CFO- and Senior Manager-sponsored initiatives by aligning stakeholders, tracking milestones, and proactively addressing blockers.

Guide or contribute to high-priority cross-functional and ad hoc projects across the Finance Division.

Apply structured problem-solving to ambiguous challenges and create practical options and recommendations for leadership.

Analysis, Strategic Insight & Flexible Resourcing

Perform research, benchmarking, data synthesis, and financial analysis to assist strategic decision-making.

Create structured outputs, including summaries, frameworks, financial models, and scenario analyses.

Deliver flexible assist across the Finance Division during periods of peak demand, staff transitions, or extended leave.

Take ownership of assigned responsibilities during temporary assignments, ensuring clear communication, continuity, and effective handover.

Assist divisional recruitment and other priority initiatives as needed.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.

CPA or ACCA finalist.

About 5 years of working experience in finance, strategy, consulting, project management, or operations, within fast-paced medium- to large organisations.

Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Proactive, detail-oriented, and solutions-focused approach.

Familiarity with financial analysis, management reporting, and business decision-making is preferred.

Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting to changing priorities.

Full professional proficiency in English, with strong written communication skills.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits.

Contract Duration

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.
